A large county with several markets

Miami-Dade covers 1,899.90 square miles and had an estimated 2,802,029 residents in mid-2025. It holds 1,125,274 housing units, and 52.2 percent are owner-occupied. The typical owned home is valued at $463,000. With roughly half the housing rented, caps and exemptions matter a lot to owners here, and so does the line between an owner-occupied home and a rental.

Who to call first

Three county offices split the work, so match the question to the desk.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, portability and classifications. The main office is in the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710 (305-375-4712). The Cutler Bay branch is at 10710 SW 211 Street, 2nd Floor (305-232-3810). Each is staffed on weekdays during business hours.
  • Tax Collector: prints and collects the bill, with 13 service locations, 24 hour online payment and mobile offices that visit neighborhoods.
  • Clerk of the Courts: records deeds, takes value petitions and runs tax deed auctions.

The appraiser does not send tax bills or set and collect taxes. A complaint about the size of a bill belongs with the taxing bodies that levy millage.

The 2026 roll

The appraiser's June 1 estimate put countywide taxable value at $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent from 2025 and 3.2 percentage points slower than the prior year's gain. A July 1 preliminary certification went to the taxing authorities. The County Commission ordered the roll extended on September 1, 2026, and the appraiser certified it on October 16, 2026. That first certification comes before any changes the Value Adjustment Board makes after appeals.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why neighbors pay different rates

The total comes from stacked taxing bodies, and the city layer varies widely. The 2026 millage chart runs from 14.9007 on one North Miami Beach line to 24.1893 in Biscayne Park, with unincorporated areas at 16.8983. Other totals include Miami at 19.9544, Miami Beach at 18.6681, Hialeah at 18.6134, Coral Gables at 18.1518 and Doral at 16.9487.

The chart lists more than three dozen taxing areas. Looking only at a city's own operating line, Doral is lowest at 1.5994 mills, Hialeah sits mid-range at 6.3018, and Biscayne Park is highest at 9.2000. A low city line can still sit on a heavy total once school, county, fire and library lines are added, and some rows add debt service or special district lines. Match your own address to a row instead of quoting a city figure.

Separate tax guides cover Miami and Miami Beach.

Due dates and early-payment discounts

Bills land in November. Payment in November earns the full 4 percent discount, and the discount drops a point each month through February. Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The Tax Collector promotes the November discount as "Save the Max" and takes payment online, at its 13 locations or at its mobile offices.

Miami-Dade payment discount by month
Payment monthDiscount
November4 percent
December3 percent
January2 percent
February1 percent
MarchNone, gross amount due
  • August: the proposed-tax notice previews the bill.
  • Twenty-five days from that notice: the last chance for a value petition at the clerk's desk.
  • Thirty days after a denial letter is mailed: the window to challenge an exemption denial.
  • May 1: the cutoff for asking the collector for installments.

When a Miami-Dade bill goes unpaid

If a bill stays open, the collector packages it as a tax certificate and auctions it to the bidder willing to earn the least interest, with bids dropping a quarter point at a time. Certificates nobody bids on pass to the county at the top rate, and the sales wrap up by June 1. A homestead parcel owing less than $250 skips the auction and goes to the county. The collector retains a 5 percent commission.

Loss of the house takes longer. The certificate holder waits two years from the April after issue, then pays a $75 application charge. At the later auction the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and settles the rest inside 24 hours on business days. Ask the clerk for auction dates. A seller with an open year should get a payoff early, since the title agent cannot close over a delinquent lien and the balance grows with advertising and interest.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How fast an assessment can climb

Homestead value is held to the smaller of 3 percent and inflation. Rentals, second homes and commercial parcels face a 10 percent annual ceiling. A sale wipes out both cushions, since the new owner is assessed at market the following January 1.

A constitutional amendment that voters approved in November 2026 is already built into the appraiser's estimator, which shows Amendment 3 figures for 2027 and 2028. Run your own folio through it before guessing at a future bill. Millage itself comes out of budget hearings held in the fall.

Exemptions and deferral

The base homestead exemption reaches $50,000 and is claimed with the appraiser by March 1. Other breaks target particular owners.

  • Seniors: an extra exemption, as large as $50,000, where a local ordinance provides it and household income stays under the cap.
  • Service-connected disability at 10 percent or higher: a $5,000 reduction.
  • Veteran owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 to postpone the share of the bill above 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents past 65.

Online tools and fraud protection

Widow(er) exemptions, and disability exemptions for a veteran or surviving spouse, can be filed online, and agricultural classification uses form MD-482 with uploaded papers. Appointments can be booked online, and a tax estimator and walkthrough video sit on the appraiser's home page.

Owners of furniture, equipment and similar business property file Form DR-405 with the appraiser by April 1. The clerk runs a free alert that notifies an owner within a day when a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, and the appraiser's compliance team takes suspected homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What changes when a Miami-Dade house sells

Your title agent pulls the collector's balance and settles the year's tax at closing, split the way your contract sets out. The buyer arrives with a reassessed value and needs a fresh exemption filing.

Deed stamps are 60 cents per $100. The county adds a 45 cent surtax per $100 that state revenue officials exclude for a deed conveying nothing but a single-family house. Ask the closing agent which line your deed falls under.

Before listing, collect your latest statement, the proposed-tax notice, proof of any exemption on file and a payoff letter for any open year. A cash buyer who takes the property as is can shorten the timeline, but open taxes still come out of your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What total millage applies in unincorporated Miami-Dade for 2026?

The chart total is 16.8983 mills for the unincorporated area. Incorporated cities have their own totals.

Where can a Miami-Dade owner pay the bill?

Use the Tax Collector: its website, any of 13 locations or a visiting mobile office. The appraiser takes no payments.

How soon must a Miami-Dade value petition be filed?

Twenty-five days from the August notice of proposed taxes. File the petition with the clerk. A denied exemption follows a 30 day clock from the letter.

Does paying early cut a Miami-Dade bill?

Yes, by up to 4 percent. The reduction shrinks every month from November and is gone by March.

Is Miami-Dade subject to the Save Our Homes limit?

Yes. Homestead growth is limited to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and a sale resets it.

Broward County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Who handles what in Broward

The Broward County Property Appraiser sets assessed values and approves exemptions. It does not mail tax bills and does not set or collect taxes. Billing and collection belong to the Broward County Tax Collector, at (954) 357-4829 or revenue@browardtax.org, as printed on the appraiser's home page.

Deed recording runs through the county's official records. The appraiser's FAQ page has a deed topic for questions on adding or removing an owner or getting copies of recorded documents. Counter service is on weekdays.

Market context for sellers

Broward has 31 municipalities, and Fort Lauderdale is the seat and biggest city, with 183,146 residents. A canal-front home near Las Olas and a condo in a western city share one appraiser and one tax collector but sit in very different markets, so a neighbor's sale price may say little about yours.

Filing for 2027 homestead

The timely filing period for the 2027 exemption runs March 3, 2026 through March 1, 2027. It applies to owners who held title and made the house their permanent home after January 1, 2026.

An owner who misses March 1 has until September 20, 2027. Section 196.011(8) allows no later date, even with good cause. The dates belong to one tax year, so check the appraiser's page for later years.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Free tools from the appraiser

The appraiser's site has several tools a home sale can use.

  • A Home Buyer's Tax Estimator that approximates the bill after a reassessment. A seller can use it to show a buyer why their taxes will differ.
  • A Portability Estimator for owners moving a homestead benefit to a new Florida home.
  • Owner Alert, a free message when a filing that changes who owns your parcel reaches the appraiser.
  • A catastrophic structural damage report form for a home left uninhabitable for at least 30 days by a catastrophic event.
  • Tabs for Senior Citizens, Appeals and Petitions, Market Sales and Important Dates, and a posted Property Owner Bill of Rights.

The menu also lists Exemption Express, Download Forms, Tangible Property, Maps and Aerials, Data Requests and a Report Fraud page. A seller who rents out furnished space can start at Tangible Property, and anyone who suspects a forged deed can use the fraud page together with Owner Alert. A buyer notice on the site tells purchasers not to expect the seller's taxes to carry over, since the new owner starts at full market value.

Selling or moving with a homestead

The sale ends the homestead cap on the old house. Someone buying another Florida home can file Form DR-501T alongside the new application, provided the new homestead starts inside the three-year window. A 2026 act amends the portability section for the 2027 roll, so ask the appraiser's portability staff what applies to your move.

Rentals face a yearly ceiling of 10 percent, so a landlord's gap between assessed and market value is usually narrower than a long-time homesteader's.

Other relief programs

Age and veteran relief varies by ordinance and service record. The Senior Citizens tab on the appraiser's site is the quickest way to see what a particular address can claim. The state also offers a $5,000 reduction for disabled former servicemembers, and a deferral through the collector with a March 31 filing date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If a Broward bill goes unpaid

Delinquency starts April 1, and the collector auctions certificates for the lowest bid rate by June 1. If a tax deed notice arrives, call the collector right away. A seller who clears the balance before any deed application avoids the auction altogether, and the title agent can pay it from sale proceeds. Homestead rules on small balances and opening bids sit in s. 197.502.

Before you list, ask the collector for a current payoff figure and confirm nothing is outstanding. A clean tax record keeps the closing simple, and a cash buyer will usually want the same confirmation.

Challenging your value

The appraiser's Appeals and Petitions section lays out the route. A formal petition goes to the clerk. Property owners get 25 days from the August notice, and an exemption denial carries its own 30 day clock from the letter.

Gather recent comparable sales and photos of any condition problems before you file, and bring them with your petition.

Paperwork to bring to the office

Whether you visit the appraiser, the collector or the exemption desk, arrive with a photo ID, your parcel number, a copy of your deed and your most recent tax bill. If you are applying on behalf of a seller who has died or moved away, bring whatever proof of your authority you have. A prepared folder shortens the visit and cuts down on return trips.

Closing agents also like to receive tax payoff figures in writing, so request a printed or emailed statement and not just a number over the phone.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Heirs and unwanted occupants

An heir can call the appraiser at (954) 357-5579 to learn how a transfer on death is treated, since some transfers are exceptions to the reset.

Uninvited occupants are a separate matter. The sheriff handles a verified complaint under s. 82.036, which carries conditions such as no tenancy and no pending litigation, and adverse possession (s. 95.18) needs seven years. If occupants are holding up a sale, talk to a Florida attorney before you list.

Steps before you list

A short checklist saves trouble at closing. Pull your latest tax bill and your exemption paperwork. Confirm with the tax collector that nothing is owed. Decide whether a buyer will be told about the reassessment, and print the estimator result if you plan to share it. Then give your title agent the parcel ID and the name of anyone who may need to sign.

At the closing table, the title agent normally prorates the year's taxes between you and the buyer and pays off any lien from your proceeds. Ask for the settlement statement ahead of time and read each tax line.

Selling for cash with taxes owed

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, so a back tax balance doesn't stall a loan approval. It still has to be paid, usually out of proceeds at closing. If you are behind, ask the collector for a payoff figure, give it to the title agent, and confirm the lien is released after funding. Keep the receipt with your closing papers.

How the county's history touches a sale

Broward became Florida's 51st county on October 1, 1915, carved out of Dade and Palm Beach territory. Northern Dade residents had complained that their tax dollars favored Miami, which helped push the new county into being.

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects Broward tax?

The Broward County Tax Collector. The appraiser neither sends bills nor collects taxes.

What is the late-filing limit for a 2027 Broward homestead?

September 20, 2027, with no later date allowed under s. 196.011(8).

Can I file my Broward homestead online?

Yes, through the appraiser's online homestead page at bcpa.net. Email, fax, mail and phone help are also available, and staff can set a virtual meeting for owners who want help with the forms.

What does Owner Alert do?

It's a free service that notifies you when a document changing your property's ownership reaches the appraiser. It is meant to help protect a parcel from scams or fraud.

When does a Broward bill turn delinquent?

April 1, with certificates sold by June 1.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Hillsborough County property tax?

Who to call about Hillsborough County property tax

The right office depends on the question. Value and exemptions belong to the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser. Money, receipts and payment plans belong to the Hillsborough County Tax Collector.

The appraiser's downtown Tampa office is on the 15th floor of the County Center, 601 E. Kennedy Boulevard, and answers at (813) 272-6100 Monday through Friday from 8 to 5. The collector's real estate tax page has bills, payment options and a property search. Disputes over value or exemptions go to the Value Adjustment Board, which is separate from both offices.

  • Property Appraiser: just value, homestead filings, the assessment cap, portability and the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment applications, partial payments and tax certificates.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: recorded deeds, liens and the tax deed auction.

The appraiser also offers a free Property Fraud Alert that flags new recordings made in your name. Heirs who hold an empty Tampa Bay house are the people most likely to want it turned on.

How does the bill and early payment discount work?

Tax notices arrive in November and can be paid beginning November 1. An account still open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Early payers save 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March is full price. A winter seller should ask the closing agent which month the closing date lands in, since sale proceeds may be what pays the bill.

For smaller checks, the installment plan requires an application before May 1 and begins with a June payment. A July payment keeps the plan alive but loses the discount. If nothing is received by July 31, the account leaves the plan and the whole balance is payable the next November, with the 4 percent break. A separate partial payment option exists for current-year bills only. An overdue real estate account must be cleared in one payment.

Dates to put on your calendar

Seven dates drive nearly every decision a Hillsborough County owner or seller faces.

WhenWhat it triggers
January 1Valuation date and homestead test date
March 1Exemption filing deadline
May 1Last day to request the installment plan
By June 1Online auction of tax certificates
AugustTRIM notice mailed, then 25 days to petition on value
November 1Bills payable
April 1Delinquency

An owner whose exemption is refused receives an Official Notice of Denial by July 1, which opens the right to a hearing before a Value Adjustment Board magistrate.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Stacking exemptions

A permanent residence can shed up to $50,000 of assessed value in two layers. The first layer touches every levy. The second sits on the slice of assessed value above $50,000 and skips school taxes. After the first year, a yearly growth limit applies. The appraiser accepts filings year round, treats March 1 as the legal deadline, and may take a late one up to 25 days after TRIM notices go out.

  • Low income senior: unincorporated Hillsborough County and the City of Tampa allow up to $50,000, and Temple Terrace allows up to $25,000.
  • Long term resident senior: Tampa and unincorporated areas, for homes with just value under $250,000 and 25 consecutive years in residence.
  • Veteran, disability, widow and blind exemptions: these need documents, and the county's veteran affairs office, at 813-635-8316, helps with discharge papers.

Claiming homestead on a house you have left is costly. The exempted taxes from the prior 10 years can turn into a lien with a 50 percent penalty and 15 percent interest, so report a move-out before the sign goes in the yard.

What did Amendment 3 change for homesteads?

Voters passed the statewide property tax amendment on November 3, 2026. The appraiser's legislative update page describes homestead exemption amounts of up to $150,000 from 2027 and up to $250,000 from 2028, with lawmakers directed to schedule further increases. The effect varies by parcel and cannot be calculated in advance, so treat the figure on today's bill as your working number until a TRIM notice shows a new one. The tax collector keeps a property tax reform page on the same ballot item.

Sellers mostly feel this through the buyer. The first bill after a purchase starts from just value, and a new exemption amount reaches the buyer only after an application is filed.

Who pays the tax when a house closes?

An open bill is settled from the seller's proceeds at the table, because the lien stays with the land. The name printed on a bill is no obstacle to paying it, since a recorded deed may not have reached the appraiser before the roll was certified.

The seller's homestead ends with the sale, and the buyer starts at just value after the next January 1 with a new application. What the seller can carry along is the portable savings, which attach to a replacement home.

  • Escrowed loans: the servicer pays from a list it sends the collector, and once the loan is paid off the next bill is mailed to the owner.
  • Deed stamps: the state rate applies here because Hillsborough is not Miami-Dade, and each party on the deed shares the liability.
  • Portability: the replacement homestead has a three year window and needs a DR-501T with the new application.

Plain preparation helps. Ask the title agent to request the payoff from the collector close to the closing date. Check earlier years for balances as well as the current bill. A cash buyer needs no lender sign-off, so a payoff taken from your proceeds does not hold up funding.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How unpaid tax reaches a tax deed sale

A skipped bill becomes a tax certificate first, and a deed sale can follow about two years later.

The collector auctions certificates online. Bids start at 18 percent and fall by 0.25 percent per step, and the lowest bidder wins a certificate that ranks first among liens, including other government ones. A deed application cannot begin until up to 22 months after issue, and the statute measures two years from April 1 of the issue year. When a homestead owes under $250, the county takes the certificate itself and no investor can buy it.

The clerk conducts the deed auction, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half of the last assessed value. An owner who is behind can still sell, since paying off the certificate at closing clears the title.

Frequently asked questions

When is Hillsborough County property tax due?

Bills are payable November 1 and go delinquent April 1. The discount is 4 percent in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent through February. An account open on April 1 picks up 3% interest and advertising costs.

Can I pay Hillsborough County tax in installments?

Yes, if you apply before May 1. The first payment is due in June, a July payment keeps you in the plan without the discount, and missing July 31 drops the account into a single November payment with the 4 percent discount.

Who decides a Hillsborough County homestead claim?

The Property Appraiser. Filing closes March 1, any denial notice is mailed by July 1, and an appeal goes to the Value Adjustment Board. The collector never rules on eligibility.

Are partial payments allowed on a delinquent Hillsborough County bill?

No. Only current-year bills qualify for the partial plan, and an overdue real estate bill needs the full balance. Call the collector before sending anything smaller.

What if I sell before my Hillsborough County bill arrives?

The bill is still paid at closing. The title agent requests the amount from the collector and takes it out of the seller's money, and the buyer applies for a new homestead by the next March 1.

Which Palm Beach County office to call

Which door to knock on depends on what you are asking. Value, exemptions and caps are the Property Appraiser's territory. How much you owe, and how to hand it over, is for the Tax Collector. Appeals and tax deed auctions run through the Clerk and Comptroller, who staffs the Value Adjustment Board.

By November 1 the Tax Collector has put more than 600,000 property tax bills in the mail, every one sent to the address in the appraiser's file. If you moved or sold, fix the mailing address with the appraiser. The collector cannot change it.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, caps, the TRIM notice.
  • Tax Collector: bills, payment, installment plan, deferral, certificates.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: appeals board petitions and tax deed sales.

The county in brief

Palm Beach County has about 1,575,726 residents. Of the homes here, 70.1 percent are owner-occupied, with a median value of $447,300. The appraiser assigns a two-digit code to each taxing municipality, starting with 00 for unincorporated land, and the first digits of the 17-digit parcel control number carry that code. Read that number off your bill and you know which city, if any, taxes the lot. Cities with codes include Boca Raton, Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Jupiter, Lake Worth Beach, Palm Beach, West Palm Beach and Wellington.

Exemptions listed on the appraiser's chart

More than a dozen exemptions appear on the chart, and a few carry dollar limits that change each year. For 2026 the senior exemption has an income limit of $38,686 in adjusted gross income, and the civilian total and permanent disability and paraplegic or hemiplegic exemptions use $37,712 in gross income. Eligibility looks at the prior year's income.

Selected exemptions and what each one asks for
ExemptionAmountPaperwork or condition
Homestead$25,000, plus a varying second tierResidency as of January 1; second tier needs assessed value of at least $50,000
Widow or widower$5,000Death certificate
Limited income senior$25,000Age 65 or older, annual income statement
Super Senior, Boynton Beach and Delray Beach onlyExempt from that city's levies25 years of ownership, value under $250,000
Disabled veteran, 10 to 90 percent$5,000VA benefits letter
Total and permanent disabled veteranFully exempt, apart from non ad valorem assessmentsVA letters
Disabled first responderFully exempt, apart from non ad valorem assessmentsAgency certificate, two physician letters

Applications close March 1. Military and disabled applicants can start at the county Veteran Services office.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead filing and the caps

To qualify, you need title in your name, a permanent Florida residence and the house as your home on January 1. March 1 is the filing deadline, and filing late costs you that year's exemption. Online, in person at a service center or by mail all work, and an approved exemption renews itself until a change occurs.

The first $25,000 reduces every levy, school taxes included. Another slice of up to $25,000 starts once assessed value goes beyond $50,000 and skips the school levy. Under Save Our Homes, a homestead assessment can climb each year by inflation or 3 percent, whichever is smaller; the state chart's entry for 2026 is 2.7.

A rental or second home has a 10 percent cap on every levy except the school board's, and the appraiser says that cap falls away the year after a sale. Tell the appraiser about any change in ownership, marriage, divorce, death or how the home is used.

Due dates, discounts and installments

The payment season is November 1 through March 31. Early payers take 4 percent off in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February, and March means the full amount.

April 1 begins delinquency. Late tax cannot be paid online, and the money has to be in the collector's hands by the final working day of the month, since postmarks stop mattering.

The installment plan breaks the bill into four payments, due around June or July, September, December and March. Applications are due April 30, and enrollment for the next cycle opens November 1. Check the collector's current calendar for the exact dates.

When a Palm Beach County home sells

A balance owed stays with the parcel until the closing table. The title agent reads the bill and takes any payoff out of your proceeds. Settle with the buyer how this year's bill is shared; bills mail in November, but closings occur all twelve months.

State stamp tax on the deed is seventy cents per hundred dollars in every county but Miami-Dade. Each person who signs is answerable to the state for it, whatever the contract assigns. It is paid at the recording counter beside the page fees under section 28.24.

From the next January 1 the new owner is assessed at market value. Your capped savings stay behind, which is why a long-time neighbor and a recent buyer can get very different bills.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens to unpaid taxes

Nonpayment advances in stages, and you can stop it by paying at any point before the auction. Once a year the collector sells certificates, no earlier than 60 days after delinquency or June 1, whichever is later. A certificate is a first lien bought by an investor who pays your tax in exchange for a competitive bid rate.

Redeeming takes the overdue tax, interest, advertising costs and a $6.25 collection fee on each certificate. If no investor bids, the county holds the certificate and interest accrues at 18 percent a year.

After two years the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed, and the clerk's office carries out the sale. Redemption remains possible right up to the sale. Falling behind does not prevent a sale of the house, as the closing settles the balance.

Disputing an assessment

Call the appraiser first; the office encourages that conversation, and its records are searchable online. If you still disagree, file with the Value Adjustment Board.

On the appraiser's calendar, mid-September is the end of the window for market value appeals and denied portability claims. A denied exemption has until July 31 or the 30th day after the denial notice. The state taxpayer page also gives a 25-day limit counted from the TRIM mailing. Your own notice has the final word on timing. The Clerk runs the board separately from the appraiser, so ask what the filing fee is before you file.

Getting ready to sell

Look up your parcel and read the exemption line to see what the county has on file. Open the Tax Collector's account to see which years are paid. If anything is open, request a payoff in writing and keep it with your closing papers. Gather the last TRIM notice and the most recent bill so the buyer and title agent see the same numbers you do.

Whether you list the house or sell for cash, the tax steps are the same. The lien travels with the parcel and is paid from the proceeds, so there is no reason to wait for a perfect payoff before you start talking to buyers.

Frequently asked questions

Where does my Palm Beach County tax payment go?

To the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. The Property Appraiser only sets value and exemptions.

Does paying early cut a Palm Beach County bill?

Yes. The discount starts at 4 percent for November and falls a point monthly, ending after February.

Does homestead end when a Palm Beach County home is sold?

The sale ends it for that house. Apply again for your next home, and use portability to bring part of your capped savings along if you buy within three years.

What is the Super Senior exemption?

It exempts a qualifying owner from city levies in Boynton Beach or Delray Beach only. It needs 25 years of ownership and a market value under $250,000 at application.

Which office records a Palm Beach County deed?

The Clerk and Comptroller records it and collects the documentary stamp tax at that time.

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Who answers questions about an Orange County tax statement?

Orange County divides the job three ways, so the right call depends on the problem. A wrong value or missing exemption belongs to the Property Appraiser at 200 S Orange Ave, Suite 1700 in Orlando. A bill, a payment or a delinquency belongs to the Tax Collector. The rate itself is a product of local boards.

  • Value, ownership, legal description and mailing address: Property Appraiser.
  • Millage: the county commission, school board, cities and special districts.
  • Statements, payment plans, certificates: Tax Collector.

The Tax Collector distributes the money to 63 taxing authorities. Streetlights, sewers and road work are non-ad valorem charges, priced per unit and printed on the same statement.

Property tax calendar

The year's value is pinned to January 1. Statements reach owners by the first of November, and the balance must arrive at the Tax Collector before April begins.

Property tax dates in Orange County
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Last day to file an exemption request
AugustProposed tax notice mailed
By November 1Statements mailed
November to FebruaryFour, three, two and one percent discounts
March 31Gross amount and deferral applications due
April 1Delinquency begins
By June 1Online certificate sale

A check postmarked March 30 but delivered in April is late, because the office goes by receipt.

What early payment saves

Pay in November and the bill drops four percent. Each later month trims one point less, ending at one percent in February, and March pays the gross figure.

Sellers who close in winter can pay the whole year at the closing table, so the month on the contract changes the net. Your title agent can quote the number for your actual closing day. When a lender escrows your taxes it may request the statement, and you receive a copy stamped with the lender's request. That copy does not call for a second payment.

Owners who are current and whose prior bill topped $100 can apply online at the Tax Collector's site for the quarterly installment plan.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exemptions for an Orange County home

Homestead leads the list, and it can lower taxable value by as much as $50,000. The opening $25,000 touches every levy, and a second slice reaches only non-school levies above $50,000 of assessed value.

File with the Property Appraiser before March 1, and live in the house as your permanent home on January 1. Widow, disability, senior and military exemptions also exist. Once homesteaded, the assessed figure may rise each year by no more than the smaller of 3 percent or the inflation change. A sale wipes out that gap on the following January 1, so a buyer's first bill can be well above yours. The appraiser's tax estimator is aimed at people weighing a purchase or sale.

Can a house with old tax debt change hands?

You can still sell. The title agent requests a payoff from the Tax Collector, and every open balance gets cleared as part of closing.

Once April arrives, the Tax Collector adds a 3 percent minimum charge and advertising cost. Parcels are listed in a local paper for three straight weeks, then certificates go up for competitive bids that start at 18 percent and drop. To clear a certificate, pay the tax, accrued interest and advertising cost. Late payers must use certified or cashier's funds, a money order, certain attorney, title or escrow checks, or cash at the counter. Personal and business checks are refused.

  • Ask for the payoff before you list.
  • Confirm whether a certificate already exists.
  • Compare escrow records with the county account.

How long before a certificate threatens the house?

Two years. Only then can the certificate holder apply for a tax deed, and Orange County routes those sales through the Comptroller's Office.

Before that, state law bars the holder from pressing the owner for payment. Homestead land gets one more cushion, because the opening bid must include half of its latest assessed value on top of the money due. An owner facing this stage should still call the Tax Collector's property tax department early and ask for a redemption total.

Deferring homestead tax

Qualifying homesteaders can postpone part of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector before April. This is a different program from the exemption.

Postponed tax remains a lien on the property. Before listing, ask the Tax Collector how a postponed balance, with interest, is paid off in a sale. The state ties the amount to household income and lets a permanent resident aged 65 or older defer the share above 3 percent of that income.

Property Appraiser website tools

The appraiser's site offers a property search by address, owner name, sale history, property use and foreclosure status. It also links a tax estimator, a map site, downloadable forms, a tax roll and millage page, an income survey for commercial owners, code tables and a property fraud alert.

  • Use the search to confirm the parcel, owner and exemptions on your record.
  • Run the estimator when you want a buyer to see a likely tax picture.
  • Download the exemption forms if a new owner needs to file.
  • Sign up for the fraud alert to watch your record.

Treat the estimator as a planning aid, since a new owner may not keep the seller's exemptions.

Landlords and tangible personal property

A rental that holds furniture, fixtures or equipment can owe a second tax. The Tax Collector describes tangible personal property tax as a levy on those items in businesses and rental property, and on structural additions to mobile homes.

These statements arrive alongside the real estate statements and carry the same discounts. Past March 31 a monthly charge of 1.5 percent accrues, and a collection firm under contract adds 15 percent on accounts left unpaid. If you are selling a furnished rental, ask the Tax Collector how any open account is handled.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

The local numbers

Orange County had 1,528,002 people in July 2025, spread over 527,776 households. Owners live in 56.8 percent of the homes, and the median value is $390,100. A median mortgage holder spends $2,055 monthly, against $1,775 for a typical rent.

A statement's lines shift with the home's location: inside a city, in unincorporated Orange County, or within a special district. Read those lines on your own account before quoting a tax figure to a buyer.

Steps before closing

These are general steps for any seller. Confirm the owner name and exemptions on the parcel record. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff on any open year and for the redemption total if a certificate exists. Gather your latest statement and the August notice for the title agent. Agree in the contract on how the current year's tax is split, and read the settlement statement before you sign. A buyer paying cash can close faster, but open taxes are still paid from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Until what date can Orange County owners pay without a late charge?

March 31, counted by the day the Tax Collector receives it. A check that lands in April is delinquent.

What does a November payment save?

Four percent. The discount shrinks by a point each month until February, and March has none.

Which Orange County office fixes a wrong value or missing exemption?

The Property Appraiser. The Tax Collector bills what the certified roll shows and cannot change value, ownership or exemptions.

Can a homeowner with unpaid taxes still sell in Orange County?

Yes. Request the Tax Collector's payoff, then let the title agent settle it at closing, with certified funds if the bill is already delinquent.

Does a tax certificate transfer my house to an investor?

No. It is a lien, and you can redeem it by paying the tax, interest and advertising cost. A tax deed application cannot come until two years have run.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who to call in Jacksonville and Duval County

Jacksonville and Duval County are consolidated, and two city departments split the property tax work. The Property Appraiser values parcels and decides exemptions. The Tax Collector sends the bills and takes the money. Both post their pages on jacksonville.gov.

The appraiser's Customer Service and Exemptions Division is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Suite 260, phone 904-255-5900. The collector is on the same street at 231 E. Forsyth Street, main line (904) 255-5700. Its weekday counter opens at half past eight and closes at half past four. Value petitions go through the Value Adjustment Board at (904) 255-5124.

If downtown is a hassle, the collector also runs branches at Yates (main), Mandarin, Neptune Beach, North Main Street, Roosevelt, Soutel and Westside, plus a newer St Johns Square branch at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121. That branch replaced the Kernan and Hogan offices, both permanently closed.

Tax districts and millage

Every Duval parcel carries a district code, and the code decides which taxing authorities apply. There are six: GS and USD1 for Jacksonville, USD2 for Jacksonville Beach, USD3 for Atlantic Beach, USD4 for Neptune Beach and USD5 for Baldwin.

A district's total millage is built from separate levies. Countywide those are the county, the public schools, the Florida Inland Navigation District and the St. Johns River Water Management District. The three beach cities and the Town of Baldwin add their own municipal levies. Within one district, homes and businesses see the same millage unless a statute or local ordinance exempts something.

The appraiser posts a millage chart for each year back to 1999, which lets you see how your district's total has moved. The individual levies are set at public meetings in September, and the dates appear on the mailed notice.

Annual tax calendar

Florida's yearly calendar repeats in Duval, so the same steps return every year.

Duval County property tax steps
StepWhen it happens
Preliminary tax roll approvedLate July
TRIM notices mailedAugust
Final tax roll certifiedOctober
Tax bills mailed by the collectorOn or about November 1
Timely homestead filing for the 2027 rollMarch 1, 2027
Tangible personal property returnApril 1 each year
Delinquency dateApril 1

If a mortgage servicer pays your tax from escrow, ask which bill it paid before you request a payoff, so nothing gets paid twice.

Filing for homestead

Owners who bought and moved in after January 1, 2026 can file online for the 2027 roll. A paper form can be mailed to Suite 260, faxed to (904) 255-7963 or emailed to the customer service address on the appraiser's page.

  • The home must be your permanent residence, or that of someone who depends on you, on January 1 of the roll year.
  • Some situations call for extra documents; the online form prompts for them at the end.
  • A previous Florida homestead may let you carry over part of the Save Our Homes difference through portability.

You can still file late until the 25th day after the August notices go out, which lands in early September. When you sell, your exemption stays behind. The buyer files fresh for the following roll.

Disagreeing with your value

Begin with an informal review at the appraiser's office. If that does not settle it, file a DR-486 petition with the Value Adjustment Board. The deadline is printed on your TRIM notice.

One practical detail: if you ask for the property record card with your petition, it is not mailed. You will find it online in Property Search, under the TRIM record card link just below the notice section. If the page will not open or print, call 904-255-5900.

The Board's page also cautions that petitioners generally must pay 75 percent of the ad valorem tax, plus every non-ad valorem charge, before the usual April 1 delinquency date, or the petition can be denied. Call the Board at (904) 255-5124 to learn your own figure.

Aerial photos and property lines

The imagery on the appraiser's site does not always show true boundaries, and the office says it should not be relied on in a purchase. Use a surveyor and a title company for any sale.

The same page says Florida law requires the office to inspect every property in the county at least once every five years. Staff do not go inside homes. Appraisers drive marked vehicles, wear shirts with the city seal and carry City of Jacksonville identification, which helps if someone knocks and claims to be from the office.

Because the images are also used by Realtors and appraisers, a buyer may have studied your roofline before the first showing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Watching for fake deeds

The Duval Clerk runs a free Property Fraud Alert. Sign up with a personal or business name, and an alert arrives within 48 hours after any document is recorded under that name in Duval County.

Scammers file bogus deeds to pose as owners, then rent or sell homes that are not theirs. Empty or inherited houses make easy targets, so a seller holding a vacant property gains the most from enrolling.

Report suspected exemption fraud to the appraiser's hotline at (904) 255-7964. If a family house is still in the name of someone who died, the unresolved ownership can affect the homestead. The appraiser's page points to Jacksonville Area Legal Aid and LISC Jacksonville for heirs' property help and says probate or another legal process may be needed.

Short-term rentals

Two obligations appear when a Duval home hosts short stays. Transient rentals owe additional sales and use tax to the Tax Collector every month, and furnishings in a rental count as taxable tangible personal property.

  • Airbnb, VRBO and similar sites do not send the tax to Duval for their users, so the owner remits it. Questions go to TouristTax@coj.net.
  • Household goods for your own use are excluded, but furniture and appliances in any rental, short or long, count.
  • Anyone owning such property on January 1 files a return by April 1.

Renting the home also ends the homestead, which raises taxable value after the next January 1.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the collector for a payoff on every open year, confirm the parcel matches your deed and keep a copy of the closing statement. The state deed tax is seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price, and the recording clerk collects it.

Gather your photo ID, the deed, the latest tax bill and your mortgage statement before you meet the title agent. The agent orders the payoff, divides the year's tax between you and the buyer, and pays what you owe from your proceeds, so you do not need cash on hand. Look at the draft settlement statement a few days early and compare each tax line with the collector's figure.

Some owners hold separate benefits at the appraiser. A disabled former servicemember rated 10 percent or more gets $5,000 off assessed value. A deferral under Form DR-570 is filed with the collector by March 31. Ask whether a local older-owner exemption applies to your parcel. A cash buyer can usually close on a short schedule, which helps when a tax deadline is close.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Duval County tax collector's main office?

It is at 231 E. Forsyth Street, Jacksonville, FL 32202, phone (904) 255-5700, open Monday to Friday from half past eight until half past four. A newer branch operates at 11160 Beach Blvd., Suite 121.

When are TRIM notices mailed in Duval County?

In August each year. The petition deadline for the Value Adjustment Board is printed on each notice, so check your own.

Can I file for homestead online in Duval County?

Yes. Owners who moved into a Duval home after January 1, 2026 can use the online application for the 2027 roll. The timely deadline is March 1, 2027, and late filing runs to early September.

Does Airbnb collect Duval tourist tax for me?

No. Hosting sites do not remit tax directly to Duval County for users, so the property owner sends it to the Tax Collector's office.

How do I get notified if someone records a deed under my name?

Sign up for the Duval Clerk's free Property Fraud Alert at duvalclerk.gov. It watches a personal or business name and emails you within 48 hours of a matching recording.

What a Pinellas tax bill covers

The tax collector counts 495,057 accounts on the 2026 roll, worth more than $2.75 billion, divided among 56 local taxing authorities, including the school board, the county commission, the cities and libraries. The appraiser lists 437,624 real property parcels, 408,947 of them residential, from condo towers to manufactured home communities. Whatever you own, you deal with the same two offices.

Three kinds of charges can show up on one notice. Ad valorem tax follows value. Tangible personal property tax covers furniture and equipment in businesses and rentals. Non-ad valorem assessments are fixed amounts for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue and solid waste, and they do not depend on value.

The appraiser keeps ownership and mailing addresses, and the collector says it does not maintain them. If no bill arrives in November, call 727-464-7777 or search the collector's database. A notice that never came does not excuse payment.

Discount cutoffs for 2026

The cutoff depends on how you pay. Online payments run until 11:55 pm Eastern on the last discount day. Counter and drop box payments stop at closing time, and a mailed check needs a postmark from that month.

Counter or drop box cutoffs for the 2026 bill
Discount monthLast day, close of businessDiscount

If a discount month ends on a weekend or holiday, paying online or in person the next business day keeps the discount.

Ways to pay

  • Online eChecks carry no fee but cannot be used for delinquent bills. Credit and debit cards add a 2.5 percent vendor fee.
  • Checks by mail go to P.O. Box 31149, Tampa, FL 33631-3149. The collector warns that USPS now postmarks at a regional processing facility, so a late drop in a local box may miss a deadline.
  • Drop boxes sit outside select offices, and paying at an office needs no appointment.
  • Multiple checks must travel in one envelope, and a check that bounces is handled by a recovery partner that may re-present it with a fee.

An online payment shows as paid at once in the collector's system, though a bank can take up to five business days to reflect it. For 2026, bills went out beginning October 30. Online payment opens November 1, and counter and mail payment opens November 2.

Installment plan

Owners with an estimated bill above $100 can pay in four installments, which earns a discount of roughly 3.5 percent overall. Applications for the 2027 plan open November 1, 2026 and run through April 30, 2027.

  • June 30: one quarter of last year's total, discounted 6 percent.
  • September 30: another quarter, discounted 4.5 percent.
  • December 31: a quarter plus half of any adjustment, discounted 3 percent.
  • March 31: a quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, with no discount.

A June payment missed can still be made by July 31 without the discount, and missing July 31 removes the account. A late second or third payment rolls into the next one and loses its discount. Once enrolled, you do not reapply each year as long as the first payment arrives.

Partial payments and deferral

Under a partial payment plan, an owner pays current-year tax in pieces of at least $100, but only until March 31, and the early payment discounts are lost. Delinquent bills are not eligible. The 2026 application stays open through March 31, 2027, and a balance unpaid by May 31 goes to a certificate sale.

Deferral suits homestead holders, since it rests on the prior year's household income. The collector stresses that deferral creates a lien and that deferred tax accrues interest every month. The 2026 application deadline is March 31, 2027, and the office answers at 727-464-3409.

Amendment 3 and your estimate

The collector said Amendment 3 would not change 2026 bills, and that any change would begin with the 2027 tax year. Afterward, the Pinellas Property Appraiser's home page reported updating its website for the amendment's passage. If you are giving a buyer a tax estimate for next year, look at the appraiser's updated exemption pages first.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appraiser offices

The county courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd Floor, Clearwater. North County is at Northside Square, 29269 US Hwy 19 North, Clearwater. Mid County shares space with the tax collector at 13025 Starkey Rd, Largo, and South County is at 2500 34th Street North, 2nd Floor, St. Petersburg. The main line is (727) 464-3207, answered on weekdays.

Selling with tax still due

Ask the collector for a payoff so the closing agent can settle it from proceeds. Delinquency begins April 1, and the collector lists its 2027 certificate sale for Friday, May 28, 2027, with online payments of 2026 taxes accepted until 5:00 pm on May 27. The title agent clears any certificate.

The buyer's reassessment will not follow your old bill, and a homestead sale ends the cap, though portability may help your next home.

If a certificate was already sold on the parcel, the payoff will include it, and the title agent will want the redemption amount in writing with a good-through date. Ask for a fresh figure if the closing date moves, because interest and fees can change the total.

Keep every receipt. A paid-in-full printout from the collector is the cleanest proof you can hand to a buyer or a lender.

A year of the tax calendar, from a seller's side

Late October: bills are mailed, and the discount clock starts in November. November through February: each month you wait costs one percentage point, so a seller expecting to close soon can often save money by paying early and settling up with the buyer at the table. March: the full amount is due by March 31. April 1: the bill turns delinquent and the account stops being eligible for online payment. May: unpaid current-year balances move toward the certificate sale.

Closing dates rarely line up with that calendar. If you close in the middle of a discount month, ask the title agent whether paying the bill first makes sense and how the buyer will reimburse you for their share of the year.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for a Pinellas seller

Start by searching the parcel on the collector's site to see what is paid and what is open. Request a written payoff that matches your expected closing date, and ask the title agent to confirm it. If you used an installment plan, deferral or partial payment arrangement, tell the title agent right away, since each one affects the figure at closing.

Give your buyer the appraiser's parcel record instead of your own bill as a guide to next year's taxes. Bills for owners of long standing often sit far below what a new owner pays, so your number may mislead.

Whether you list the house or sell for cash, expect the lien to be settled from the sale proceeds and ask the closing agent for a settlement statement that shows the tax line.

Frequently asked questions

Which office handles the Pinellas bill?

The tax collector mails and collects it. The property appraiser sets value and keeps the mailing address.

What is the 2026 Pinellas November discount?

It is 4 percent. December is 3, January 2 and February 1, with no discount in March.

What do Pinellas installments save?

The collector says about 3.5 percent overall, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three quarters.

Can I make partial payments in Pinellas?

Yes, in amounts of at least $100 before April 1, but early payment discounts are lost.

Does Amendment 3 touch the 2026 Pinellas bill?

No. The collector said any change would begin with the 2027 tax year.

Lee County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Who bills and who values

Two separate offices handle Lee County's tax side. For value, exemptions and the mailing address on file, dial the appraiser at 239-533-6100. For anything about paying, dial the collector at 239-533-6000.

Sellers run into this at closing. Value and exemption changes are off the table at the collector's counter, and the appraiser takes no money. Roads, fire, water and sewer assessments belong to whichever authority levied them, and its contact information sits on the bill.

  • Appraiser: parcel records, value, exemption files, mailing address.
  • Collector: bills, receipts, quarterly and partial payment plans, deferral.
  • Clerk: deed recording, stamp tax, and petitions in value disputes.

Deadlines and early payment

Payment season starts November 1 and ends March 31 of the next calendar year. Whatever is still owed on April 1 is delinquent.

Florida's early-pay scale gives 4 percent in November, then one point less each month until February; March earns nothing. If the notice still names a lender after you paid the loan off, the November discount is not blocked, the collector says.

One calendar covers every city here, Cape Coral through Sanibel. Owners can pay six ways: web, phone, mail, in person, kiosks, and 24-hour lockers at four centers. Late tax calls for more secure funds than a personal check or eCheck, so arrange certified money ahead of any closing.

Payment plans from the Lee County Tax Collector

Owners can choose quarterly installments, partial payments or homestead deferral, and the installment application is the first to close.

Lee County payment plans at a glance
PlanApplyMain rule
Quarterly installmentsBy April 30 of the tax year (applications open November 1)Estimated tax must exceed $100 per notice; payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31
Partial paymentsNovember 1 to March 31Up to five payments per account; none online; no discounts
Homestead deferralBy March 31Age, income and lien rules apply; deferred tax becomes a lien and fire insurance is required

The first installment earns 6 percent, the second 4.5 percent, the third 3 percent and the last nothing. A first payment not made by July 31 ends enrollment. Partial payments apply to the live tax year only and never to delinquent tax, and installment enrollees cannot add them.

A mid-year sale leaves the plan running, since the new owner takes it over through year end. Let the closing agent know early.

Homestead and senior exemptions

The first $25,000 of assessed value is exempt from every levy under homestead. The appraiser prints a second layer of up to $26,411 for 2026, which reaches non-school levies only and sits on value above $50,000.

File Form DR-501 by March 1. Choices: online at leepa.org, email to exemptions@leepa.org, mail to PO Box 1546, Fort Myers, FL 33902, or hand delivery at 2480 Thompson Street, 4th Floor, Fort Myers, during weekday business hours. The office completes processing by July 1. Save Our Homes, which limits annual assessment increases, starts one year after the grant.

Senior exemptions for income-qualified owners aged 65 and over differ by taxing body:

  • City of Sanibel, City of Bonita Springs and City of Fort Myers: $25,000.
  • City of Cape Coral: $50,000.
  • Town of Fort Myers Beach and Village of Estero: $50,000 and up to $250,000.
  • All Lee County millages: $50,000 and up to $250,000.

The appraiser also lists exemptions for disabled veteran owners, disabled first responders, surviving spouses and deployed service members, plus $5,000 exemptions for widows, widowers, blind owners and others with disabilities. Most renew every January 1 unless ownership or residency changes.

What happens to homestead when you sell?

The exemption does not transfer. The buyer files a new application, and yours ends at the start of the next year.

If a TRIM notice lists homestead in the purchase year, it is showing the seller's benefit, and that will be taken off. Long-term renting can end the exemption, as can moving title into certain trusts or LLCs. The office asks to be told about every ownership change.

Buying again in Florida means a new homestead application at the new address, along with a portability claim for the Save Our Homes benefit. The state allows three years, counted from January 1 of the year the old homestead ended, and the portability form is DR-501T, due March 1.

TRIM notice versus tax bill

The appraiser mails TRIM in mid-August as a preview. The real charge arrives from the collector, usually in November, and only the bill lists non-ad valorem items such as garbage, fire or water.

On the notice you will see market value, exemptions, Save Our Homes status and proposed tax. To contest a value, petition the Value Adjustment Board inside 25 days of the notice date; a denied exemption has its own 30 days from the denial letter. Save both documents for any buyer curious about carrying costs.

Amendment 3 takes effect January 1, 2027, the collector's FAQ answers, so the 2026 bill is unaffected. Millage depends on your address, across school, city and district levies, so rely on your parcel lookup and notice, not a countywide average.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Who pays Lee County tax at a sale?

On the settlement statement, the closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties. The bill, though, goes to the owner of record at the time the roll reaches the collector, which means a past owner can still get one in the mail.

Forward it to the new owner or the closing agent. Transfers are recorded by the clerk and relayed to the appraiser afterward, so delays happen. Any unpaid tax turns up in the title search and is cleared from seller funds.

The stamp tax on a Lee County deed is the usual Florida rate of 70 cents per $100 of consideration (Miami-Dade differs). Both parties are answerable, and payment goes to the clerk when the deed is recorded.

Lee County at a glance

About 875,607 people live in this Gulf Coast county, 15.1 percent more than in 2020. The county has 479,540 housing units, 74.3 percent occupied by their owners, and a median home value of $362,200 for 2020 to 2024. With 29.2 percent of residents at 65 or older, the senior exemptions above matter in many sales.

Incorporated areas are Cape Coral, Fort Myers, Bonita Springs, Estero, Sanibel and Fort Myers Beach; everything else is unincorporated and handled by the same two offices.

Getting ready to sell: a short checklist

  1. Search your parcel on the appraiser's site and confirm the owner name and mailing address.
  2. Get a current balance from the collector, including word on any delinquent year.
  3. On installments? Collect a record of what you have paid and give it to the closing agent.
  4. Set aside the TRIM notice and last tax bill in case buyers ask about costs.
  5. Pick the location of your next homestead early, so the portability filing can be planned.

A cash buyer skips lender underwriting, yet the title search still shows unpaid tax, so the same papers apply.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Do the Lee County tax dates change each year?

No. The calendar repeats: open November 1, due March 31, delinquent April 1, with a discount that falls from 4 percent to 1 percent between November and February.

Can I still join the Lee County installment plan after April 30?

No. Applications run November 1 to April 30. After that, only partial payments remain, open through March 31.

Does the buyer get my homestead exemption in Lee County?

No. The buyer files a new application, and a TRIM notice that lists homestead after a purchase is still showing the seller's old benefit.

Whom should I contact if my Lee County value looks wrong?

Start with the appraiser at 239-533-6100. A formal petition uses a DR-486 form, filed with the clerk inside 25 days of the proposed-tax notice.

What happens if Lee County property tax is unpaid when I sell?

It is paid from your proceeds at closing, with any added charges. Late tax cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck, so ask the collector what funds it accepts.

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Who does what on a Pasco tax bill

Three elected offices split the work. The appraiser sets values, the collector sends bills and takes payment, and the clerk staffs the appeals board and records your deed.

The appraiser's roll counts 335,946 real property parcels, among them 206,994 single family homes and 11,888 condominium units. Appraiser offices are in Dade City (352-521-4433), Land O' Lakes (813-929-2780) and New Port Richey (727-847-8151).

The Tax Collector has offices in New Port Richey, Gulf Harbors, Land O'Lakes, Wesley Chapel and Dade City. Its tax department answers at 352-521-4338, prompt 3.

  • Pasco County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, taxing districts list, records search.
  • Pasco County Tax Collector: bills, online payment, installment plan, partial payment, delinquent taxes.
  • Pasco County Clerk and Comptroller: Value Adjustment Board petitions and the Official Records.

Due dates and the installment plan

Pasco follows the usual Florida rhythm: a bill in November, discounts through February and delinquency on April 1. The details below come from the collector.

Owners whose estimated tax tops one hundred dollars can use an installment plan. For tax year 2027, forms open November 1, 2026 and the filing cutoff is April 30, 2027; no applications are taken from May 1 through October 31. The first payment has to arrive by July 31 or you drop out of the plan. Each parcel needs its own application, and renewal after that is automatic.

The collector's menu also lists a partial payment application. Before delinquency, state law leaves partial payments to the collector's discretion, so call before you send less than the whole bill.

Installment schedule
PaymentMonth dueDiscount
FirstJune6 percent
SecondSeptember4.5 percent
ThirdDecember3 percent
FourthMarchNone

Homestead exemption

File once with the Property Appraiser by March 1 and the taxable value of your primary home goes down. The Tax Collector does not handle homestead filings. The appraiser accepts applications all year but applies the March 1 cutoff.

The appraiser's exemptions menu is sorted into six groups: Homestead, Disability, Military and First Responders, Agriculture, Parent and Grandparent, and Senior Aged 65 and older. Under state rules the base homestead benefit is up to $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to school taxes, and the second $25,000 reaches only value above $50,000 for non-school taxes. An added senior exemption exists for some owners if Pasco has approved it and income is under a limit, so ask the appraiser.

A sale or deed ends the capped assessment. A change of ownership returns the parcel to market value at the next valuation date, with exceptions such as transfers between spouses. The state's 2026 Save Our Homes cap is printed at 2.7 percent.

  • File by March 1 of the year you want the benefit, with the home already your permanent residence on January 1.
  • Renting the house or moving out ends eligibility.
  • A servicemember may rent out the homestead without losing it under state law.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Other pages worth a look before listing

The collector's menu has a change of mailing address form, an electronic bill and receipt signup, instructions for printing a paid receipt and a page about tax deed sales. On the appraiser's side there is a catastrophic event page, a taxing authorities and districts list and a reporting page for possible homestead fraud.

A storm-damaged or inherited house is a common reason to sell, and those pages explain what relief exists and which districts levy on the parcel.

  • Update your mailing address with the right office before you move so notices reach you.
  • Print the paid receipt for your closing file once the tax is cleared.
  • Use the taxing districts list to see which local districts tax your parcel.

What happens when a Pasco bill goes unpaid

April 1 starts the clock with a late penalty, a lien is sold afterward, and after two years the property can go to public auction.

The penalty is 3 percent of the tax, followed by advertising charges. By the first of June a tax certificate is issued against the parcel for the tax, penalties and costs. Interest on it runs between 5 percent and 18 percent. If the tax is still unpaid after two years, the property may be sold at public auction.

On delinquent bills the collector wants a money order, cashier's check or wire, and takes cash only at its offices. A personal or business check comes back, and the delay can add interest. Escrow checks from an attorney, title company or mortgage broker are accepted.

A certificate buyer is barred by state law from contacting you to demand payment for two years after April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. A stranger calling about your lien that early is a red flag.

How tax is settled at a Pasco sale

You seldom walk a check to the collector yourself, since the closing agent deducts what the parcel owes.

Afterward, the appraiser reports ownership changes through the year. Unpaid tax produces a duplicate notice to the new owner, and delinquent tax a reminder. The owner shown on the collector's website is the owner on the certified tax roll, which is usually finished in early October.

Outside Miami-Dade the state deed tax is 70 cents per $100 of price, and each party to the deed is liable whoever agrees to pay. The clerk quotes the recording charge in its FAQ.

The buyer feels the change, too. A sale resets assessed value, so the new owner's bill can come in well above your capped one. A buyer who will live in the house files for homestead by the next March 1.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Challenging an assessment

Talk to the Property Appraiser first. If you still disagree, petition the Value Adjustment Board, which the Pasco Clerk and Comptroller staffs. A board petition carries a non-refundable $50.00 filing fee under the clerk's FAQ.

Two petitions are different: a portability petition on the DR-486PORT form costs $15.00, and a petition over a denied homestead application, deployed military exemption or tax deferral has no fee. State rules allow 25 days from the proposed-tax notice for a value petition and 30 days from a mailed denial letter for an exemption denial. The notice arrives in August, and the dates on it control.

Business equipment and rental furnishings fall under a tangible personal property return, covered on the appraiser's site. If you rent the house before selling, ask the appraiser whether one applies.

Before you put the house on the market

Look up the parcel, write down what is owed and request a payoff if anything is open. Collect your homestead paperwork and the August notice. If a tax lien or certificate is involved, ask the collector for the redemption figure on a specific closing date, because interest keeps running.

Choosing a cash sale does not remove any of these steps, but it can shorten the calendar since there is no loan approval. Either way, plan for the payoff to come out of your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

Which Pasco County office takes my tax payment?

The Pasco County Tax Collector, through five working offices and an online portal. Tax questions go to 352-521-4338, prompt 3. The Property Appraiser sets value and exemptions but takes no payments.

What does late Pasco County tax cost?

A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1, followed by advertising charges. A tax certificate is issued on or before June 1, carrying interest between 5 percent and 18 percent.

Does Pasco County offer a payment plan?

Yes, when the estimated tax tops one hundred dollars. The 2027 plan needs an application by April 30, 2027. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, and the first must arrive by July 31.

Does a Pasco homestead pass to the buyer?

No, it stays with the owner. The buyer files by March 1, and the sale moves the assessed value up to market level at the next valuation date.

Can I sell a Pasco County house with delinquent taxes?

Yes. Delinquent tax, with any certificate redemption costs, is settled from your proceeds before the deed passes. The payoff figure comes from the Tax Collector's tax department.
