content:
Polk County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Polk County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Polk County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Polk County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Polk County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Polk County houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Polk County property tax?
We buy Polk County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Reading a Polk County tax bill

Polk bills carry more lines than most. Beside county and school millage, a parcel can show fire, garbage, lighting, roadway and community district charges, and the Tax Collector keeps a public roster of who bills for what.

When you list, a buyer comparing two houses by headline value can miss those extra lines. Find out which ones follow your parcel before the first showing and jot them in your listing notes.

  • The Property Appraiser at polkflpa.gov sets value and handles exemptions.
  • The Tax Collector at polktaxes.com sends and collects the bill.
  • Each taxing body named on the bill answers questions about its own rate or assessment.

Location and housing stock

Polk sits between Orlando and Tampa along the I-4 corridor. The north is urbanizing quickly, while the land south of State Road 60 is mostly ranch and scrub. The county seat is Bartow.

That split shows up on the bill. Newer northern neighborhoods are more likely to sit inside a district built for roads, drainage or amenities. A rural southern parcel usually has fewer special charges but may rely on a well or septic system, and a buyer's inspector will look at both.

The county counts 231,135 single family parcels and 329,750 housing units, so comparable sales near you are normally easy to find. The parcel map search on the appraiser's site shows exactly which taxing areas touch your lot.

Who levies what

The Tax Collector sorts the levies into groups. If a line is unfamiliar, call the body that charges it.

Levy groups on a Polk County bill
Billing groupCharges in that group
Board of County Commissioners, ad valoremGeneral revenue, environmental land acquisition, library MSTU, parks MSTU, stormwater MSTU
County assessments and liensFire services, garbage collection and landfill, lighting district, code enforcement lien, roadway improvement MSBUs
School BoardGeneral revenue fund, local capital fund
Other assessing bodiesCommunity development districts, water control districts, a water authority, PACE programs

Ad valorem items rise and fall with assessed value. Assessments follow a service, a district or a lien, so they can hold steady even when your value drops.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Community development district charges

A CDD adds a yearly assessment that the next owner inherits, so disclose it. The roster includes Lake Ashton, Silverlake, Poinciana, Eagle Hammock, Towne Park and Westside Haines City, plus Haines City Water Control, West Lakeland Water Control and the Tohopekaliga Water Authority.

If your subdivision is among them, your bill probably has a non-ad valorem line that stays put when home value falls. Buyers and their lenders count it toward monthly cost.

  1. Find the district name on your bill or in the Tax Collector's parcel search.
  2. Ask the district manager for the current assessment and any remaining balance.
  3. Give that figure to the closing agent so the payoff or proration comes out right.

PACE programs sit on the same roster. A PACE assessment stays with the property, so if you used one, get the balance in writing before you accept an offer.

Homestead and other exemptions

Homestead is the big one. You need to live in the home as your permanent residence on January 1 and apply by early March. It removes up to $50,000 from the taxable base, and filing costs nothing.

  • Senior exemption: owners 65 and older under the household income limit, with Polk granting the larger amount.
  • Long-time resident exemption: 25 years in the home and a just value under $250,000, applied to county general millage.
  • $5,000 reductions for widows or widowers, disability and service-connected disability.
  • Total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions for eligible owners.

Once approved, exemptions renew by themselves each year, and you hear by mail only if one is denied. If you are moving to another Florida home, the portability form lets you carry assessment savings forward, up to $500,000.

Installment plans and deferral

The Tax Collector runs two programs for owners who can't pay in one lump. Both have hard paperwork dates, so decide long before a sale.

The installment plan needs an application by April 30 of that tax year, and the prior bill must have topped $100. After you enroll, the office re-enrolls you automatically. If the house sells mid-plan, ask the collector how the remaining payments pass to the buyer.

Homestead deferral is built for owners whose income is low relative to the bill. Household income under $10,000 allows deferral of everything. Taxes above 5% of income can be deferred beyond that share, owners 65 and older can defer beyond 3%, and older owners under the additional exemption income limit may defer the whole amount. Deferral is barred if deferred amounts and liens exceed 85% of just value or the primary mortgage exceeds 70% of just value. Form DR-570 goes to the collector by the end of March after the assessment year.

Deferred taxes pile up as a lien, so plan on them being paid from your proceeds at closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If a deadline is missed

Delinquency starts April 1, and a certificate sale of unpaid parcels happens by June 1. Bidding opens at 18% interest and goes downward, and redeeming costs at least a 5% charge.

A certificate is an investor's lien, not a change of title. The holder can apply for a tax deed two years after the April 1 that followed issue, and the Clerk of the Courts runs the auction. Until then the record owner can pay all taxes, interest, fees and costs and keep the property.

If you plan to sell with taxes owed, ask the collector for a written payoff before you list. The figure keeps growing, so request a fresh one close to the closing date.

What changes for the buyer

The county reassesses the parcel at just value on the next New Year's Day, so the buyer's first bill can run well above yours. Transfers between spouses are among the exceptions. Your homestead cap doesn't travel with the house.

Deed stamps in Polk are the statewide 70 cents per $100, and the state holds every signer of the deed responsible no matter who the contract names as payer. The clerk collects the tax at recording. Homestead assessment growth is capped at 2.7% for 2026 and was 2.9% for 2025.

TRIM notices arrive in August and final rates come in the fall, so the closing agent prorates the year with the best numbers available. If rates change afterward, the contract language decides who covers the gap.

Preparing to sell

A few ordinary steps keep a sale on track. Pull your latest bill and note every line. Ask the title company or closing agent for a payoff of anything owed. Gather any exemption approval letters, district assessment statements and loan payoff details. Tell prospective buyers early about recurring assessments.

A cash sale skips lender appraisals and most financing delays, but the tax payoff, proration and deed taxes still get settled at closing, so the same paperwork applies.

Frequently asked questions

When is Polk County property tax billed?

Bills go out in November for the current calendar year, after rates are set that autumn. The early-payment discount runs 4% in November, stepping down to 1% in February.

When do Polk County taxes go delinquent?

April 1. A certificate sale of unpaid parcels follows by June 1, and the Tax Collector adds interest and an advertising charge to delinquent accounts.

Can I defer Polk County homestead taxes?

Possibly. Send Form DR-570 to the Tax Collector before the end of March in the year after assessment. Eligibility depends on household income, age and how much debt and liens already sit against the home.

Do I reapply for Polk homestead every year?

No. Once approved it renews on its own, and only a denial is mailed. File again if you buy a different Polk home or the property's use changes.

What is a CDD charge on my bill?

It's an assessment from a community development district that financed local infrastructure. It appears as a non-ad valorem item, stays with the parcel after a sale, and should be confirmed with the district before closing.

Brevard County in brief

Brevard runs 72 miles along the central Florida east coast and has roughly 600,000 residents in 16 municipalities. Kennedy Space Center and Patrick Space Force Base are the two big demand drivers. A seller in Titusville, Melbourne, Palm Bay or a small beachside city deals with very different local governments, yet the tax bill runs on county rails wherever the house sits.

Permits depend on the address, while tax billing does not. On unincorporated land the county issues building permits, reviews plans and enforces code. Inside a city, the city does most of that. Before a pre-sale repair, confirm which jurisdiction issues the permit, since the mailing address on the tax bill can name a city different from the one that governs the lot.

The appraiser's office sets value, and the collector's office sends bills and takes the money. Nobody at the county's other offices sets your assessed value.

The tax collector's calendar

The collector publishes a calendar by month, and discounts run on the postmark. These are the entries a seller is most likely to need.

MonthWhat happens
NovemberCollection starts, 4% discount through November 30
December3% discount, third installment due December 31
January, February2% then 1% discount
MarchFull amount due March 31, fourth installment, last day for homestead tax deferral filing
AprilUnpaid taxes delinquent April 1, installment applications for next year accepted until May 1
MayDelinquent list advertised weekly for three weeks, cost added to the bill
JuneCertificate sale starts by June 1; first installment due June 30
SeptemberSecond installment due September 30

Quarterly installment plan

The plan is open when estimated tax is above $100. It splits the year into four payments, due by June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, and the application, Form DR-534, is due before May 1.

The June and September payments are figured from last year's gross tax. Changes from new value or exemptions are folded into the December and March payments once the roll is certified. After you enroll and stay current, you do not reapply each year, as long as the first payment arrives by June 30. If it has not arrived by July 31, participation is cancelled.

Anyone with a mortgage escrow account should skip installments, because the lender pays in November to capture the largest discount. Questions go to (321) 264-6969, and the form goes to the collector at P.O. Box 2500, Titusville, FL 32781-2500. Whatever is unpaid on April 1 follows the normal delinquency rules.

Payment methods and fees

Standard bills are mailed by November 1, and the collector asks owners to call if nothing has arrived by the second week of November. Installment payers get bills quarterly, in June, September, December and March. A duplicate can be mailed on request.

  • E-checks made online are free, and a payment sent in error can be reversed by calling before 5:00 pm that day.
  • Credit and debit cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay carry a 2.75 percent fee with a $2.75 minimum. International cards are 3.95 percent. A third-party vendor keeps the fee.
  • A returned check draws a service charge under s. 68.065: $25 under $50, $30 from $50 to $299.99, $40 from $300 to $799.99, and 5 percent at $800 or more.
  • Wire payments must name the tax account number, the owner and the property ID, and cover all bank fees.

A current mailing address on file protects against ownership problems, which matters most for an owner who has already moved out.

When a bill goes unpaid

In May the late list for real estate is printed in a local paper on three consecutive weeks, and the ad cost plus an electronic fee land on the owner's balance. Certificates go up for sale as early as June 1 or soon after. Late business property gets one May listing, and warrants follow July 1.

A holder who has waited out the statutory period may then apply for a deed under s. 197.502. On a homestead, the opening bid includes half of the last assessed value, and a homestead balance under $250 is issued to the county, never auctioned.

Can the sale close while tax is unpaid?

Yes. Back taxes will not block a closing. The title agent still needs the collector's payoff and any certificate costs, so request them early. A sold certificate has to be redeemed at the table.

A deed to the buyer also resets the parcel to just value on January 1, which ends the homestead growth limit, so the buyer's first bill can sit far above yours. If you are moving to another Florida house, ask about portability and Form DR-501T.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Value disputes and exemption questions

Start with the Brevard County Property Appraiser at (321) 264-6700. If the record misstates something simple, such as the bedroom count, a phone call may settle it. Formal petitions use the DR-486 forms and are filed with the clerk within 25 days of the August notice, or 30 days after an exemption denial letter.

Homestead applications are due March 1. Amendment 3, a homestead exemption ballot item, may change exemption amounts, so check the appraiser's site before you quote a buyer next year's taxes.

Relief programs for older or military-connected owners

Several programs depend on local adoption, so ask the appraiser which apply in Brevard and your city.

  • Residents 65 and older: an ordinance may add as much as $50,000 for qualifying household income.
  • Disabled ex-servicemembers: a $5,000 assessed value reduction.
  • Former servicemembers past 65 with a lasting service-related disability: a homestead discount tied to the VA percentage.
  • Homestead tax deferral: March 31 is the filing deadline.

Heirs and inherited houses

Heirs lose the exemption once the owner is gone. Call the appraiser to learn how the transfer is treated, since certain transfers at death escape the ownership reset, and pull a payoff from the collector before the sign goes up.

Gather the deed or probate paperwork, the latest tax bill and the parcel number first. Ask the title agent to run a lien search so any certificate or unpaid balance is found while there is still time to deal with it.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork worth having at closing

Bring your deed, the most recent tax bill, the collector's written payoff and any letter confirming an exemption. If you used the installment plan, bring a record of the payments made so the title agent can show what is already paid. Keep a copy of the final settlement statement with your tax records, because questions about the closing figures can come back months later.

Before you list a Brevard house

A few calls early in the process save trouble later.

  1. Phone the collector for the current balance and ask whether any installment plan, deferral or certificate is attached to the parcel.
  2. Phone the appraiser to confirm the owner name, mailing address and any exemption in your name.
  3. Check which government issues permits for the lot before any repair.
  4. Give the written figures to your title agent so they appear on the closing statement.

A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, though the payoff, the proration and the deed still need the same care.

Frequently asked questions

Which Brevard office mails the tax notice?

The tax collector mails the November bill. The property appraiser mails the proposed tax notice in August.

What is the Brevard delinquency date?

April 1. Taxes unpaid then become delinquent, and certificates are offered on or before June 1.

What is the minimum for the Brevard installment plan?

Estimated tax must exceed $100, and the application on Form DR-534 must reach the collector before May 1.

Do mortgage escrow owners use installments in Brevard?

No. Lenders pay in November to capture the discount, so installments are not for escrow accounts.

Is the Brevard discount based on postmark?

Yes. Discounts follow the postmark, with 4 percent through November 30.

Volusia County at a glance

Volusia County had 553,543 people in the 2020 census, up from 494,593 ten years earlier, and the mid-2025 estimate is 606,573. About 27.3 percent of residents are over 65. Owners live in 73.7 percent of the 241,881 households, the midpoint owner home is valued at $313,000, and builders pulled 2,826 permits in 2025. With so many older owners, the exemption categories further down matter before any sale.

How a parcel turns into a tax bill

Three hand-offs turn a parcel into a bill. The property appraiser sets value and decides exemptions. The county council, school board, city commissions and other taxing bodies choose millage, where one mill means a single dollar levied per $1,000 of value.

Once the appraiser finishes the roll and the Department of Revenue approves it, the appraiser certifies it to the tax collector, who mails each notice to the owner's last address of record. Ad valorem tax is paid in arrears: the tax year runs January 1 to December 31 and the bill arrives after it ends. You get one bill per parcel, following how the deed was recorded. The appraiser also mails a Notice of Proposed Taxes in August, listing value and hearing dates.

If your bill never arrives

Ask for it. Section 197.122 puts three duties on the owner: know that tax is due each year, find out the amount, and pay before delinquency. A lost envelope is no defense.

Annual bills leave by November 1. Call the collector if yours is not in hand by mid-month. Installment participants get quarterly statements in June, September, December and March instead. A parcel whose taxes run through a lender escrow gets an informational notice saying the original went to the escrow trustee. After a move or a sale, update the mailing address on the appraiser's records, which also hold the legal description.

Due dates, discounts and penalties

A deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next working day for walk-in payments before 5 p.m. and online payments before 11:59 p.m. Eastern.

Volusia County tax collector calendar
DateWhat happens
On or about Nov. 1Bills mailed
March 31Last penalty-free day, and the cutoff for a deferral application
April 1Delinquent, with a 3 percent minimum charge
April 30Advertising deadline and last day to apply for a new installment plan
Last business day of May, 4:30 p.m.Cutoff to pay in an office and avoid a certificate

Early-payment discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent run November through February, and March carries none. A payment postmarked after April 1 is priced by the day the office receives it.

Installment payments

The plan is open to owners whose estimated tax tops $100, with the estimate taken from last year's gross tax. Form DR-534 is available November 1 through April 30 and must reach the office at 123 W. Indiana Ave., Room 103, DeLand, before May 1.

Four quarterly statements follow. The June and September amounts rest on the prior year's tax, and any change from new value or exemptions is trued up in December and March once the roll is certified. If the first payment is made by June 30, the owner does not reapply next year. Call the office if the first notice has not arrived by June 15. Anything unpaid on April 1 is handled as a delinquent real estate tax. Mortgage borrowers should not enroll, since lenders must pay in November to earn the maximum discount.

Partial payments

You can pay part of a bill before April 1 on real and business property, with a sworn affidavit mailed along with the check. A partial payment is anything below the full amount due.

  • Installment accounts cannot use it.
  • No discount applies once an agreement with the collector exists.
  • Whatever remains unpaid on April 1 becomes delinquent and is due in full.
  • A balance open at 4:30 p.m. on the last business day of May puts a lien certificate on the parcel.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How the tax certificate sale works

The sale is held online through LienHub by June 1, and certificate information posts there in mid-May. Before it, delinquent parcels are advertised once a week for three weeks, starting at the north end of the county and working south in parcel order. The paper lists more parcels than will sell, because payments keep arriving after the list is built.

A buyer pays the gross tax, a 3 percent fee, advertising and sale costs. A winning bid cannot exceed 18 percent simple interest and pays at least 5 percent unless bid at zero. Interest begins accruing the month after issue. Unsold parcels become county held at the top rate.

To clear the lien, an owner pays the certificate amount plus the sold rate through the redemption month, and a $6.25 fee applies from June 1. Payment may be cash, guaranteed funds or a debit or credit card. A certificate lasts seven years and can be sold between investors for a $2.25 recording fee. A buyer may not press the owner for payment during the first two years, and the collector can bar one who tries.

Before a tax deed sale

After two years, a holder who wants a deed applies through LienHub, and one certificate is enough. The collector's example counts from taxes that went delinquent April 1, 2021, which allowed an application after April 1, 2023.

The applicant first pays the redemption amounts on all other certificates, any omitted or delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, and statutory fees including an application fee and a title search fee. The Clerk of the Circuit Court runs the auction itself, and the collector refers questions there. A homeowner who spots a certificate on the parcel can still redeem it with the collector before a sale takes place.

Exemptions from the property appraiser

The appraiser's exemption page names twelve groupings. Questions go to the records department at 386-736-5901.

  • Homestead, senior, disability, veteran, and widow or widower.
  • Granny flat and first responder.
  • Religious, literary, charitable and educational property.
  • Conservation, economic development and historical.
  • Agricultural classification.

Homestead is the largest. The state sets it at up to $50,000 in two layers, only the first of which touches school levies. Filing closes March 1, and you must live in the home as of January 1. The benefit belongs to one owner. After a sale, the home returns to market value the next January 1.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes due

Get the payoff in writing from the tax collector, with a figure good through closing. Because the year is paid in arrears, a closing in July leaves half the year's tax unbilled, and the contract decides who covers it.

Check the parcel's balance and any certificate on the collector's search first. The state doc stamp tax runs seventy cents per $100 of price; settle in the contract which side pays it. If a tax deed application may exist on a certificate older than two years, ask the clerk as well. A buyer paying cash can close around these items quickly, but the payoff still has to be settled at the table.

Frequently asked questions

Until what day can Volusia owners pay with no penalty?

March 31. Weekend or holiday deadlines roll forward for in person and online payments, but the 3 percent charge starts April 1.

Is there a Volusia County discount if I pay in December?

Yes, 3 percent. November pays 4 percent, January 2 percent, February 1 percent and March none.

Can I redeem a certificate on my Volusia County home by card?

Yes. The collector takes cash, cashier's or certified checks, money orders and credit or debit cards, and the owner owes the rate bid at the sale.

How soon can a Volusia County certificate become a deed application?

Two years after the delinquency date that year. The holder files online with the tax deed vendor, LienHub.

Who should I call in Volusia County about exemptions?

The property appraiser's records department at 386-736-5901. The collector handles bills, installments and deferral filings.

Sarasota County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Sarasota County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Sarasota County, FL Property Tax Guide sale

Owe Sarasota County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Sarasota County houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Sarasota County property tax?
We buy Sarasota County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

The two offices behind your bill

Two elected offices share the work. The property appraiser, based at 2001 Adams Lane in Sarasota, determines your parcel's value and who gets an exemption. The tax collector sends out the bill and receives the money. Neither office sets the rate, which each taxing body votes on for itself.

Your real estate notice is one document. It folds ad valorem tax together with non-ad valorem assessments, for example fire protection and solid waste. Business personal property gets its own ad valorem only bill. If nothing arrives by mid-November, contact the collector, who also offers a printable copy online. Counter locations are downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port and Mid County.

Related pages: Sarasota, North Port and Venice.

Payment and delinquency dates

Payment opens November 1 and the gross amount is due by March 31. April 1 is when an unpaid balance turns delinquent.

Discounts step down by month: 4 percent for November, 3 for December, 2 for January, 1 for February. Lenders that collect escrow must pay within the 4 percent month. The roll is certified in late September, and bills follow by the end of October.

Two hardship tools exist under state law. Ask the collector for an installment plan by May 1 of the assessment year. A homestead owner may instead file Form DR-570 for a deferral by March 31.

Yearly dates for Sarasota County owners
DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date and the day exemption eligibility is judged
March 1Last timely day for homestead, senior, disability and nonprofit filings
April 1Tangible personal property returns due; earlier-year tax delinquent
June 1Income papers due for the extra senior exemption
July 1Disapproval notices mailed
Mid-AugustTRIM notices mailed
First week of OctoberCertified roll goes to the collector

Contesting your value

You may talk to the appraiser first, but you can also file with the Value Adjustment Board or sue in circuit court without doing so. The three paths need not be taken in order.

A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM mailing, a date printed on your notice. After a denied exemption or denied assessment transfer you get 30 days from the letter's mailing date. The Clerk to the Value Adjustment Board answers filing questions at (941) 861-5279.

Still unhappy with the board's ruling? A circuit court claim may be filed within 60 days of roll certification. The board looks only at value, classification and exemption. If the rate bothers you, speak up at the budget hearing printed on the notice.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring to a value dispute

Paper beats opinion. Most issues end in informal talks, and what tends to help is proof such as sales comparisons and damage records. Organize it in one folder, with the strongest item on top, and bring two copies so you can leave one behind.

  • Your TRIM notice and parcel number.
  • Closing figures for similar houses sold close by.
  • Contractor estimates or photographs of storm or structural damage.
  • Residency papers if a homestead was denied.

The appraiser's phone is 941.861.8200. Hurricane damage has its own page on the appraiser's site.

From estimate to bill: the yearly calendar

The appraiser's calendar runs from June to the spring after bills go out.

  • By June 1: estimates of taxable value go to each taxing authority.
  • July 1: the appraiser certifies taxable value to each authority.
  • Within 55 days of certification: TRIM notices go out by first class mail.
  • Within 101 days of certification: each authority certifies its final millage to the appraiser and the state revenue department.
  • First week of October: the certified roll is delivered to the collector and the state.
  • March or April: the appraiser tells each authority how Value Adjustment Board decisions and corrections changed the roll.

This sequence explains why a TRIM notice lists proposed rates while the November bill carries final ones. The notice also gives budget hearing dates. Hold on to it until the bill comes, then compare the two side by side.

Exemptions that shrink a bill

Homestead leads the list. The house must be your permanent home on January 1, and applications are due March 1. Late filings still get a review.

The exemption is worth up to $50,000, and $25,000 of it reaches school taxes. Afterward the Save Our Homes cap limits yearly growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is less. The appraiser's guide adds:

  • $5,000 for a widow or widower who has not remarried.
  • $5,000 for total and permanent disability.
  • $5,000 for blindness.
  • $5,000 for a veteran rated at least 10 percent disabled.
  • For a veteran 65 or older with a permanent combat-related disability, a homestead discount equal to the VA rating percentage.

Voter-approved Amendment 3 reaches the 2027 bill and leaves the 2026 bill as issued.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Unpaid tax and certificates

Tax left unpaid is sold as a certificate, and the holder can eventually ask for a deed. The collector's own wording is blunt: nonpayment can mean losing the property.

Certificates go on sale by June 1. Bidding is on interest, lowest wins, in quarter-point steps. A deed application, carrying a $75 fee, can come two years after the April 1 of the issue year. At the clerk's sale the winner posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is more. Our tax deed page goes deeper.

If you're behind, the balance can be paid through closing. Your title agent requests the figure from the collector.

Tax at a sale

The buyer answers to the collector for the whole bill. Between buyer and seller, the closing statement credits the buyer for the months you held title, and nothing is wired to the collector as a seller part-payment.

Mailing matters afterward. Tell the appraiser where to send your notices once you move, and forward any real estate bill for a house you sold. Business equipment is different: if you owned it on January 1, that year's bill stays yours. Recording details sit in our Sarasota County records guide.

A short list for sellers

Before listing, pull the parcel record, your last bill and any exemption letters, and ask the collector for a balance that includes older years. Hand the paperwork to the title agent early so questions surface while there is still time to answer them.

On closing day, read the tax proration line on the settlement statement and keep a copy for your records. If a figure looks off, ask the agent to walk you through it before you sign. A cash buyer can close without waiting on a lender, but the same balance check and credit still apply.

After the sale, watch your mail for a few months. Forward any tax notice for the old address to the new owner or the collector, and confirm that the appraiser has the buyer's name on the parcel. Keep the closing papers for your own tax records.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When is Sarasota County property tax due?

Payment opens November 1, and the tax is delinquent after March 31. Early-pay discounts are 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February.

Where can I pay what I owe?

Use the Sarasota County Tax Collector, through its website payment options or at offices in downtown Sarasota, Venice, North Port or Mid County.

Can I appeal my value?

Yes, with a Value Adjustment Board petition filed within 25 days of the TRIM mailing. A denied exemption allows 30 days from the denial letter.

Who pays the tax bill when a house sells?

The buyer answers to the collector. The seller's months are credited to the buyer on the closing statement.

What if I can't pay in full?

Ask the collector about an installment plan, which needs an application by May 1 of the assessment year, or a homestead deferral on Form DR-570 by March 31.

Manatee County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Manatee County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is

Who sends the Manatee County tax bill?

Two offices share the work in Manatee County. Value comes from the property appraiser; billing and collection belong to the tax collector. The appraiser's TRIM notice goes out first, the collector's bill follows, and the money is then passed along to local taxing authorities.

For an exemption, a parcel record or an assessed value, contact the Manatee County Property Appraiser. For what you owe, which discount applies or whether a certificate exists, contact the Manatee County Tax Collector. The clerk of court keeps recorded deeds and liens, at manateeclerk.com.

  • Property appraiser: parcel search, homestead e-filing, tangible personal property returns, TRIM notices, value reviews and Value Adjustment Board information.
  • Tax collector: bills, payments, installment plans, delinquent accounts and the annual tax certificate sale.
  • Clerk: recorded deeds, mortgages and liens, plus tax deed sales run for the county.

Payment deadlines and discounts

Early November brings the bills, and each month cuts the discount further until the full amount falls due March 31. Collection for the 2026 roll began with a mailing on November 2.

Three things count as on time: arriving in person by 5:00 p.m., carrying a postmark, or paying online by 11:59 p.m. The 2026 discount schedule follows.

Discount periods for paying 2026 Manatee County bills in full
Payment windowDiscount
November 2 to December 34%
December 4 to December 313%
January 1 to January 312%
February 1 to February 281%
March 1 to March 31No discount, last day before delinquency

Can Manatee County owners pay in installments?

Yes, under section 197.222 of the Florida Statutes, which has the collector offer four quarterly payments. Last year's taxes need to have topped $100, and applications close May 1 of the assessment year.

How the four payments step down:

  • June 30, first installment: 6% discount. Paid by July 31, it earns no discount.
  • September 30, second installment: 4.5% discount.
  • December 31, third installment: 3% discount.
  • March 31, fourth installment: no discount, and the last day before delinquency.

Selling in the middle of a plan year? Let the collector know, because the closing payoff must cover what is left.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your the middle of a plan year house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Email reminders from the tax collector

Free email alerts from the collector tell you when taxes are due, a payment posts, a discount period is ending and taxes go delinquent. A tutorial on its site explains signup, and a separate management page lets you change or delete alerts.

A seller can use these during a listing: an alert confirms that your payment posted before the closing agent orders a payoff. The collector's help center also has checklists and answers for an office visit, and appointments are listed on its website.

With an escrowed loan, confirm with the servicer who is paying, since a lender payment and an owner payment can overlap.

What happens if Manatee County taxes go unpaid?

A balance left after March 31 turns delinquent April 1 and may gather fees, interest and collection costs. Afterward, a payment counts only if it arrives by the month's last business day; the postmark no longer helps.

By June 1 certificates are sold on unpaid items. Manatee holds a single sale a year and issues a certificate for each parcel still open; paying the taxes cancels it. Unsold certificates default to the county, where investors can buy them later from its list.

A certificate is only a lien. Section 197.502 lets a holder ask for a tax deed after two years, and the collector then identifies the owner, lienholders and any contract-for-deed buyer to be notified. Homestead parcels open at a higher bid, since half the latest assessed value is added.

Exemptions that lower a Manatee County bill

The property appraiser takes applications, and its website supports electronic homestead filing. On paper the form is DR-501, with the first state deadline in early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off taxable value. Only the first $25,000 reduces school taxes.
  • A homesteaded home's assessed value can rise only so fast under a state cap, which is 2.7% for 2026.
  • Investment and second-home parcels face a different ceiling of 10 percent a year.
  • Portability moves a long-time homesteader's cap savings to a new home, filed on Form DR-501T.
  • Homestead tax deferral goes through the tax collector, on Form DR-570, for owners who qualify.

Homestead stops when the home is rented or you move. A confidential form at the appraiser's office takes reports of suspected exemption fraud.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy the middle of a plan year houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Disputing a Manatee County value

The August TRIM notice is the starting point. On the appraiser's homepage, an owner who thinks a value is wrong can request a review of the property data and assessed value, and a link leads to the Value Adjustment Board page for a formal hearing.

Formal petitions go through the clerk, on one of the DR-486 forms, and are due 25 days after the notice date. If an exemption is denied, a separate 30 days applies. Both periods run from mailing dates printed on your paper, so read it as soon as it comes.

Business owners with tangible personal property report to the appraiser each year by April 1 and can request a 30-day extension from the same office.

The tax bill at a sale

An unpaid bill seldom blocks a sale. Funds from the buyer can settle it at closing, and the title company orders the payoff. The collector reports the account standing and any certificate, and a certificate is a title issue best handled early.

The state deed stamp rate is 70 cents for each $100 of price, collected by the clerk as the deed is recorded. A cash sale shortens the timeline because no lender appraisal or underwriting has to finish first, and it leaves the tax items just as they were.

If the parcel already has back taxes or a deed application, get the figure from the collector in writing before the closing date is set.

Before the contract is signed, a few steps keep surprises away from the closing table.

  1. Ask the collector for the account standing.
  2. Give the closing agent any installment history.
  3. Check the settlement statement's tax line against the collector's number.

Will the next owner pay the same tax?

Probably not. Your capped assessment ends with the sale, and the parcel moves to full market-based value the next January. A buyer who budgets from the old bill can be surprised.

If you are the seller, mention this to buyers so their budget uses a realistic figure, and encourage them to ask the lender or title company for an estimate. The appraiser's site posts the preliminary roll, reports and earlier years' millage for anyone who wants to compare. For the rate on one address, ask the collector or appraiser, since each taxing authority sets its own.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Who answers questions about a Manatee County tax bill?

The tax collector covers bills, payments, installments and delinquent accounts. The property appraiser covers values and exemptions, and the clerk covers recorded deeds and liens.

Does Manatee County reward early payment?

Yes. For 2026 bills the discount is 4% from November 2 to December 3, 3% from December 4 to December 31, 2% in January and 1% in February. March has none.

When do Manatee County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Unpaid parcels then enter the collector's yearly certificate sale, and paying the taxes cancels a certificate.

Can a Manatee County owner list a house while tax is unpaid?

Yes. Closing can absorb what is owed. The title company orders the payoff, and the collector confirms whether a certificate exists.

When must I apply for a homestead exemption in Manatee County?

File with the property appraiser by March 1. The home must be your permanent residence on January 1, and electronic filing is available.

Who to call about a Seminole County property tax question

Three elected offices split the work. One values the property, one collects the money and one records the deed. Calling the right one first saves a few days.

  • Property Appraiser: 1101 E. 1st Street, Sanford, open weekdays 8 to 5. Call 407-665-7506 for general service or 407-665-7512 about exemptions and fraud.
  • Tax Collector: bills, installment plans, deferral requests and certificates, with payments taken in person, by mail or online.
  • Clerk of Court: deed recording and stamp tax, plus a free property fraud alert that the appraiser encourages every owner to join.

The appraiser's site offers its data free in a downloads area, updated daily in Excel, Access and several GIS formats. Special data requests need 10 business days and may cost labor time.

The Seminole County tax roll

The county has about 491,884 residents, and two in three households own their home. That leaves roughly a third renting, and a landlord who buys a house never qualifies for homestead, so a seller marketing a rental should be ready to hand over the parcel's tax history.

Seminole County roll, 2026
Roll categoryCount or value
Real property parcels181,187
Residential parcels138,250
Condo parcels16,439
Commercial parcels6,923
Apartment units45,960
Tangible personal property accounts13,489
Taxable value$60 billion
Market value$92 billion

The $32 billion spread between market and taxable value is what exemptions and caps hold back. A long-held homestead sits well under market on the roll, so a buyer starts from a different place than you do.

Homestead filing dates

Filing is split into two windows: January 1 to March 1 for the current year, then pre-filing from March 2 to December 31 for the next year. The appraiser urges early filing to avoid lines.

A fall buyer can pre-file right away, while a February buyer has very little room before the March 1 cutoff. Requests to split or combine parcels, or to record plats, wait until the current year's taxes are paid. Email the appraiser once a bill is settled so the request moves.

The November 2026 amendment

Voters approved the constitutional amendment on property taxes, and the appraiser links to an explainer. Treat the current bill as unchanged, since the roll already certified for 2026 stands, and use the explainer to plan for later years.

As a seller, just confirm which exemptions the house carries today. A larger exemption reaches a buyer only after that buyer files.

How the tax year runs

Ownership and use on January 1 fix the assessment. March 1 closes homestead and agricultural filings, April 1 closes business personal property returns, and mid-August brings the TRIM notice with a short petition window.

  • November: bills mailed, board hearings start, and the early-payment discount is at its largest.
  • February: the last month with a discount.
  • April 1: delinquency begins.

When a closing lands in a high-discount month, buyer and seller can agree in writing who keeps the savings.

What happens to Save Our Homes when the house sells

The sale ends your benefits. The buyer is assessed at market value from the next January 1, and none of your cap passes along. If you buy again in Florida, you can carry savings to the new homestead, up to $500,000, provided that home is set up within three years. The 2026 cap is 2.7 percent.

Homestead lapses when a house is rented or abandoned, so call the appraiser before turning a Seminole County house into a rental.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to appeal a value or a denied exemption

Start by asking the appraiser to review the property record. If the dispute remains, the petition deadline is printed on the August notice. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own shorter window running from the denial letter. Miss it and you wait a full cycle, which hurts when a sale is pending.

  • Read the notice for the exact deadline.
  • Collect recent sales and photos of defects.
  • Ask the title agent how a pending petition affects the closing.

The petition goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

Paperwork to gather before listing

Pull the latest bill and TRIM notice so buyers see the exemptions and caps on the parcel. Confirm whether the house had homestead on January 1 and whether any deferral or installment plan is active. Gather the deed, any lender payoff letter and open permits, and copy the TRIM notice that shows the savings you plan to port.

The appraiser also publishes a first-time Florida homebuyer guide and a Property Owner Bill of Rights. A buyer from out of state can read them to learn how homestead filing works before the first January 1 passes. Early gathering shortens the gap between contract and closing.

Deed recording and stamp tax

The state stamp rate applies. Everyone on the deed is answerable for it, so the contract should name who pays. Recording opens at a few dollars a page plus technology add-ons, and a personal representative's deed from a probated estate is not taxable.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with an unpaid tax bill

The title company can pay an open bill from your proceeds. If the bill was sold as a certificate, an investor must also be paid, and that investor must wait two years before pressing you. A homestead owing under $250 has its certificate taken by the county. Ask for a payoff before you list.

  • Payoff statement from the collector.
  • Certificate search by the title agent.
  • Confirmation of any lender escrow.

A cash buyer can skip lender underwriting and close quickly, but it does not skip these payoffs. They come out of your proceeds either way.

Exemptions and tax relief

Homestead removes up to $50,000 of taxable value in two layers, the second skipping school taxes. Seniors may qualify for more where a local ordinance applies, so ask the appraiser what Seminole has adopted. Owners with a service-connected disability may get further breaks, and deferral requests go to the tax collector by March 31.

Ask about these before you list, because an exemption you qualify for lowers this year's bill and that affects the proration at closing. Bring proof of age, residency or disability to the appraiser's office, and file by March 1 so the benefit applies to the current year. If you sell after January 1 but before filing, the exemption for that year can still be lost, so file first when you can.

Once a buyer is under contract, the title company will ask the collector for a current payoff, and the appraiser can confirm in writing which exemptions are on file. Having both documents in hand makes closing day routine and keeps the buyer from being surprised by a higher bill the following November.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Seminole County sale trigger a reassessment?

Yes. On the next January 1 the house is assessed at market value, and your caps and exemptions stay behind.

When are Seminole County tax bills mailed?

In November, from the tax collector. Proposed-tax notices come first, in mid-August.

Where is Seminole County homestead filed?

At the property appraiser's office, by March 1, on Form DR-501. The home must already be your permanent residence on January 1, and pre-filing opens March 2 for the next year.

How long is the Seminole County appeal window?

You get 25 days from the August notice. The petition, on a DR-486 form, goes through the clerk to the Value Adjustment Board.

Who pays stamp tax on a Seminole County sale?

Every party to the deed is liable under the law, so the sale contract should name who pays. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, handled by the clerk at recording.

Quarterly installments in Marion County

Owners can enroll if they file Form DR534 before May 1 of the year they join and the prior year's bill topped $100. Once enrolled, there is no yearly reapplying, with one catch: miss the first installment and the account drops out, and the owner must reapply by April 30 of a later year. Four payments follow a fixed pattern, and the first two are based on last year's gross tax.

Marion County installment schedule
PaymentDueAmountDiscount
FirstJune 30One quarter of last year's gross tax6%
SecondSeptember 30One quarter of last year's gross tax4.5%
ThirdDecember 31One quarter of this year's adjusted tax3%
FourthMarch 31One quarter of this year's adjusted taxNone

A first payment can still be made by July 31, though without the discount. After July 31 the account returns to ordinary annual billing.

The alternative is one lump sum. Paying in November earns 4%, and the discount falls a point a month to 1% in February. Quarterly payers collect bigger percentages on early installments but spread payment over the whole year, so the plan suits owners who prefer steady cash flow to one large bill. If you plan to list soon, remember that the discounted amounts follow last year's bill, which can differ from what the new roll produces.

What happens to the plan when the house sells?

The plan belongs to the tax year, not the seller. If the property changes hands after one or more quarterly payments, the new owner must stay on the plan for that year.

A half-paid plan therefore travels with the house. The buyer takes on the remaining quarters, and your title company needs to know which ones were paid. Ask the collector for a payment history and give copies to both sides.

  • Put the plan details in the disclosure packet so nobody discovers them at the closing table.
  • Check that the settlement statement credits installments you already covered.
  • A buyer who prefers one annual bill should ask the collector whether the account can revert.

Where to go in person

The Tax Collector keeps offices around the county, open Monday to Friday from eight to four. Tax deed and certificate questions go only to the main branch, which matters if your parcel carries an old balance.

  • Main office, McPherson Complex, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala.
  • Dunnellon, inside the Rainbow Springs Government Complex.
  • Belleview, in the Belleview Regional Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Forest, at Forest Center on State Road 40 in Silver Springs.
  • State Road 200, at Jasmine Square in Ocala.
  • North, at Ocala Springs Shopping Center on U.S. 441.
  • Summerfield, at Spruce Creek Terrace Shops.
  • Ocala Annex, which serves driver license customers only.

Midweek visits between 9:30 and 10:30 in the morning are the quietest; Mondays, Fridays and month-end days run busiest. The shared number is (352) 368-8200.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Which Marion offices handle value, billing and records?

Three offices touch a sale, and each owns a different question. All are in Ocala but keep separate websites and search tools.

The Property Appraiser at 501 SE 25th Avenue sets value and processes exemptions, taking walk-ins or booked appointments. The Tax Collector issues and collects the bill. The Clerk of Court and Comptroller records deeds, hosts the Value Adjustment Board filings and conducts deed sales.

The statewide calendar sits over all three: January 1 fixes ownership and condition, March 1 closes exemption filings, April 1 is the tangible personal property deadline, and the proposed-tax notice lands in August. The collector's payment page gives November 1 as the due date.

Tourist Development Tax on vacation rentals

Rentals of six months or less owe a 4% Tourist Development Tax, collected from the guest and passed to the Tax Collector. Marion County has no contract with platforms such as Airbnb or VRBO, so the owner has to register, collect and remit directly.

State sales tax in Marion County is 7.5%, made up of 6% plus a 1.5% infrastructure surtax. The tourist tax applies to rent and to fees tied to the stay, such as cleaning and pet fees.

  • The return is due on the first of the following month and is late after the 20th.
  • Operators file every month, collections or not.
  • Late filing costs 10% of the tax for each month, with a $50 floor and a ceiling of half the tax due.
  • An owner who sells or closes the business should notify the office in writing.

Past guest stays leave a paper trail. Gather your registration number, monthly returns and proof of payment, because a careful buyer will want to see the account is current.

The appraiser's website for sellers

The site offers a tax estimator, a request form for a mortgage estimate letter, a change-of-address form and a homestead e-file page, along with a damage report page and a confidential channel for tips about suspected homestead fraud.

Run the estimator at a realistic sale price. A sale resets assessed value, so the buyer's first bill can differ sharply from yours, and lenders ask about that gap. Homestead takes up to $50,000 off the taxable base, with only the first $25,000 applying to school taxes, and the state cap that protects your own assessment ends at transfer.

After you move, file the address change. Notices follow the address on record, and a bill that never arrives still has to be paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens when Marion County taxes go unpaid?

April 1 is when routine billing turns into collection. Delinquent parcels are advertised and certificates are sold by June 1. A certificate buyer covers the bill and earns interest but cannot demand money from the owner for two years.

The collector's menu offers an online tax deed application, online purchase of county-held certificates and a delinquent tax page. Homestead parcels start higher at a deed sale. Paying off a certificate sooner costs less, because interest keeps building.

Selling a Marion County house with taxes owed

You can. Back taxes are common in estate sales and in houses left empty, and buyers expect them. Get the exact balance from the collector, and the closing agent deducts it from what the buyer brings.

The state charges seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in deed stamps, paid at the clerk's recording desk. With an inherited house or several unpaid years, secure a written payoff before you accept an offer. The Clerk's Property Alert Service sends a message whenever a document is recorded under your parcel or name, which helps spot deed fraud.

  1. Request the balance in writing from the collector.
  2. Ask whether any certificate exists on the parcel.
  3. Give the payoff letter to the title company.

Keep the payoff letter and the closing receipt together in your sale file. If the figure changes before closing, ask the collector for a fresh one and pass it along right away.

Frequently asked questions

Who sends the Marion County tax bill?

The Marion County Tax Collector. The Property Appraiser sets the value but does not mail a bill, and the Clerk records deeds and handles deed sales.

What is the first Marion installment due date?

June 30, with a 6% discount on one quarter of last year's gross tax. A late first payment is allowed through July 31 without the discount.

Does the buyer keep my Marion installment plan?

Yes, for that tax year. If the property sells after payments have started, the new owner continues on the plan.

Do Marion vacation rentals pay a tax beyond sales tax?

Yes, a 4% Tourist Development Tax on rentals of six months or less. The owner pays it to the Tax Collector because no platform contract exists.

Where can I ask about a tax certificate in Marion County?

At the main Tax Collector office, 503 SE 25th Avenue, Ocala. Only the main branch handles tax deed and certificate information.

Which office does what

Billing and payment sit with the tax collector. Values and exemptions belong to the appraiser, while appeals and tax deed auctions run through the clerk's office. A call to the wrong office costs time.

The tax collector's mailing address is 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Property tax questions go to propertytax@colliertax.com or 239-252-8171. The Property Appraiser can be reached at (239) 252-8141 for value and exemption questions.

Early payment discounts and late dates

Bills are payable in November, and paying early earns a discount that shrinks monthly: 4% in November, down a point each month to 1% in February. The gross amount is due in March, and the bill goes delinquent in April.

Collier County payment months
Month paidDiscount
November4% off
December3% off
January2% off
February1% off
MarchGross amount due
AprilDelinquent

The collector doesn't accept post-dated checks. Certificate sales on unpaid items finish by June 1. Offices close on listed holidays, including Thanksgiving and the day after, and on one training day in October.

The assessment and notice cycle

The appraiser values every parcel as of each New Year's Day. In mid-August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice, the formal proposal of next year's tax.

  • August: TRIM notice arrives, listing proposed values and tax.
  • September and October: local taxing authorities hold budget hearings.
  • November: bills go out from the tax collector.

Other property faces a 10 percent yearly ceiling on assessed growth. Read the TRIM notice closely, because it starts the appeal clock.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Contesting a value

Petitions go to the Value Adjustment Board, whose clerk is the Collier County clerk and comptroller. An assessment appeal is due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice, .

Other petitions run on different clocks. The clerk's table lists these:

  • Exemption or classification denial: 30 days after the appraiser mails the denial, with all denials mailed by July 1
  • Tax deferral denial: 30 days after the tax collector mails the denial
  • Portability and change of ownership or control: 25 days after the TRIM notice

The filing fee is $50.00 per petition per parcel for most types and $15.00 for a portability petition. The board has two county commissioners, one school board member and two citizen members, and special magistrates hear the cases and recommend decisions. Late filing needs a good cause statement.

Reading your bill

The tax collector bills ad valorem tax, a tax based on worth, on real estate and on a business's tangible personal property. One mill equals a dollar of tax on each thousand dollars of taxable value, and every taxing authority sets its own rate, so the county, school district, city and special districts all appear on one bill.

Run three checks before you pay or sell:

  • Match the parcel number and legal owner on the bill to your deed.
  • Confirm the homestead exemption shows on the bill if you applied by March 1.
  • See whether any non-ad valorem charge appears, because those are assessments rather than value-based tax.

The tax collector's site links to a tax search where you can pull a notice or receipt, and a mortgage lender that pays from escrow should still be checked against that record.

Homestead and exemptions

To get homestead, the appraiser must receive your application by March 1, and you must be living in the house as your permanent home on January 1. The exemption tops out at $50,000. Its first $25,000 applies to every levy including school tax, and the second $25,000 touches only non-school levies on value beyond $50,000.

Save Our Homes lets a homestead's assessed value rise each year by 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is smaller. The state's chart prints 2.7% for 2026. After a sale the parcel goes back to full market-based value the next New Year's Day, which can make a buyer's bill very different from the seller's. Portability lets an owner bring accumulated savings along to a replacement Florida home, provided it begins inside a three-year window after the old one ended.

Renting out the home, or moving out for good, ends homestead protection. Senior owners may qualify for added local exemptions, and disabled former servicemembers have separate benefits. The appraiser can say which apply to your Naples or Marco Island address.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Deferral and installments

Both are listed on the tax collector's property tax page. To defer homestead tax, file Form DR-570 with the collector by March 31 following the assessment year. The deferral applies to the portion above 5 percent of household income.

For a permanent resident 65 or older, the deferred portion is whatever exceeds 3 percent. The installment plan under section 197.222 needs an application by the May 1 cutoff in the year of assessment. Confirm current terms with the collector, since deferred tax accrues interest and carries a lien.

Who settles the tax at a sale

Unpaid current-year tax is settled at closing, normally by the closing agent from the proceeds. Ask for a payoff figure good through your closing date, and make sure earlier years show as paid.

Taxes that stay unpaid lead the county to sell a certificate. Once two years have run from the April 1 following issue, the holder can file for a tax deed, and the clerk then runs the auction. On a homestead parcel, the opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessment. At the clerk's auction, a winning bidder pays within 24 hours, so a delinquent house can be lost quickly, and a seller with unpaid years should settle them before listing. For recording costs on your own sale, see the Collier County property records guide.

On closing day, compare the title agent's tax lines with the collector's payoff and keep the receipt.

If a bill arrives after you have sold, don't ignore it or pay it blindly. Forward it to the closing agent and confirm in writing who is responsible. Updating your mailing address with the collector after closing helps you receive any refund. A cash buyer who skips a lender may still ask for the same tax payoff proof, so have the paperwork ready before the closing date.

Tax deed and foreclosure listings

The Collier Clerk posts both a tax deeds list and a foreclosure sale list on its records search page. The tax deeds list covers properties where the tax collector sold certificates for delinquent real estate taxes.

Each certificate goes to whoever bids the lowest interest rate, moving in quarter-percent steps. Certificates nobody buys pass to the county at the maximum rate. The holder may not contact the owner for payment until two years from the first April 1 after issue. A homeowner with a small delinquency has options before then, since payment to the tax collector redeems the certificate. Ask the collector's office for a payoff early rather than waiting for a sale notice.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What date marks Collier County tax as late?

April 1. The gross amount is due in March, with discounts only from November through February.

What early-payment discounts does Collier County offer?

The discount starts at 4% in November and ends at 1% in February. After that the full gross amount applies, starting in March.

How long is the window to contest a Collier County assessment?

Petitions are due within 25 days after the appraiser mails the TRIM notice. Most petitions carry a $50.00 filing fee.

Does Collier County accept post-dated checks for property tax?

No. The tax collector doesn't accept post-dated checks for property tax bills.

What is the mailing address for Collier County tax payments?

Mail it to the Collier County Tax Collector, 3291 Tamiami Trail East, Naples, FL 34112. Questions go to 239-252-8171.

Alachua County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Three offices behind one tax bill

Three elected offices split the work. One values property and rules on exemptions, one mails and collects the bill, and one records deeds and takes the documentary stamp tax.

The Property Appraiser prepares the real estate and tangible personal property rolls, which fix ownership, mailing address, legal description and value. Your tax is the taxable value after exemptions, multiplied by the millage rate each taxing authority sets. If no bill shows up in November, call the Tax Collector at (352) 374-5236.

  • Value, ownership and exemptions: the Alachua County Property Appraiser (acpafl.org), which also offers a free Title Alert for ownership changes.
  • Bills, payment plans and deferral: the Alachua County Tax Collector.
  • Recorded deeds and doc stamps: the circuit court clerk, who also conducts foreclosure and tax deed sales.

Due dates and early payment discounts

Bills typically arrive near the first of November. The gross amount is payable through the end of March, and delinquency starts April 1. The earlier you pay, the bigger the reduction.

Early payment schedule, by postmark
Postmark monthReduction in the bill
NovemberFour percent off
DecemberThree percent off
JanuaryTwo percent off
FebruaryOne percent off
MarchFull amount, no reduction

Discounts are decided by postmark. After delinquency, April 1 adds a minimum 3 percent charge and May adds an advertising charge, with the total tied to the date the payment is received.

Millage rates on the notice

The county's 2026 TRIM explainer shows a 2025 countywide millage of 7.6000 mills and a proposed 2026 rollback rate of 7.2107 mills, which would be the tenth straight year of a lower countywide rate. Treat the 2026 number as proposed until the final rate shows up on your bill or on the Tax Collector's site.

The county is only one line on a TRIM notice. A home inside a city adds that city's levy, and in Gainesville some charges that used to ride on monthly utility bills now appear on the notice. Owners in unincorporated areas may also see a Law Enforcement Municipal Services Taxing Unit line, listed at a proposed 3.5678 mills. Non-ad valorem items such as county fire, solid waste and stormwater are charged by assessment instead of millage.

Homestead and other exemptions

File with the county appraiser by March 1. To qualify, the house has to be where you lived permanently as of the January 1 before.

The homestead exemption is worth up to $50,000 in taxable value. School taxes only see the first $25,000. The second $25,000 lowers the non-school levies, and only on value above $50,000.

Once you hold homestead, Save Our Homes limits how fast assessed value can rise: 3 percent a year or the CPI change, whichever is smaller. The state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026. That protection ends with a sale or foreclosure, when value resets to just value the next January. Spousal transfers are among the exceptions.

If you are buying another Florida home, portability can carry the accumulated savings to it, provided the new homestead is set up within three years of giving up the old one. Disabled ex-servicemembers, deployed servicemembers and seniors may have additional relief, and a city or county ordinance sets the senior exemption.

Homestead stops when you rent the house out. Moved already? Ask the Property Appraiser where your status stands before you list.

Installments and homestead deferral

Two options exist for spreading a bill out or postponing it, each with separate rules: a quarterly installment plan and a homestead tax deferral, both run through the Tax Collector.

The installment plan needs prior year taxes above $100, with applications closing April 30. Discounts are 6 percent on the June 30 payment, 4.5 percent on September 30, 3 percent on December 31, and nothing on March 31.

Deferral is open to a homestead property whose primary mortgage stays within 70 percent of assessed value, with the form due at the end of March. Interest on the deferred amount accrues at up to 7 percent a year. The balance becomes payable all at once if eligibility, use or ownership changes, so selling the house means paying it off at closing.

Landlords and tangible personal property tax

Owning a rental means two taxes: the real estate bill, and tangible personal property tax on whatever furniture, fixtures and equipment are inside.

Tangible property is valued as of January 1. File a return by April 1 and you earn an exemption of up to $25,000. File late, or not at all, and you owe penalties and lose it. Unpaid tangible tax goes delinquent on April 1 with a $10 fee and interest at 1.5 percent a month, and May 1 adds a 20 percent collection fee.

That lien stays attached to the property through a sale, so buyer and seller prorate it at closing. A vacant residential rental may qualify for assessment discounts, and the county's waste collection office, 352-338-3233, can explain.

What happens when taxes go unpaid

After advertising the delinquent parcels, the Tax Collector holds an online certificate sale on lienhub.com by early June. The auction begins at an 18 percent interest rate, and bidders go lower.

Whoever wins pays your tax and earns interest, and the certificate sits first in line against the property. Two or more years after delinquency, its holder can apply for a tax deed, and a parcel nobody redeems is auctioned publicly. You clear a certificate by paying the Tax Collector the tax, interest, costs and charges.

For two years after April 1 of the issue year, Florida law bars the holder from asking the owner for money. If the house carries a certificate, the payoff can usually come out of sale proceeds, and the Tax Collector's office will quote the figure.

Taxes at the closing table

The county had 290,028 residents in July 2025. Owners live in 54.1 percent of homes, which signals a big renter base, and the median home value is $288,800. College-town turnover makes title work worth starting early, so order a tax and lien search from your title company the moment a contract is signed.

Whoever is on the roll receives the bill, and the two sides divide the year at closing. A documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration, outside Miami-Dade, is paid to the clerk as the deed is recorded. All parties on the deed share liability for it, regardless of what the contract says. With a mortgage that escrows taxes, the lender receives the bill and has to pay inside the 4 percent window.

Steps before you list

A short routine keeps tax surprises off the settlement statement.

  1. Open your parcel record at the Property Appraiser and check the owner name, mailing address and any exemptions.
  2. Call the Tax Collector and ask whether this year is paid, what is owed, and whether a certificate or installment plan exists.
  3. With a deferral on the property, get the payoff in advance, since the full balance is due on sale.
  4. Give the figures to your title company for the closing statement.

Selling a rental? Add the tangible personal property return to the list. That lien stays with the property after closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When does Alachua County mail property tax bills?

Around the start of November. If yours does not arrive, call the Tax Collector at (352) 374-5236.

How long can I wait before Alachua County taxes go delinquent?

Pay by the end of March. After that, a 3 percent minimum charge applies from April 1.

Is the 2026 Alachua County millage final?

The county's explainer shows 7.2107 mills as the proposed 2026 rollback rate, against 7.6000 in 2025. Confirm the final rate with the Tax Collector or on your bill.

Does selling my Alachua County home end my homestead?

A sale counts as a change of ownership, so assessed value returns to just value the next January. The new owner files a fresh homestead application.

Can an Alachua County owner with unpaid tax still sell?

Yes. The title company can pay delinquent tax and any certificate out of the buyer's funds. Ask the Tax Collector for the payoff amount before the closing date.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.
