Who handles what on a Bay County bill

Different offices own value and collection. The Bay County Property Appraiser sets value and decides exemptions. Local governments set millage rates. The Bay County Tax Collector prints the bill, mails it and takes payment.

In order, the appraiser assesses, the County Commission and other taxing bodies set millage, the appraiser compiles the roll, and the certified roll passes to the Tax Collector. A change to name, mailing address, location or assessed value has to go through the Property Appraiser. When a mortgage company pays through escrow, it asks for the original bill and you are sent a copy.

  • Property Appraiser: value and TRIM notice questions, (850) 248-8401.
  • Tax Collector: payment, delinquent tax and tax deferral.
  • Clerk of Court and Comptroller: official records, plus clerk work for the Value Adjustment Board.

The tax calendar through the year

Each step of the Bay County year belongs to a different office, and the dates follow the state calendar.

  • January 1 fixes value and ownership for the tax year.
  • March 1 is the last day to file exemption and classification applications.
  • In August the Property Appraiser mails the TRIM notice of proposed taxes, and a challenge to value must reach the court clerk within 25 days.
  • September and October bring tentative budget hearings, with final budget and millage hearings in October and November.
  • The Tax Collector sends the bill in November.
  • April 1 makes unpaid tax delinquent, and certificates sell by June 1.

A spring listing may close while last year's bill is still open and the new roll is under construction.

Tax Collector offices

There are four service offices, and a Bay County bill can only be paid at these offices or online.

  • Panama City: 850 W. 11th St., Panama City, FL 32401.
  • Panama City Beach: 10520 Hutchison Blvd., Panama City Beach, FL 32407.
  • Lynn Haven: 700 Florida Ave., Lynn Haven, FL 32444.
  • Callaway: 805 S. Tyndall Pkwy, Callaway, FL 32404.

Bring the property tax notice or the property address. Delinquent balances must be paid in certified funds: cash, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. You can book an appointment through the Tax Collector's site, and online payment is available too.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What a Bay County seller does before listing

Begin with the tax notice and the Property Appraiser's record for the parcel, and check the owner name against the deed. A mismatched name or an old mailing address can keep the bill from ever reaching you, and only the Property Appraiser can correct either one.

Next, look for non-ad valorem charges for paving, stormwater or solid waste. They are billed beside the tax and owed at closing like the rest. A house that sat vacant, or was repaired after storm damage, may carry an assessed value that no longer fits its condition. Read the TRIM notice in August instead of waiting for the bill.

Last, ask the title company for a lien and tax search. Panama City, Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway all sit in the same county tax system, so the same offices answer for any of them.

Due dates and early payment discounts

Expect your bill in the mail by November 1. March 31 is the deadline, and delinquency starts April 1. The discount months are November through February.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent off.
  • January: 2 percent off.
  • February: 1 percent off.

Paving, stormwater and solid waste assessments, the non-ad valorem items, share this calendar and the same early discounts. They are levied by local governments and certified to the Tax Collector, so direct a question about one to the government behind it.

Filing for homestead and other exemptions

March 1 is the cutoff for applying with the Bay County Property Appraiser, and you need to have been living in the house as your permanent home by January 1. Exemptions never go through the Tax Collector's window.

Homestead can take as much as $50,000 off taxable value. Schools get only the first $25,000 of that benefit. The second $25,000 works against non-school levies, and applies to value over $50,000.

After you qualify, assessed value can climb no faster than 3 percent or CPI each year, whichever is lower. That is the Save Our Homes cap, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. A sale or foreclosure wipes the cap out and resets value to just value the next January. Renting the house out ends homestead altogether, though servicemembers get a limited carve-out.

When a homestead application was filed on time and still denied, there is no petition fee. A late application, received after March 1, does carry one.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to dispute a Bay County valuation

The route is a petition to the Bay County Value Adjustment Board. Petitions are due 25 days after the TRIM notice goes out in August, so call the Property Appraiser for the exact date each year. A late petition is treated as late filed and reviewed.

Value Adjustment Board filing details
Filing detailAmount or address
Filing fee$50.00, non-refundable
Online filingAdds a 3.5% non-refundable card processing fee
Each extra contiguous parcel or account$5.00 after the first
Mail address for checks225 McKenzie Avenue, Panama City, FL 32401

Section 194.014 requires a petitioner contesting value to pay all non-ad valorem assessments and at least 75 percent of the ad valorem taxes, less the discount, before the taxes go delinquent. If that partial payment is missed, the board must deny the petition by April 20.

If you cannot pay the bill

Two relief tools exist. The first is the homestead tax deferral on Form DR-570, filed with the Tax Collector by March 31, which covers tax over 5 percent of household income, or over 3 percent for a permanent resident aged 65 or older. The second is an installment plan under section 197.222, applied for by May 1 of the assessment year. Ask the Bay County Tax Collector which plans it runs and what the payoff would be.

Ignore the bill and April 1 makes it delinquent. State law then requires a certificate sale by June 1, and two years after April 1 of the issue year the certificate holder can seek a tax deed. A seller caught in that sequence can generally settle the debt from the sale price at closing.

Tax at the sale

The bill goes to the owner of record on the roll, and at closing the year is split between buyer and seller. Ask the title company to pull the current bill, any non-ad valorem balance and the discount month in effect.

The clerk collects a documentary stamp tax on the deed at recording: 70 cents per $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade. Every person named on a taxable deed is liable for it, even if the contract puts payment on one side.

Once the next January arrives, the buyer has no inherited cap, so what you paid is a poor predictor of what they will owe. For an inherited or storm-worn house, clear liens and unpaid balances first and then record the deed in Panama City.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Paperwork to pull together

Collect these before you sign a sale agreement: the latest tax notice, your deed, the Property Appraiser's parcel record, any exemption approval letters, and a list of non-ad valorem charges on the bill. Put the title company's payoff request in writing and keep the reply. The same folder works whether you list the house or sell for cash, and it helps a buyer's attorney confirm there are no open balances before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Bay County property tax due date?

March 31 is the due date, and April 1 starts delinquency. Notices normally go out by early November.

How much is the Bay County early payment discount?

Four percent in November, shrinking by a point each month through February, with nothing off in March.

Where is the Bay County Tax Collector?

Panama City is the central location, with additional offices in Panama City Beach, Lynn Haven and Callaway. Bring your notice or property address.

When is the Bay County value petition deadline?

It falls 25 days after the TRIM notice is mailed in August, and a late petition is treated as late filed and reviewed. Questions go to the Property Appraiser at (850) 248-8401.

Does a Bay County buyer keep my Save Our Homes cap?

No. Ownership changes reset the property to just value the following January, with narrow exceptions such as some spousal transfers.

Charlotte County tax basics

One combined notice arrives each year from the county tax collector, built on values the property appraiser set. Charlotte County collects in arrears, so a November bill pays for the calendar year that is nearly over.

The notice has two kinds of charge. Ad valorem tax rises and falls with value. Non-ad valorem assessments follow things like square footage or the number of units, and the collector names stormwater, fire and rescue and solid waste as examples. County commissioners, the School Board, city commissioners and other authorities set millage, and the appraiser does not.

The county had about 217,212 residents in 2025, and 83.8% of its 131,960 housing units have owner occupants. Median home value is $328,900. Because 87.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, many carry capped assessments, while a buyer starts from the reset value.

Which office handles what

Each office has its own lane: the appraiser sets value and approves exemptions, the collector issues and takes payment on the bill, and the clerk runs tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values, exemptions and homestead applications, phone (941) 743-1593 for exemption questions on a notice and (941) 743-1498 for assessed value questions.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment plans and delinquent taxes, phone (941) 743-1350.
  • Clerk's office: online tax deed sales, phone (941) 637-2130.

Installment applications go by mail to the collector at 18500 Murdock Circle, Port Charlotte, FL 33948. If you sold the house, send any bill that reaches you on to the buyer or return it to the collector.

Billing dates and discounts

Statements are mailed by the first of November. Pay early and you get a discount that begins at 4% and drops a point each month.

Charlotte County billing and collection steps
StepTiming or amount
Statements mailedBy November 1
Early paymentFour points off in the first month, then one fewer each month through February
DelinquentApril 1, with 3% interest plus advertising costs
Installment eligibilityEstimated tax over $100
Installment paymentsJune 30 (6% off), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%), March 31 (none)
Certificate saleBy June 1, bidding down from 18%

When an escrow account pays the tax, the mortgage company should request the bill and the owner gets a copy for information.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

The installment plan

Send the application to the collector before May 1. Your first payment is then due by June 30.

Skip the first payment and the plan is cancelled, which leaves the whole tax due by March 31. Once you make that payment, you are in for the year and enrollment renews on its own. To leave, ignore the June bill and wait for the November notice at the gross amount. Anything unpaid on April 1 is treated as a delinquent bill.

Installments one and two are each a quarter of the estimate. Numbers three and four add half of any true-up each, so the last two bills can differ from the first two.

When taxes go unpaid

Real estate tax left unpaid turns delinquent April 1 and heads to a certificate sale by early June.

The collector advertises delinquent parcels in a local paper weekly for three weeks, and advertising and collection fees land on the delinquent account. The sale is a reverse auction on the interest rate starting at 18%, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate, a first lien. Each certificate stays valid for seven years. Two years after the delinquency date, the holder may ask for a tax deed, and the clerk runs that sale online.

  • Delinquent taxes are accepted only by cashier's check, money order or cash.
  • A deed sale opens at a total that includes a $75.00 collector fee, a $150.00 ownership and encumbrance report, a $60.00 clerk fee and a $59.00 web fee, plus taxes, interest and half the assessed value.
  • Paying all taxes, costs and interest before the deed is issued stops the sale.

Homestead exemption

The county appraiser takes homestead applications until March 1 of the year you want the benefit, and you must live there as a permanent resident by New Year's Day.

Florida lets you remove up to $50,000 from taxable value. School levies reduce by the first $25,000 only, while the other $25,000 hits non-school levies on value over $50,000. Once you are in, the assessed value can climb no faster than 3 percent or CPI, and the state's chart lists a 2.7 percent cap for 2026. A sale resets the figure to full just value the following January 1.

Renting the home out ends homestead, except for the servicemember rule in the statutes. Older owners and military service members may qualify for extra benefits, and the appraiser's office rules on each case.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other charges the collector handles

The collector also bills tangible personal property tax, which falls on the furniture and equipment of a business or rental property and on structural additions to mobile homes. These bills go out with the real estate bills and earn the same early discounts.

On April 1 tangible tax goes delinquent and picks up 1.5% interest, a $2.00 late fee and advertising costs. Warrants are issued before April 30 on unpaid accounts, and within 30 days the office applies to the circuit court for an order allowing levy and seizure.

  • A $6.25 redemption fee applies when a certificate is redeemed on or after June 1.
  • Paper bills can be swapped for email bills through the office's Bill Express sign-up, though an undeliverable bill doesn't extend a discount period.
  • Email addresses given for e-billing become public records.

Selling in Charlotte County

Your closing agent divides the year's tax between the two parties and takes anything owed, delinquent amounts included, out of the proceeds.

Call (941) 743-1350 for a payoff and ask whether a certificate was sold, since a holder has to be repaid with interest before the lien clears. The state stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 comes due when the deed is recorded, and each party to the document is liable.

A buyer of a homesteaded house won't inherit the seller's exemption or capped value. Ask both offices for figures on your parcel.

A short list for sellers

Request a written payoff from the collector before you accept an offer. Hand a copy to the title agent and, if you owe back taxes, ask how the certificate holder gets repaid. Check that any installment plan is settled or assigned in the contract. After closing, keep the settlement statement and the paid receipt. A cash sale skips the lender's underwriting, but the tax payoff is the same step either way.

If the sale falls through, you still owe the year's tax, so keep paying on schedule until a new closing date is firm. Send the collector your forwarding address as soon as you move, so notices find you. If you hold an installment plan, confirm in writing who takes over the next payment, and ask the title agent to note it on the settlement statement. Small paperwork habits like these prevent most disputes after a sale.

Frequently asked questions

Which office mails the Charlotte County bill?

The Charlotte County Tax Collector mails it on or before November 1, using the roll certified by the property appraiser. Call (941) 743-1350 with billing questions.

What is the early payment discount in Charlotte County?

Four percent off in November, falling one point each month to 1% in February. March brings none, and delinquency starts April 1.

Can Charlotte County taxes be paid in installments?

Yes, when the estimate exceeds $100 and the application is in before May 1. Four payments follow, ending March 31.

How long before a certificate can become a tax deed application?

Two years after the tax went delinquent. A certificate lasts seven years, and redemption is possible until a deed is issued.

Where does a Charlotte County homestead application go?

To the county appraiser, by March 1. That office decides eligibility, and the collector only bills.

Citrus County at a glance

The 2025 population estimate is 171,666, up 11.6% from 153,843 in 2020. Owners occupy 85.2% of the 90,919 housing units, and median home value is $245,500. Seniors make up 38.1% of residents, so many owners watch their bills closely and plenty of sellers hold capped assessments.

Which office does what

The property appraiser handles valuation and exemption rulings here, while the tax collector sends the bill, takes payment and sells certificates.

  • Property appraiser: homestead and other exemption applications, portability, agricultural classification and the August TRIM notice. The office phone is (352) 341-6600.
  • Tax collector: bills, discounts, installment applications and delinquent tax advertising.
  • Clerk: files the deed at closing and collects stamp tax.

March 1 is the yearly cutoff for portability, exemptions, classifications and assessment reductions, and April 1 for tangible personal property returns. Owners who buy a home after January 1 are encouraged to pre-file for the next year.

Discounts and due dates

November's 4% discount is the largest on offer. It shrinks a point every month, and by March you pay the gross amount, which is due March 31.

Citrus County real estate tax calendar

December3% discount; third installment due December 31

Paying in installments

Quarterly payments let you split the bill into four pieces across the year. The application must reach the collector by April 30, and eligibility turns on prior year taxes above $100.

June 30 is the first due date, at 6% off, and a payment taken between July 1 and July 30 gets no discount. September 30 brings the second at 4.5% off and December 31 the third at 3% off. The fourth, due March 31, has no discount. Miss that first payment and the plan ends, leaving the full tax due by March 31.

Payments one and two follow last year's bill. Ownership, value or exemption changes show up in payments three and four. Enrollment renews itself each year. A buyer taking over an active plan should check with the office, and the contract should say who pays each remaining installment.

Unpaid taxes

A bill turns delinquent on April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount.

In May the collector prints the delinquent list in the local newspaper weekly for three weeks, and that cost lands on the bill. Sale of certificates begins by June 1. Unpaid tangible personal property carries a 1.5% penalty after April 1 and is advertised once.

Two years after a certificate is issued, its holder may apply for a tax deed. Redemption stays open until the deed issues, and a homestead parcel's opening bid includes half the assessed value. Request a payoff before listing, and keep the written figure with your closing file.

Homestead and Save Our Homes

Homestead exemption can reduce taxable value by up to $50,000 if the county appraiser has your application before the March 1 cutoff.

The first $25,000 reduces every tax, and a second $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on assessed value over $50,000. The appraiser puts typical savings at roughly $500 a year. After the first year, the assessment can't rise by more than the lesser of CPI change or 3 percent. If you moved from one Florida homestead to another within three years, you may be able to take some of your Save Our Homes savings along.

Homestead ends if the owner rents the unit or stops living there permanently, and a sale resets value to just value the next January 1. Furniture and equipment used in a rental or business is taxed separately as tangible personal property.

Relief for older and military-service owners

With seniors more than a third of the population, relief programs matter here. An ordinance can add a senior exemption of as much as $50,000 for older owners under an income cap. Ask the appraiser's office whether one applies locally.

If you are selling a homesteaded house, plan to tell the buyer plainly that the exemption and any capped value end with your ownership. The buyer should file a new application of their own before the next March 1 cutoff, and the appraiser's office can explain how. You can also remove your own exemption from the record after closing so no one wonders who still lives there. Ask your insurance agent and mortgage servicer to update their records too.

  • Deferral: send Form DR-570 to the collector by March 31. The deferral covers tax beyond 5 percent of household income, or beyond 3 percent when a permanent resident is 65 or older.
  • Disabled former servicemembers: $5,000 off assessed value at a service-connected rating of 10 percent or higher.
  • Former servicemembers past 65 with a permanent service-connected disability can receive a homestead discount matching their VA percentage.

A denied exemption can go to the value adjustment board, but the petition window is 30 days.

What changes at closing

The title company divides this year's tax between you and your buyer, and any back taxes come out of your proceeds.

The recorded deed carries Florida stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of price, and both buyer and seller stay liable. A buyer's first bill often differs from your last one. Before closing, ask for these three things.

  • A written payoff covering the current year and any earlier balance.
  • Word on whether a certificate was sold against the parcel.
  • The standing of any installment plan, which renews each year.

Steps for a Citrus County seller

Gather your latest bill, any installment notice and your homestead paperwork. Call the collector for the payoff, then give the figure to your title agent so it can be matched against the settlement statement. If taxes are behind, expect the payoff to include the penalty and advertising costs. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, which can shorten the timeline, but the tax lien still has to clear at closing.

Sequence matters. First confirm what is owed. Next decide whether to pay it before listing or let the title agent pay it from proceeds. Then check that no certificate has been sold against the parcel, because a holder must be repaid before the lien clears. Finally, ask for a copy of the paid receipt and store it with your closing papers. Bring a photo ID and your parcel number to any office visit, and ask each office to email you what it tells you in person so you have a written record. If you are leaving the area, give the collector a mailing address so a late notice doesn't get lost.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Citrus County early payment discount?

It starts at 4% for November and drops a point each month through February. Nothing comes off in March, and April 1 begins delinquency.

When is the installment application due in Citrus County?

Applications close April 30. The first payment is due June 30, and a payment in July earns no discount.

When does a Citrus County tax bill turn delinquent?

On April 1, with a 3% penalty on the gross amount. Certificates go on sale by June 1.

What is the homestead filing deadline in Citrus County?

The appraiser must have your form by March 1. The appraiser, not the collector, rules on eligibility.

Can I sell a Citrus County house that has delinquent tax?

Yes. The title company deducts whatever is owed from your sale proceeds, so get a payoff early and find out if the county sold a certificate.

Who bills and who values

Two offices split the work. One office mails the bills and collects payment. The other sets each parcel's value and decides who qualifies for an exemption.

Mailing is done by November 1. If a lender pays your tax, you receive an information-only copy. Value is set as of January 1, though payment is normally due starting November 1. Florida Statute 197.122 puts the burden on owners to find out what they owe and pay before delinquency, even when no bill arrives in the mail.

  • Property appraiser: value, homestead, portability and other exemptions, filed by March 1.
  • Tax collector: payment, installment and partial payment plans, certificate sales.
  • Clerk: records the deed and collects stamp tax.

Discounts and due dates

The discount begins at 4% in November and drops a point a month to 1% in February. March carries none, and April 1 brings delinquency.

Installments and partial payments

To use installments, apply by April 30 with estimated taxes above $100, then pay the first quarter by June 30.

The first installment carries a 6% discount. A July payment earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan. The second, due September 30, carries 4.5%. The third, due December 31, carries 3%, and the fourth, due March 31, carries none. Last year's notice drives the first two payments, and the final two absorb any change in ownership, value or exemptions.

Partial payments are a separate option under Florida Statute 197.374. The owner submits a Partial Payment Plan application with the first payment or in person, and payments can begin November 1. Online payment isn't accepted for this plan. Early payment discounts are forfeited, so the full March amount is due, and any balance left on April 1 is delinquent and goes into the June certificate sale.

When taxes go unpaid

Expect a 3% penalty on April 1, more fees from May 1, and a certificate sale by June 1.

If a certificate sits unredeemed, a tax deed application can follow two years on, with a $75 application fee. The clerk conducts the auction. The owner can pay the taxes before the deed issues and stop the sale.

Costs climb at each stage, so request a payoff before you put a house with unpaid tax on the market.

Deadlines that catch sellers

Three dates deserve attention during a listing, in winter or summer. March 1 is the exemption filing deadline for any buyer who wants homestead in the first year. March 31 is the final due date for a full bill or the fourth installment, and April 1 starts the penalty clock.

The installment plan also has a July trap. A first payment that misses June 30 but lands before July 31 earns no discount, and missing July 31 cancels the plan and returns the owner to the regular due dates and discounts. If you close in summer, find out which installments are paid so the contract divides the rest fairly.

A value petition filed with the clerk is due 25 days after the TRIM notice, and an exemption denial carries a 30 day window. Read the TRIM notice each August.

  • Application for installments: April 30.

Homestead and the Save Our Homes cap

Send Form DR-501 to the appraiser by March 1. The home has to be your permanent residence on January 1.

The exemption can be worth as much as $50,000. The first $25,000 reduces all taxes, and the added $25,000 reduces only non-school taxes on value over $50,000. After the first year, assessed value rises by no more than 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower. The published chart lists caps of 2.9 percent for 2025 and 2.7 percent for 2026. Portability allows a move to a new Florida homestead within three years, with Form DR-501T filed alongside.

Non-homestead property has a separate 10 percent annual limit on assessed value growth. A rental or second home can still see its taxable value climb every year.

Settling the tax when you sell

At closing the agent apportions the year's tax, subtracts any balance from your proceeds and sends the deed to the clerk for recording, which is when stamp tax is collected.

A deed carries a stamp tax of 70 cents on each $100 of consideration everywhere except Miami-Dade, and the state revenue agency holds all parties to the document liable no matter who agrees to pay. Confirm which tax year your payoff covers, because partial payment rules apply to the current year only.

With a lender-held escrow, find out when any refund would arrive, and check with the collector that this year's bill is settled.

A practical order of steps

Start with a written payoff from the collector, and ask whether any plan is open on the parcel. Next, tell the title agent which installments are paid so the contract can split the rest. Then check that your exemption paperwork is in order so you can explain it to the buyer. On closing day, read the settlement statement's tax lines against the collector's figure, and afterward file the paid receipt with your closing documents.

A cash buyer doesn't need a lender's approval, so closings can move fast. That makes it more useful to settle the payoff early, since there is less time to fix a surprise.

If you inherited the house, bring the paperwork that shows you may sell it, and tell the collector where to send future notices. If the property is a rental, collect your tenant's contact details so the buyer can reach them. Ask your title agent for a list of documents it needs from you well before the closing date, and gather them in one folder. Having each item in hand keeps a sale on schedule even if a tax question comes up late. Finally, save an email or letter from the collector confirming your balance, so any later question about the same year can be answered with a document and not a memory. Store it with your deed copy and closing statement.

Apply by the end of April, with an estimate above $100. The June 30 first payment gets the biggest discount.

A card adds 2.50%. Online e-check payments carry none.

By June 1, covering the prior year's delinquent real estate taxes, with extra fees from May 1.

Use Form DR-501 and send it to the appraiser by the first of March. The collector only bills.

Who values and who bills

In Escambia the appraiser sets the value and the collector sends the invoice. The Property Appraiser maintains the roll for Escambia County, the City of Pensacola and the Town of Century, and its site labels assessed values and exemptions as the 2026 certified tax roll.

The Tax Collector gathers money for the District School Board, the Board of County Commissioners, Pensacola, Century, the Sheriff, the Downtown Improvement Board and the Northwest Florida Water Management District, plus several state agencies. You can look up a bill by name, address or account number, and the site offers paperless e-billing and tax reports.

Millage by area

The street address decides your total, because the Tax Collector prints a separate stack of levies for each part of the county. One mill is a tenth of a cent per dollar of taxable value.

2026 millage by area

The school line has two parts: 2.2480 set by the local board and 3.1060 set by state law. Only the unincorporated column carries a Sheriff line, so a house outside city limits pays for that service through its own levy, and the Pensacola stack leaves it out.

Billing calendar and penalties

Notices go out November 1 to whoever owned the property on January 1. Paying early earns a discount that shrinks by a point each month, from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. March is full price.

  • April 1: delinquent. Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty, tangible property 1.5 percent.
  • May 1: advertising costs start to accrue.
  • A bill that never arrived is no excuse. The owner must find out the amount, even when mail went to an old address.

If you move, send the new mailing address to the Property Appraiser, because the roll lives there.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Installment plan

Owners who paid more than $100 of tax the prior year and have no mortgage escrow can split the bill. Applications open online January 1 and close April 30 for that cycle.

  • First payment by June 30, with a 6 percent discount.
  • Second by September 30, with 4.5 percent off.
  • Third by December 31, with 3 percent off.
  • Fourth by March 31, with no discount.

The first two payments each equal a quarter of last year's tax. The last two divide the actual balance. Miss the June payment and the plan ends, and a regular November bill follows. Partial payments toward a current bill can be accepted at the collector's discretion, but they need an application, earn no discount and cannot be made after March 31.

The Duplicate Tax Notice Request Program lets you name a relative or friend to get a courtesy copy of every bill. Mail the signed application to the Collections Department, P.O. Box 1312, Pensacola, FL 32591-1312.

Flat charges on the bill

Some lines ignore your home's value, yet unpaid amounts can still lead to a certificate. Where the parcel sits decides which ones appear.

  • Unincorporated Escambia: fire protection, rescue and advanced life support, street lighting, road paving, retention ponds and solid waste, all assessed by the county commissioners.
  • Inside Pensacola: stormwater, based on the impervious surface on the lot, assessed by the City Council.

Title agents ask about these at closing, so read the bottom of the bill as well as the millage section.

Homestead exemption

A permanent residence can have up to $50,000 taken off its taxable value. File Form DR-501 with the Property Appraiser by March 1. After the first year, assessed value rises under a cap, shown at 2.7 percent on the state's 2026 chart.

A sale restarts the clock. The buyer is assessed at market value from the following January, while portability may move part of your cap to a replacement Florida home.

Disputing a value

The process begins with the proposed-tax notice that arrives in August. A petition on Form DR-486 must reach the clerk within 25 days of the mailing. The same notice lists budget hearing dates for the school board, the county and Pensacola.

A denied exemption goes the other way, through the Value Adjustment Board, and you have 30 days from the mailing of the denial letter. Keep every notice.

Before you call or file, collect your August notice, a copy of your deed and anything that supports your number, such as a recent appraisal or photos of damage. Write down who you spoke with and when. A short, specific request tends to get a faster answer than a general complaint.

When a bill goes unpaid

After April 1 a certificate can be sold on the parcel, and a deed application may follow later. The Tax Collector warns that nonpayment can cost you the property.

  • Investors bid the interest rate down in quarter-point steps.
  • A deed application must wait two years and carries a $75 fee.
  • For a homestead, the opening deed bid adds half the latest assessed figure.

Closing with a certificate attached is routine. The title agent pays the redemption out of the seller's side of the statement.

Other reductions

Seniors, disabled owners and military families each have their own forms. A service-connected disabled veteran aged 65 or more may receive a homestead discount matching the VA rating. A disabled former servicemember gets $5,000 off assessed value. Deferral requests go to the Tax Collector by March 31. Ask the appraiser which local senior options the county offers.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the Tax Collector's office for every account under your name, including a Business Tax Receipt if you rented the property or ran a business there. Deed stamps are 70 cents for every hundred dollars of price, paid at the clerk. If your lender escrows, find out what it paid and how quickly any refund arrives. An inherited house may need clerk estate records before a title agent will insure it.

A plain order of events helps. Request the payoff first, then give it to the closing agent along with your ID and loan information. The agent pays the tax and any other liens from your proceeds and sends you a final statement. Compare that statement with the collector's figure before you sign, and keep a copy for your own records.

Frequently asked questions

What do the 2026 millage lines add up to inside Pensacola?

The City of Pensacola area totals 16.9597 mills, built from county, school, city, water district, library and children's trust lines. Unincorporated parcels total 13.3552.

Who qualifies for the Escambia installment plan?

Owners who paid more than $100 in tax the year before and have no escrow. The application closes April 30, and a missed June 30 first payment ends the plan.

Does the Escambia homestead cap pass to a buyer?

No. The buyer starts at market value the next January. Portability can carry some of your cap to another Florida home.

Can a relative get copies of my Escambia bill?

Yes. Under the Duplicate Tax Notice Request Program you name a relative or friend, then mail the signed form to the Collections Department, P.O. Box 1312, Pensacola, FL 32591-1312.

Can I sell an Escambia house that has a tax certificate on it?

Yes. Closing redeems the certificate from your proceeds. Get a payoff figure from the Tax Collector before the closing date.

Offices that handle your Hernando County tax bill

Hernando County divides tax duties among three elected officers. One values land and approves exemptions, one sends the bills and banks the payments, and one records deeds and holds tax deed auctions. Before a sale closes you will likely contact each of them.

When is Hernando County property tax due?

Notices are mailed in November. The county takes payment up to March 31, and an account that is open when April 1 arrives is delinquent.

Pay in November and you keep 4 percent. Each later month takes off a point, through February, and in March you pay the full amount. A payment mailed in a discount month counts by its postmark. Online e-checks cost nothing on current or delinquent bills, while a card payment adds a fee of 2.5% or $2.75, whichever applies as the minimum, paid to an outside vendor.

Businesses and rental properties also owe tangible personal property tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment. That charge rides on the same bill and gets the same discounts. A $25,000 exemption is open to owners who file a return by April 1. A landlord selling a rental can ask whether such an account is tied to the address.

How does the Hernando County installment plan work?

Under the plan a bill is paid in four quarterly pieces, and each piece is accepted only in its own month. You can sign up beginning every November 1, with a cutoff of April 30. Enrollment is final once the June payment clears.

Hernando County Tax Collector installment schedule
Due dateDiscount
June 306%
July 31None, keeps you on the plan
September 304.5%
December 313%
March 31Final payment, no discount

If you miss an installment, it comes due along with the next one. Anything left owing on April 1 is delinquent and gets no discount. Leaving the plan forfeits the discounts as well. Section 197.222 is the statute that created it.

A separate route allows partial payments on the current year between November 1 and March 31. It needs a signed application, wipes out all discounts and permits five partial payments at most, with the rest due by March 31.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

Homestead in Hernando County lowers the taxable value of your own residence by as much as $50,000. To qualify, you need to hold title and have made the house your permanent Florida home as of January 1 in the year of the application.

Filings being accepted now apply to tax year 2027, with a March 1, 2027 cutoff. A later filing is counted for 2028. Owners can file in person at an appraiser office, send paperwork by mail, or use the secure online portal. A statewide Save Our Homes cap limits annual increases in assessed value to 3 percent or the change in CPI, whichever is lower. The Florida Revenue chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

Your bill shows all exemptions combined as one dollar amount labeled Exemption. After a sale the appraiser removes the seller's exemption and cap beginning the following year, and the new owner must apply again.

Unpaid taxes and the certificate sale

Starting April 1, delinquent tax in Hernando County accrues 3% interest, is advertised in a local newspaper, and adds advertising and collection charges. At month's end in May the tax collector auctions the resulting tax certificates over the internet on LienHub. You can still pay through May 29.

  • Bids open at 18 percent interest and step down toward 0.25 percent.
  • Whoever wins pays the taxes and takes a first lien on the parcel.
  • The county itself takes any homestead parcel with a taxable amount under $250.00, as well as one in litigation.
  • A certificate lives seven years unless bankruptcy interrupts it.
  • Once two years pass, the holder can request a tax deed sale, and the clerk runs it.

Any payment method works on a delinquent bill, except that a parcel already in tax deed status requires certified funds. When a deed sale draws no bids, the land is put on the list of lands available for taxes, and the county has 90 days to buy it first.

Closing on a Hernando County sale

Tax owed by the seller comes out of the sale proceeds at closing, and the recorded deed is what sends future bills to the buyer. After a completed deed reaches the clerk, the appraiser updates the roll's owner name. The collector's file catches up once the certified tax roll arrives in October.

On a deed, Florida charges documentary stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of the price everywhere except Miami-Dade. Everyone named on the deed shares liability. Your closing statement ought to divide this year's bill between the two sides. If a tangible personal property account appears on the bill, tell the title company.

Each taxing body sets its own millage. The collector lists the county commission, the City of Brooksville, the school board and the regional water district among them. A millage report goes up on the appraiser's site after the roll is finally certified. To find the rate for one parcel, look at the TRIM notice that arrives in August or call the tax collector.

A few ordinary steps help. Have the title company get a written payoff from the collector near the closing date, because balances move. Keep the parcel number and a copy of your deed within reach when you phone an office. Scan every tax year for a balance, not only this one. When back taxes or a certificate could stall a buyer who needs a mortgage, a cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the title company can pay off the debt from your proceeds at the table.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How to appeal your assessment

To contest a value, file a DR-486 petition with the Value Adjustment Board through the clerk's office. You have 25 days from the appraiser's August TRIM mailing. A petition that arrives after the date printed on the notice is too late, so note when your envelope shows up.

When a homestead exemption, classification or deferral is turned down, a separate 30 day limit runs from the date the denial letter was sent. The board rules on value and exemptions and nothing else. Rates are decided at the September and October budget hearings of each taxing body. If you own a rental or agricultural parcel, ask the appraiser's office, whose site has pages on agricultural classification, mobile homes and tangible property, whether another filing applies.

Collect your evidence first: recent sales of similar homes, photos of condition problems and repair estimates. Appraiser staff can often fix an obvious mistake in square footage or exemption status without any hearing.

Frequently asked questions

When does Hernando County property tax become delinquent?

On April 1. The county takes payment through the end of March, then the collector adds 3% interest plus advertising and collection fees.

What discount does Hernando County give for paying early?

Four percent for a November payment, then one point less each month through February. March has none, and a postmark fixes the payment date on current-year bills.

Can I pay my Hernando County tax bill by card?

Yes, for an outside vendor's fee of 2.5% or a $2.75 minimum. Online e-checks are free on current and delinquent bills, and tax deed payments must be in certified funds.

How do I apply for the Hernando County homestead exemption?

File with the property appraiser in person, by mail or through the online portal. The 2027 deadline is March 1, 2027, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1.

Who runs the Hernando County tax certificate sale?

The tax collector holds it each year at the end of May, on LienHub. Bidders register there, and parcels come up one after another by parcel number.

Offices that touch an Indian River County tax bill

Responsibility is split three ways. The Property Appraiser sets values and accepts exemption filings, the Tax Collector mails and collects bills, and a county Value Adjustment Board hears appeals. Recorded deeds are kept by the Clerk of the Court.

The Property Appraiser has two offices, one in Vero at 1800 27th St., Bldg. B, Vero Beach, (772) 226-1469, and one in Sebastian at 1921 U.S. 1, (772) 226-1133, both open Monday through Friday from eight to five. The Tax Collector's tax department is at (772) 226-1343. As an agent for local governments, the Collector has no say over assessed value or the amount due.

Vero Beach, Sebastian, Indian River Shores, Orchid and Fellsmere are the municipalities in the county. A house in any of them is billed by the same county Tax Collector.

Due dates and early payment discounts

Bills go out by November 1. The early payment discount shrinks one step each month until March.

Discount by postmark month
Postmark monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchFull gross amount

A bill that never shows up in the mail is still the owner's responsibility. Anyone without one by about November 9 each year should call the Tax Collector. Send address changes in writing to the Property Appraiser, and expect a separate bill for every parcel you own.

Two messages on a bill deserve attention. "Do Not Pay" means a mortgage company has requested your original bill. "Back Taxes Remain Unpaid" means delinquent tax also sits on the account. Call (772) 226-1343 to learn the amount.

What if the bill goes unpaid?

April 1 is the delinquency date, and a 3% penalty attaches to the gross tax. In May an advertising fee is added and the account is listed in a local newspaper once a week for three weeks. A certificate must then be sold by June 1.

The Tax Collector refers bidders to a county page on a tax certificate sale website. The certificate is a first lien on the parcel. Two years after the April 1 of issue, its holder may seek a deed, and the Clerk then auctions the property under the state's deposit and 24 hour payment rules.

Partial payments are not accepted on current or delinquent real estate bills. An owner who cannot pay in full has three routes: next year's installment plan, a homestead deferral if eligible, or a sale that clears the tax from proceeds.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Does Indian River County offer a four-payment plan?

Yes, provided next year's estimated bill is above $100. You apply before the plan year starts, and 2026 tax year applications are accepted November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027.

The plan has four bills: June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (no discount). June and September are computed from last year's tax, while December and March absorb the true-up to the new roll. A first payment made late, in July, loses the 6%. Skip it entirely and the account reverts to an ordinary November bill.

The office cannot accept an installment outside its month, and a payment that misses its month forfeits the discount. If the house sells mid-plan, the account stays on the plan for that year, so give the closing agent a list of the installments you paid. A buyer who would rather have an annual bill next year can ask the Tax Collector to drop the account.

Deferral and exemptions

A homestead owner whose age and income qualify may postpone part or all of the bill by applying to the Tax Collector by March 31. Interest builds on the deferred amount as a lien, and everything comes due at death, on a sale of the home, or when homestead status ends.

Homestead filings go to the Property Appraiser by March 1, and you must be a permanent Florida resident on January 1. A filing submitted after September 6 is applied to the 2027 tax year. The state exemption has two tiers, and the tier that also exempts school tax covers the first $25,000 only.

On a homestead, the Save Our Homes cap (2.7 percent for 2026) restrains growth. When the home sells, value resets to market the next January 1, so the buyer's bill may look nothing like yours.

How to petition against an Indian River County value

File with the Value Adjustment Board by the date printed on your Notice of Proposed Property Taxes. Florida sets that at 25 days after the notices are mailed. The Property Appraiser's home page links to the board's own site.

If the appraiser denies an exemption, you have 30 days from the mailing of the denial letter. Bring comparable sales, photographs and repair estimates with you. A petition built on a clear record of condition and recent sales is easier for a hearing officer to act on than a general complaint about the number.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If the bill arrives after the house has sold

A November notice follows the certified tax roll, which means it can land on someone who sold earlier in the year. The Tax Collector gives simple directions for that situation.

  • A real estate bill for property you no longer own should be forwarded to the new owner or returned to the Tax Collector's office.
  • A business equipment bill is different: if you owned the equipment on January 1, you still owe the tax. If you did not, call the Property Appraiser at (772) 226-1370.
  • Each parcel gets its own bill, so check that the legal description on yours matches everything you own.
  • Address changes go to the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector, and the appraiser offers an online change-of-address form.

Acting on a misdirected notice right away keeps it from turning into a delinquent account that a buyer's lender might spot.

Seller's closing checklist

Start by ordering a payoff and confirming which bill is open. The new owner is answerable for the whole November bill, but closing agents ordinarily prorate it and credit the buyer for the seller's months. Nothing goes to the Tax Collector as a partial payment from the seller. Keep a copy of every receipt and payoff letter for the closing file.

  • Look for a back-taxes message on the account.
  • List any installment payments already made.
  • Ask if a deferral lien is attached to the homestead.
  • Check the recorded deeds at the Clerk's office.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and every party on the document can be liable. Where back tax, a deferral lien or a damaged roof complicates a sale, a cash buyer taking the house as-is can have the title company pay the balance. Cash also skips lender appraisal and underwriting, which removes one common cause of delay.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I pay Indian River County property tax?

Use the county tax payment portal that the Tax Collector links from its site. Discounts follow the postmark date, and the tax department at (772) 226-1343 can explain other payment options.

When does Indian River County property tax become delinquent?

April 1, when the 3% penalty is added. In May unpaid accounts are advertised, ahead of a certificate sale due by June 1.

When can I apply for the 2026 tax year installment plan?

Applications for the 2026 tax year run November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and the first payment falls in June.

Can I pay part of an Indian River County bill?

No. Partial payments on current or delinquent real estate bills are not accepted.

Do I owe the whole year's tax if I sell in spring?

The bill goes to the owner, but closing agents normally prorate, so the buyer repays the seller for the months after closing. Check the split on the closing statement.

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Who bills and who values

Lake County divides property tax between two desks. One sets the worth of each parcel and files exemptions. The other prints the bill and takes the money. A problem with value belongs to the first and a problem with payment to the second, and neither can repair the other's side.

To fix a name, mailing address, parcel location or assessed value, phone the Property Appraiser at (352) 253-2150. Bills open for collection on November 1, and a notice lost in the mail does not excuse a late payment. Escrowed loans are marked with a code at the top of the notice and a banner along the bottom.

  • Property Appraiser: assigns values, processes homestead and other exemptions, sends the proposed-tax notice in August.
  • Tax Collector: mails bills, receives payments, and holds the June certificate sale for accounts still open.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: records the deed, takes in the stamp tax, and staffs the value adjustment board.

Early payment discounts and deadlines

An owner who pays in November saves up to 4 percent. Each later month trims one point off that saving until February, and from March there is nothing to claim.

Lake County payment schedule for the full annual bill
Paid in full byDiscount
November 304 percent
December 313 percent
January 312 percent
February 281 percent
March 31Gross amount, no discount

For mailed checks the postmark decides which discount applies. Come April 1, a statutory 3 percent interest charge joins the balance, and unpaid items head toward the certificate sale by June 1.

Installment terms and the sale calendar are fixed by the collector yearly. Phone that office before planning around either.

What millage rates apply to a Lake County home?

The answer changes with location. The 2026 final millage rate sheet from the appraiser gives one total for each taxing district code, from the low 13s in unincorporated land up to the high 19s in some cities.

The unincorporated codes at the top of the sheet total 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678, depending on the code. Three lines repeat in every row: the county general fund at 5.0254, the school board state line at 3.0560 and the school board local line at 2.9980. What separates one district from another is the extra layers, such as a city levy, a fire or ambulance district, a hospital district or a community development district.

  • Clermont: 16.2875 total, with a city line of 4.2000.
  • Leesburg: 15.8704 total, with a city line of 3.3783.
  • Mount Dora: 18.7921 total, with a city line of 6.3000.
  • Eustis: 19.8819 total, with a city line of 7.3898.
  • Montverde: 15.3975 total, with a city line of 2.8300.

Your code appears on your notice and on the parcel record; match it to its row on the sheet. The cities on the sheet are Astatula, Clermont, Eustis, Fruitland Park, Groveland, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lady Lake, Leesburg, Mascotte, Minneola, Montverde, Mount Dora, Tavares and Umatilla.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption and Save Our Homes

Making the house your residence by January 1 and filing before March 1 exempts as much as $50,000 of value. School levies reach only the first slice of that exemption, so the school lines on the millage sheet (3.0560 and 2.9980) get the smaller break.

The application is Form DR-501, filed with the appraiser. Leasing the home out or moving away ends the benefit. Extra senior, veteran and disability breaks may exist locally, and the appraiser's home page links to a list of them with eligibility rules.

Save Our Homes caps how fast a homestead's assessment can climb, tying the ceiling to inflation. The state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. Once the house sells, the parcel is assessed at market value again, and the buyer's first full bill can differ sharply from yours. If you are buying another Florida home, portability may let you bring the accumulated savings along; it uses a separate form and a three-year window.

Property tax when you sell

The settlement statement splits this year's tax between you and the buyer. Older unpaid years have to be settled before title moves, and the title company typically sends the collector that money out of what the seller would receive.

No statement exists yet for the current year when a house sells in spring or summer, so the title agent estimates it. Ask the collector for the exact number and for any older balance while terms are still being worked out.

  • Check the parcel record for the right owner name and mailing address.
  • Ask the collector if any year is delinquent or has been sold as a certificate.
  • Mention your homestead exemption to the title company so the split uses the correct amount.
  • Request a draft settlement statement early and check its tax line against what the collector told you.
  • Tell the buyer that the next bill may be higher once the value resets.

State law sets deed stamps at 70 cents for each $100 of consideration. The contract may name a payer, yet both parties stay liable.

Unpaid tax and tax certificates

A bill still open on April 1 is delinquent, and the parcel can in time reach a tax deed sale. Before that it is sold as a certificate, and the holder must wait two years before asking for a deed.

The certificate sale opens on or before June 1. Bidders compete by taking the lowest interest rate, and certificates nobody wants go to the county. Homestead parcels owing under $250 are issued to the county without an auction. When a deed sale does happen, the clerk holds a public auction and the high bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit.

Owners who cannot pay may qualify for deferral. A homestead owner with a low income can ask the collector to put off part of the bill using Form DR-570, due at the end of March. The installment prepayment request has its own May 1 date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How do you challenge a Lake County value?

When the August notice shows a value you dispute, you have 25 days from the notice to petition the value adjustment board. Count from the date printed on it, not the day it arrived.

If an exemption or deferral is denied, a separate 30-day clock starts on the day the denial letter was mailed. The clerk's office supports the board and posts its forms. Speak with the appraiser first; questions about square footage or exemption status often get resolved without a petition.

Before you call, gather the notice, recent nearby sales, photos and any repair estimates. Those are the papers the appraiser will want to see.

Budget hearings by the taxing authorities take place in September and October, with final millage following. Rates are argued there, while your own house's value is argued with the appraiser.

Frequently asked questions

When are Lake County property taxes due?

Pay in November for 4 percent off, with the discount shrinking to 1 percent in February. The full amount is due by the end of March, and a 3 percent charge applies from April 1.

Who do I call to change my Lake County mailing address on a tax bill?

Phone the Lake County Property Appraiser at (352) 253-2150. The collector cannot alter a name, address, location or assessed value.

What is the total millage in unincorporated Lake County?

Unincorporated codes total 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678 on the 2026 final sheet, depending on district. Find your code on your notice.

Does selling my Lake County house reset my tax value?

For the buyer, yes. Your capped value stays behind because the sale is a change of ownership.

Can I sell a Lake County house with unpaid property tax?

Yes. The balance and any certificate redemption are paid from your proceeds. Obtain a payoff from the collector and hand it to the closing agent early.

Leon County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Leon County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Leon County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Leon County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Leon County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Leon County houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Leon County property tax?
We buy Leon County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who handles property tax in Leon County

The job is shared. A valuation office assigns parcel worth and approves exemptions, a collection office mails bills and takes money, and elected boards choose the millage that links them.

Sequence matters: values first, rates next, then a certified roll, and finally mailed notices. The collector cannot edit the roll, so a corrected name or address has to be requested from the appraiser.

  • Appraiser: values, exemption files, parcel data, owner records.
  • Collector: notices, payments, quarterly plans, delinquency, certificates.
  • Clerk: deed recording and the stamp tax paid with it.

Billing dates and delinquency

Bills for each calendar year open for collection on November 1, and it falls to the owner to find out the amount before April 1. The 2026 bills were mailed in November.

Once April 1 arrives, the balance grows by a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, interest at 1.5 percent monthly and collection costs under s. 197.332(1). Delinquent names must be published in the newspaper within 45 days, and anything still open then is headed for a tax certificate sale on June 1.

The state discount ladder of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent, November through February, applies in Leon as elsewhere. With an escrowed loan, the lender should request the original notice from the collector so the owner gets a duplicate copy.

Installment plan for Leon County property tax

An estimated tax above $100 qualifies an owner for four installments. File the application with the collector before May 1; after that, enrollment continues automatically each year.

Leon County quarterly installment schedule
InstallmentDueDiscount and notes
FirstJune 306 percent off
SecondSeptember 304.5 percent off
ThirdDecember 313 percent off, plus half of any true-up
FourthMarch 31Full price, plus the remaining true-up

To get the discount, pay the first quarter by June 30. A late first payment is accepted through July 31 but at full price, and after July 31 enrollment is cancelled and the whole bill is due March 31. Quarters one and two mirror last year's notice, while new owners, values or exemptions affect quarters three and four. Selling mid-year? Hand the title company a record of payments made.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Exemptions through the Leon County Property Appraiser

March 1 is the yearly filing cutoff. The appraiser's site describes homestead and a group of veteran and service benefits; homestead comes first because the others depend on it.

Homestead in Florida comes in two tiers. The first $25,000 of assessed value is protected from all levies, school taxes included, and the second tier protects value over $50,000 from non-school levies alone. You must live there permanently as of January 1; leasing the home or leaving ends the benefit.

Each of the veteran and military exemptions the office describes requires homestead first:

  • A $5,000 reduction when a service-connected disability rates 10 percent or higher (surviving spouses may be eligible).
  • A discount percentage for combat-related disability at age 65 or older, matched to the VA rating.
  • Full exemption for total and permanent disability.
  • A deployment exemption, claimed with Form DR-501M and deployment orders.

Paperwork can be sent four ways, fax included. Income-limited senior exemptions may be added locally. Ask the appraiser what applies at your address.

How assessment caps work in Leon County

For non-school taxes, assessments on property without homestead cannot climb above 10 percent a year. Homestead growth is capped by Save Our Homes at 3 percent or inflation, whichever is smaller.

State caps have been 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. The sale resets the parcel to full just value on the following January 1, which means a buyer does not keep a long-time owner's low assessment. Remember this when setting a list price.

Amendment 3 starts January 1, 2027 and does not touch 2026 bills. The appraiser expects state guidance; watch that office's site ahead of the next roll.

Business personal property tax

Tangible personal property owned by a business is taxed separately from real estate and enforced differently. If it goes unpaid, the collector petitions for tax warrants; no certificate is placed on the land.

A month after the warrants are prepared, the office asks the Clerk of the Circuit Court for an order allowing levy and seizure of property, or garnishment of the delinquent taxpayer's bank account, for the tax and costs. Landlords with furnished rentals, or owners running a business out of a house, should know the same collector takes both real estate tax and this separate tax, with collection beginning each November 1. A seller asking for a payoff should ask whether any tangible account is tied to the address, and a buyer purchasing a rental from an investor should ask the same before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Tax at closing in Leon County

Request a proration and a payoff number for any delinquent amount, and report installments you have paid. The agent splits the current year between buyer and seller, while late balances are paid out of your proceeds.

Deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, the same everywhere in Florida except Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk at recording, and all parties named on the deed are liable regardless of how they divide it.

On the settlement statement, look for the tax proration line and compare it with the collector's balance. If the numbers differ, ask the title company to explain before you sign. A balance paid at closing should come with a receipt or confirmation, and it is worth keeping that with your sale records.

The house loses its homestead on sale, and the buyer files again by March 1. A seller relocating in Florida can bring along the Save Our Homes benefit with Form DR-501T, filed within three years of January 1 of the year the old homestead ended.

Before you list

  1. Get the current balance from the collector, along with word on any delinquent year or certificate.
  2. Check whether a business or tangible personal property account is attached to the address.
  3. A rented house means working around the tenant's lease, and renting ends homestead.
  4. Keep your latest notice and bill ready for buyers curious about carrying costs.
  5. Obtain a written payoff before agreeing on a closing date.

A cash sale cuts out lender underwriting, but title work still looks for tax balances, so the same steps apply. If a payoff changes between contract and closing, ask the collector for an updated figure and send it to the closing agent right away.

Leon County housing in brief

Tallahassee sits in Leon County, which counted about 299,048 people in mid-2025 over 668 square miles. Owners occupy only 52.6 percent of its 143,256 housing units, owner-occupied homes carry a typical value of $301,800, and median gross rent is $1,291.

Since owners live in barely half the homes, plenty of sellers are landlords with tenants in the house. Homestead ends once a house is rented, and the lease can dictate the closing date.

Frequently asked questions

When does Leon County property tax become delinquent?

April 1 following the assessment year. After that the collector charges a delinquency fee, an advertising fee, monthly interest and statutory collection costs.

Can I pay Leon County property tax in installments?

Yes, when estimated tax exceeds $100 and you apply before May 1. The four dates are June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31; the first three carry 6, 4.5 and 3 percent discounts.

By when must Leon County homestead be filed?

March 1. The appraiser takes applications by email, mail, fax or in person, and will tell you the exemption amount.

Does Amendment 3 change my 2026 Leon County bill?

No. The amendment starts January 1, 2027, so 2026 bills stay as issued.

Who changes the name or address on a Leon County tax bill?

The appraiser handles it. Changes to the roll go through that office, so reach out before bills are mailed again.

Who sends the bill and who sets the value

Valuation belongs to the Martin County Property Appraiser; billing and collection belong to the Martin County Tax Collector. Both are constitutional offices of the county, while recorded deeds and liens live in the clerk's Official Records.

  • Martin County Property Appraiser: real property parcel search by parcel ID, account number, subdivision, address or owner last name, plus published millage.
  • Martin County Tax Collector: tax statements, alternative payment plans, delinquent taxes and certificates, an important-dates page, a tangible personal property page and a glossary. Offices operate in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, and the phone line is 772-288-5600.
  • Martin County Clerk Official Records: the search for recorded instruments.

Amounts owed go to the collector. Value, exemptions and parcel records go to the appraiser. Ten taxing authorities levy tax on Martin County parcels, and each proposes its own millage rate before public hearings set the budgets.

Where to pay and get help

The tax collector runs four offices: Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City. Its home page posts estimated wait times for each office, and e-checks cost nothing. An account can be looked up through the online payment pages or the county-taxes portal with no trip needed.

The site also carries a glossary of tax terms, a page on tangible personal property taxes, an FAQ on tax certificate sales and a page on alternative payment plans. Site information can change daily and is not a legal guarantee, the collector warns, so phone to confirm any amount before you rely on it at a closing.

To understand the value side, use the appraiser's parcel search and compare your TRIM notice with the published roll data. Lenders and title companies commonly request the appraiser record along with the collector's account history.

When Martin County property taxes are due

Mailing usually happens around November 1, and the gross amount must be paid by March 31. The early discount starts at 4% in November and ends at 1% in February.

Martin County tax calendar

What delinquency costs

Starting April 1, unpaid real property taxes carry 3% interest. Unpaid business personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 delinquent fee, and those accounts are advertised in a local newspaper within 45 days.

On real estate, an ad appears in the newspaper each week for three weeks ahead of the certificate sale, and the parcel is charged for it. Whoever buys the certificate must hold off two years before asking the owner for payment; a tax deed application may follow.

Business and vehicle taxes on the collector's calendar

The calendar covers more than real estate. Business personal property earns the same early discounts and turns delinquent on the same April 1. Warrants for delinquent personal property accounts are prepared before April 30, two years after the assessment year.

  • Local business tax receipts: renewals are due September 30 and become delinquent October 1, when a late fee applies.
  • Heavy trucks over 5,000 pounds, truck-trailers, semi-trailers and certain vehicles for hire: registration and renewal due December 31.
  • Mobile home decals: they also expire December 31.

Rental owners and anyone running a business from the property should ask the collector about these items, since a house sale does not shut down a business account attached to the address.

Is there an installment plan in Martin County?

Yes, section 197.222 allows an alternative payment plan of four payments. Applications for the next year close April 30.

  • June 30: first payment with a 6% discount.
  • July: a late first payment may be accepted with a 5% penalty, otherwise participation is canceled.
  • September 30: second payment with a 4.5% discount.
  • December 31: third payment with a 3% discount.
  • March 31: fourth and final payment.

Once enrolled, taxpayers continue without reapplying. Selling midway through the plan means asking the collector for the unpaid portion, which is settled at closing.

Exemptions that can lower a Martin County bill

Filing is with the property appraiser, and the first deadline is early March.

  • Homestead takes up to $50,000 off value. School taxes see only the first $25,000 of it.
  • A state cap limits yearly growth on a homestead. The state chart prints 2.7% for 2026.
  • Other property has a 10 percent annual ceiling.
  • Portability carries cap savings to a new homestead, for up to $500,000 of difference. Chapter 2026-239 changes first apply to the 2027 roll.
  • An honorably discharged Florida resident with a service-connected disability of 10 percent or more receives a $5,000 cut in assessed value.

A sale resets the parcel to market-based value the following January. The TRIM notice arrives in August, and petitions go to the clerk.

How Martin County tax is settled at a sale

The collector's payoff number lets the title company clear the tax when the sale funds. All four offices, in Stuart, Hobe Sound, Indiantown and Palm City, can be reached at 772-288-5600 about whether a certificate exists.

Florida charges deed stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. A contract-for-deed buyer on record is among those notified before a tax deed sale, so a land contract does not hide a parcel from the process.

  1. Get the payoff figure and certificate details from the collector.
  2. Give the closing agent a record of any installments paid.
  3. Check the settlement statement's tax line before you sign.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but title work still looks for unpaid tax, so the same steps apply.

Preparing to sell with a Martin County tax account

A short routine before listing keeps tax questions from slowing a contract.

  1. Look up the parcel with the appraiser and confirm the owner name and mailing address.
  2. Ask the collector for the account history and any certificate or delinquent balance.
  3. If you are enrolled in the installment plan, list the payments made so far.
  4. If a business or rental account is tied to the property, close or transfer it with the collector.
  5. Keep your latest TRIM notice and tax statement on hand for buyers and lenders.

Because amounts change daily, confirm the payoff again a few days before closing and send the final figure to the closing agent. The buyer should also expect a higher bill after the sale, since value resets to market.

Frequently asked questions

When are Martin County property tax statements mailed?

On or about November 1 each year. The gross amount is due by March 31.

What interest does Martin County add after April 1?

A 3% interest charge on unpaid real property taxes. Tangible personal property accrues 1.5% per month plus a $2.00 fee.

Does Martin County have an installment plan for property tax?

Yes. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three. Applications are due by April 30.

Who do I call in Martin County about my tax account?

Call the Martin County Tax Collector at 772-288-5600. For parcel values and exemptions, contact the Martin County Property Appraiser.

Can I sell a Martin County house if taxes are overdue?

Yes. The balance can be cleared at closing. Get the payoff and any certificate details from the collector beforehand.

The Okaloosa County market in brief

Okaloosa County has 221,810 residents, up 4.8 percent since 2020, on 930.19 square miles of land. It counts 108,608 housing units and 85,411 households. The median owned home is valued at $351,200, 68.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied, and median rent is $1,612. About 31,494 residents are former service members and 18.2 percent are seniors, so military and age-based relief comes up often. The county issued 1,057 building permits in 2025.

Many residents move in and out, which means a deep buyer pool and also many sellers who bought recently and carry a fresh assessment.

Due dates and penalties

Collection for the calendar year starts November 1, with notices out by then. Gross payment is accepted through March 31, and the discount ladder is below.

  • November payers keep 4 percent.
  • December payers keep 3 percent.
  • January and February drop to 2 and 1 percent.
  • March has no discount; April 1 is delinquency.

A 3 percent penalty hits real property taxes in April, and reminder notices of unpaid taxes are mailed by April 10. Current taxes can be paid by mail, in person, online or by phone, and card payments add a bank card user fee. After delinquency the office takes cash, cashier's check or money order, and postmarks no longer count.

The installment plan

The county offers a four-payment plan for owners whose estimated taxes exceed $100 and who do not pay through escrow. Paper or online applications are accepted until May 1.

Okaloosa installment plan schedule
InstallmentDueShare and discount
FirstJuly 31One quarter of estimated taxes, 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30
SecondSeptember 30One quarter, 4.5 percent discount
ThirdDecember 31One quarter plus half of any adjustment, 3 percent discount
FourthMarch 31One quarter plus the other half of the adjustment, no discount

Missing the first payment cancels the plan, and the full amount is due by March 31 of the following year. Participants are re-enrolled automatically, and discounts do not apply to delinquent payments. A sale in mid-plan leaves a remaining balance that the closing agent has to settle.
