Values, notices and challenges

Values are fixed as of January 1. Rentals and other non-homestead parcels can rise at most 10 percent a year, a cap that helps an investor until a sale resets it.

The proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and a petition about value must reach the clerk within 25 days. Taxing bodies then hold budget hearings in September and October and adopt final millage in October and November.

  • January 1: value date.
  • March 1: exemption deadline.
  • April 1: tangible personal property return deadline, for owners of furnishings in a rental.

A landlord's furniture, fixtures and equipment fall under tangible personal property tax. The collector bills it on the same discount ladder as real estate, with a 1.5 percent monthly fee added after April 1 delinquency. Compare your parcel with similar properties nearby before deciding whether to file a challenge.

Other items the Tax Collector handles

Beyond the real estate bill, the collector's year-round schedule touches sellers with rentals or business property.

  • Tangible personal property returns go to the property appraiser by April 1, and the same discount ladder applies to the bill.
  • A 1.5 percent monthly fee is added to unpaid tangible personal property tax after April 1, and the list of delinquent taxpayers is advertised once in a local newspaper.
  • Tax warrants are issued before April 30 of the next year on unpaid tangible bills, and the collector may ask the circuit court for an order to levy and seize the property.
  • Mobile homes and recreational vehicles permanently affixed to the owner's land and declared real property receive a permanent RP decal, which transfers to the buyer when land and home sell together.

For an RP decal, the owner first obtains Form DR-402 from the property appraiser to show that the land and the mobile home title are in the same name. A seller with a mobile home on owned land should settle that paperwork before listing. Do it early, because a missing form can hold up the transfer of the decal to the buyer.

Exemptions

With a large military population, the service-related reductions deserve a look. Relief includes a $5,000 reduction for disabled ex-servicemembers and a possible full exemption for total and permanent disability. A servicemember on orders can rent out a homestead without losing the exemption, and deployed members can claim a share through Form DR-501M.

The property appraiser also handles address changes, and the collector lists (850) 651-7240 for that office. Ask whether the optional senior exemption is in force and what income limit applies.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens if Okaloosa County taxes go unpaid?

Delinquent parcels are advertised weekly for three weeks at the owner's expense. The certificate sale follows on LienHub by June 1, with bids falling from 18 percent.

The certificate is a seven-year first lien, and redeeming it means paying tax, interest, penalties and advertising fees. A deed application becomes possible after two years, with the clerk of court running the auction. The collector also sells county-held certificates that earn 18 percent.

On homestead land, the opening bid includes half of the assessed value, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit with the balance due within 24 hours. A seller with any unpaid year should clear it before listing.

Taxes at closing

Closing agents prorate the current year and check for any earlier balance. The year of sale is billed the next November, so the settlement figure is an estimate.

The deed is taxed at 70 cents per $100 of price. A long-time owner's capped value, which the state chart limits to 2.7 percent growth for 2026, does not pass to the buyer.

Before you list, ask the collector's office whether any account is open, ask the title company how it will prorate the year, and confirm that your mailing address on file is current so notices reach you. A cash buyer who takes the house as is can close faster, but open taxes and recorded liens are paid from your proceeds all the same.

Preparing a mobile home, rental or furnished property for sale

If your property includes anything beyond a plain house, add a few steps. List the furniture and equipment you plan to leave and confirm whether a return was filed. Gather your RP decal and the property appraiser's paperwork if a mobile home sits on your land. Ask your title company to check the deed and title names so they match. These steps are general, and your closing agent can tell you which apply to your sale. Put the list in writing and share it with the buyer's side, so everyone agrees on what stays, what goes and who is responsible for any open tax account.

Frequently asked questions

What does an Okaloosa County owner pay if taxes are late?

A 3 percent penalty is added to real property taxes in April. Advertising and collection fees follow, and the total depends on the day payment arrives.

How do I join the Okaloosa County installment plan?

Apply before May 1 at the collector's office or online. Your estimated taxes must exceed $100 and cannot be paid through escrow.

When is the first Okaloosa installment due?

July 31, with a 6 percent discount if postmarked by June 30. Skip it and the plan is canceled, with the whole bill due the next March 31.

Who changes my mailing address for Okaloosa tax bills?

The property appraiser. The collector gives (850) 651-7240 and www.okaloosapa.com for address changes.

Who conducts Okaloosa tax deed sales?

The clerk of court holds the public auction after a deed application. The tax collector handles the earlier certificate sale online.

Which Osceola County office answers my tax question?

The work is split three ways, and each office has its own phone number, so choose before you dial. The Property Appraiser decides assessed value and takes care of exemptions, tangible property returns and the tax roll. Call (407) 742-5000, or use the website, which has a tax estimator and a homestead filing page. Notices, payments and the tax certificate process belong to the Tax Collector. Deeds and mortgages are filed with the clerk, who doubles as county recorder.

For the Tax Collector, dial 407-742-4000. Four offices keep weekday hours until 4:00 pm: the main office at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee, another at 2595 Simpson Road in Kissimmee, a St. Cloud office at 1300 9th Street, Suite 101B, and a Campbell City office at 4730 South Orange Blossom Trail. Appointments can be booked online.

  • Osceola County Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, millage page, tax estimator.
  • Osceola County Tax Collector: notices, payment, installment plan, certificates.
  • Osceola Clerk of Court and Comptroller: Official Records search, which includes a property fraud alert signup.

Tax calendar

Collection for the calendar-year assessment opens November 1. Notices usually reach the last address on the tax roll by that date. You can pay through March, and April 1 is the delinquency date.

Lenders that escrow your tax are expected to request the bill and send you a copy. The collector still treats it as your job to confirm the tax is paid and a bill was received.

Dates an Osceola County owner should know
DateWhat happens
January 1Assessment and valuation date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
March 31Gross amount due on real estate tax
April 1Unpaid real estate tax delinquent, 3 percent charge added; tangible personal property returns due
April 30Installment plan applications for next year due
By June 1Online sale of tax certificates
NovemberCollection opens, top discount through November 30

Early discounts and the installment plan

A November payment cuts the bill by 4 percent. The reduction shrinks by a point every month until it is 1 percent in February, and a March payment is the gross amount.

Prefer four smaller payments? Apply for the installment plan by April 30 of the year before the bill, and make the first payment by June 30. A July payment gives up the discount and carries a 5 percent late charge; if July 31 passes with nothing paid, the plan is cancelled. Two more installments are due September 30 and December 31.

Furniture, fixtures and equipment used in a business or rental, along with structural additions to mobile homes, are taxed on a separate tangible personal property bill. When the estimate tops $100.00, quarterly payment is allowed. Landlords selling a furnished rental should ask the appraiser about the April 1 return.

  • Both kinds of bill qualify for the early payment discounts.
  • Changes to a name, an address or an assessed value are made at the Property Appraiser, not the Tax Collector.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead for a seller or buyer

The application deadline with the Property Appraiser is March 1, and the benefit begins in the year you file. State materials describe a ceiling of $50,000 in two tiers; only the first tier applies to school taxes.

The appraiser's website includes a File Homestead page and a form for reporting exemption fraud, while the clerk runs a separate property fraud alert. Tell the appraiser when you sell. A sale or deed ends the capped assessment, and value resets on the following January 1. The buyer files a fresh application by March 1 if the house will be a residence.

Farmland holds its own classification, and Osceola's appraiser says that classification does not pass to a new owner. Someone buying pasture or grove land applies again in the January to March window, and classified parcels are re-inspected at least every three years.

What follows delinquency

The steps run in a set order. April 1 adds a 3 percent charge to unpaid tax. Advertising comes next, then the sale of a lien, and two years later the certificate holder may apply for a tax deed.

A local newspaper prints the delinquent list, in parcel order, three weeks in a row. On or before June 1 the collector auctions certificates online through LienHub. Bids start at 18 percent, and the investor willing to take the lowest rate wins. What that investor holds is a lien, not a deed, and it carries no right to enter your property.

You clear it by paying the certificate amount, interest at the sold rate and, from June 1 onward, a $6.25 redemption fee. Certificates that drew no bidder are offered afterward on LienHub. A certificate still outstanding on the second April 1 after the sale lets its holder request a tax deed, once other certificates on the parcel and the present year's tax are paid.

  • A certificate holder is barred from demanding payment from you in the first two years.
  • A lien does not block a sale; the closing pays it off.

Taxes and the deed at closing

At closing the tax lien is paid off first, and the deed is then entered in the Official Records. Florida charges documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of price on the deed, apart from Miami-Dade, where the rate differs. All signers of the deed share liability, and the clerk collects the tax when the deed is recorded.

Page-by-page recording charges are set by statute, with a modernization trust fund charge and a technology charge on top. The clerk also has a branch office in Poinciana.

Timing counts. November is when bills go out, so a closing earlier in the year happens before the new bill exists. Ask the closing agent how the year will be prorated, and file the Tax Collector's payoff letter with your closing papers. If a 10 percent non-homestead cap applied to your rental, expect the buyer's value to reset after the sale.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What a seller can do this month

Pull up the parcel on the appraiser's site and confirm the owner name and any exemption are right. Then look at the Tax Collector's account for the same parcel and note which years are paid. If there is a balance, phone 407-742-4000 and ask for the payoff in writing. Finally, put the payoff letter, your latest notice and a copy of the deed into one folder for the title agent.

Choosing between a regular listing and a cash sale does not change any of this. The tax lien rides with the parcel either way, and closing pays it from the proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

What is the delinquency date for Osceola County tax?

April 1. The Tax Collector adds a 3 percent charge to the gross amount that day, advertises the delinquent list, and runs an online lien auction by June 1.

What discounts does the Osceola County Tax Collector give?

Four percent off for November, then a point less each month through February. March brings no discount, and March 31 is the gross due date.

Where is the Osceola County Tax Collector?

The main office is at 2501 E. Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy in Kissimmee. Others sit on Simpson Road in Kissimmee, in St. Cloud and in Campbell City, all on the 407-742-4000 line.

How do I redeem an Osceola County tax certificate?

Pay the certificate amount plus interest at the rate it sold for, and a $6.25 fee when redeeming on or after June 1. Contact the Tax Collector for the exact payoff.

Does back tax stop me from selling in Osceola County?

No. The lien rides with the parcel and the payoff is deducted at closing. Before you sign, phone 407-742-4000 and ask the Tax Collector for the number.

  • Value, exemptions, name and address: Property Appraiser.
  • Bill, payment, delinquency, certificates: Tax Collector.
  • Appeals of assessments, denied exemptions and deferrals: Value Adjustment Board, made up of three county commissioners and two school board members or a special master.

Most seller questions can be settled with two calls. Ask the appraiser what the parcel is valued at and which exemptions it carries, then ask the collector what is owed and by when.

Payment schedule

Notices normally go out by November 1 for the calendar tax year, and the gross figure is due March 31. Each month you wait trims the discount by a point.

Discounts and penalties on real estate taxes
Month paidDiscount or penalty
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone
April 1 onwardDelinquent, 3% penalty; advertising fees added May 1

If a discount window ends on a weekend or legal holiday, it stays open until the next business day. Getting the bill is the owner's job, so call the collector if none arrives.

Delinquent taxes and certificates

A 3 percent penalty lands on April 1. After that date, only cashier's check, money order, cash or credit card is accepted. The amount you owe is fixed by the date the office actually receives your money.

Delinquent parcels are advertised for three weeks in a local paper, a job the county commission gives to the lowest bidder, and the cost is added to the delinquent bill. By June 1 the collector runs the certificate sale online through LienHub.com as a reverse auction. It opens at 18 percent interest and goes to the lowest bidder.

  • A certificate is a lien. Buying one gives the investor no ownership rights.
  • Costs jump at once when the county holds the certificate and someone buys it, or when a tax deed application is filed.
  • Years of nonpayment can end with the property being sold.

The investor has to wait two years from April 1 of the issue year before applying for a tax deed, and during the wait can't contact you to demand payment. Homestead parcels also carry an opening bid that includes half of the latest assessed value.

If you're selling in this position, ask for a fresh payoff statement. The total grows as costs are added.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead filing dates

The appraiser's posted dates give a homestead filing period of January 1, 2027 to March 1, 2027. The Persons 65 or Over and Deployed Service Member exemptions run January 1 to June 1, 2027.

You can file online. Search for your parcel on the appraiser's site and click Apply for Exemptions, after updating your Florida ID and vehicle registration to the home address. The ground rules: the home must be your permanent residence by January 1, and your filing must reach the appraiser by March 1. The first $25,000 counts against every levy. The additional amount reduces non-school levies only, on value above $50,000.

Florida lets a county or city add a senior exemption worth up to $50,000 by ordinance, within an income limit, plus a 25-year version for homes valued under $250,000. Ask the appraiser which Santa Rosa taxing authorities have enacted them. A $5,000 reduction is available to owners rated 10 percent or more for a service-connected disability.

What changes at a sale

A new buyer's parcel is reset to just value, and your exemptions leave when you do. The state reads change of ownership broadly. It covers a sale, a foreclosure and any transfer of legal or beneficial title, except where the same person stays entitled or the transfer goes to a spouse.

Watch for mail that offers a copy of your deed for a fee. The appraiser issues a Property Owner Protection Alert about these letters. The businesses sending them have no official role, and neither the Property Appraiser's office nor the Clerk of Courts took part. Skip the offer. If you need a copy of a recorded deed, ask the Clerk directly.

Deed stamps are $0.70 per $100 of price, and price includes any mortgage the buyer assumes. The Clerk collects at recording. A deed sale winner has to post a deposit equal to 5 percent of the bid, or $200 if that is larger.

Handling tax due at closing

Ask the closing agent to order a tax payoff and apply it at closing, so nothing is left on the parcel for the buyer. The collector's online parcel search shows the balance, and the Milton, Midway, Pace and Jay branches answer questions in person. With escrow, your loan servicer requests the bill, but you still want the payoff confirmed ahead of closing.

Know who answers what. Legal description, value, exemptions and name or address changes belong to the appraiser. Rates belong to the taxing authorities that hold advertised public hearings. Non-ad valorem charges typically cover fire departments, street lighting, paving and special local projects, so ask the agency named on the bill.

For a closer bill review, ask the appraiser how your assessed value compares with just value. That gap is the Save Our Homes benefit the buyer won't inherit. The state lists a 3.4% CPI for 2024 with a 3.0% cap, 2.9% for 2025 and 2.7% for 2026.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid tax bill is a problem to solve, not a barrier to selling. The balance is taken out of your proceeds at the closing table. A sensible order of steps:

  1. Call the collector for a current balance and, if anything is delinquent, a written payoff.
  2. Hand that number to the title company or closing agent.
  3. Check the appraiser's record for your exemption status and mailing address.
  4. Review the settlement statement to see the tax line and any proration before you sign.

A cash buyer can shorten the timeline because no lender is waiting on an appraisal, but the payoff and proration work the same way.

Think of the closing statement as your final tax audit. Match the tax line against the bill you printed, look for a proration credit that fits the date you hand over keys, and ask the closing agent to explain any figure that surprises you. Fixing a mistake before funding is far easier than chasing a refund afterward.

Bring a photo ID and your contract to any office visit, and write down the parcel number so staff can pull the right account quickly. Ask each office to confirm by email or letter whatever it tells you by phone, and keep those messages with your closing papers in case a question comes up later.

Frequently asked questions

What is the payment schedule?

The gross amount is due by March 31, with bills mailed on or before November 1. Payments in November earn 4%, December 3%, January 2% and February 1%.

What is the late penalty?

A 3 percent penalty is added on April 1 for unpaid real estate accounts. Advertising fees are added on May 1, and a tax certificate sale follows by June 1.

Where do I file homestead?

Use the Apply for Exemptions button on your parcel page at the appraiser's site. The posted homestead period for 2027 runs January 1 to March 1.

Who hears an assessment appeal?

That falls to the Value Adjustment Board, which also takes denied exemptions and tax deferral appeals. A value petition is due within 25 days after the TRIM notice.

Does the county sell my house when I miss a payment?

Not at first. What gets sold is a tax certificate, a lien that starts at 18 percent interest. Only a later tax deed application can lead to the property itself being sold.

St. Johns County housing market in brief

St. Johns grew from 190,039 people in 2010 to 273,425 in 2020 and an estimated 346,328 by mid-2025. Owners occupy 82.2 percent of the 115,794 households, and the midpoint owner home is valued at $489,200. Permits reached 4,735 in 2025, so a seller competes with plenty of new construction.

Owners with a mortgage report a median monthly cost of $2,351, against $728 for those without one. For a newer buyer, much of the carrying cost is the loan and not the tax, which is worth remembering when you talk about the bill.

Help for new owners from the property appraiser

The appraiser's new owner page gives buyers a short checklist: find the parcel's record card, complete the sales questionnaire, and verify the name and mailing address, because the TRIM notice and bill go to that address. A button on the record card estimates the tax bill.

  • Customer service: 904-827-5500.
  • Business equipment returns: 904-827-5508.
  • Building department: 904-827-6800.
  • Planning and zoning: 904-209-0675.
  • Utility department: 904-209-2700.

Owners also update a Florida driver license through the tax collector, a step that matters because the homestead application checks that the license shows the homestead address. New business owners may need a local business tax application and an account with the appraiser.

Key dates in the tax year

  • January 1: the property's status sets its value for the assessment year, and ownership and residence on this day decide homestead eligibility.
  • January 1 to April 1: business equipment returns are filed.
  • March 1: filing closes for homestead, other personal exemptions, classified use, agricultural classification and organizational exemptions.
  • August and September: TRIM notices go out with proposed assessments, millage and hearing dates.
  • November: the tax collector mails bills.

When March 1 lands on a weekend, the cutoff moves to the next business day.

Homestead exemption

For the 2026 tax year the exemption is $51,411, now indexed to inflation. A first block of $25,000 applies to every levy, school bills included. The remaining $26,411 applies to assessed value between $50,000 and $75,000 and leaves school tax untouched.

To qualify, you must be a Florida permanent resident who holds title and lives in the home on January 1. Neither spouse may claim a residency-based exemption in another state, and the office wants proof. Applicants bring a Florida license or ID showing the homestead address and Social Security numbers for both spouses, which are required for online filing. A noncitizen needs a Permanent Resident Card. If you owned a Florida home before, give its address or parcel number. If you close after January 1, that year's exemption is out of reach for the new owner's own claim, so the buyer files the following year.

Once approved, you need not reapply unless marital status, ownership or title changes. A late application for just cause can be filed through the end of the TRIM period, which usually falls late in August.

Renting a homestead, trusts and LLCs

Renting part of a home is fine. The portion you do not rent stays eligible, and a garage apartment or other separate rental space can be carved out while the rest keeps the exemption. Renting the whole property for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends the exemption, and a rental lasting over six months in a tax year is presumed commercial.

Ownership structure matters too. Property held in a trust qualifies if the applicant is the trustee or the trust language gives beneficial title. Moving the house into an LLC or another business entity counts as a change of ownership, which strips every exemption and cap. After a divorce or marriage, the appraiser may ask for a new application, and it sends notice when the deed is recorded in St. Johns County. If the deed is recorded elsewhere, you are responsible for telling the office.

Portability of your Save Our Homes benefit

Portability lets you carry the gap between market and assessed value, up to $500,000, from one Florida homestead to another. The move must happen within three tax years, counted January through December from the sale, and a December sale counts as one tax year.

Downsizing is allowed, and the transferable amount shrinks in proportion to the lower value of the new home. Everyone who owned the old home and owns the new one must apply together, and each spouse of a married couple counts. You can use portability any number of times but never from outside Florida. Spouses who abandon a jointly titled home may split the difference with Form DR-501TS, provided they were married on the abandonment date. The benefit total appears on the TRIM notice and the record card. Non-homestead property carries a separate 10 percent cap, and that benefit cannot be ported.

Other exemptions and the proof they need

All of these are due by March 1, and the office asks applicants to visit in person.

Selected personal exemptions
ExemptionAmountProof asked for
Age 65 or older, limited incomeUp to $50,000Form DR-501SC and prior year household income
Widowed$5,000Mark it on the homestead form or give the death certificate
Blind$5,000Form DR-416 or DR-416B, or SSDI proof
Totally and permanently disabled civilian$5,000Form DR-416 or SSDI letter
Veteran disabled 10 percent or more$5,000DD-214 and a VA disability letter
Combat-related disabled veteran, 65 or olderEqual to the disability ratingForm DR-501DV, DD-214, VA letter

The appraiser also lists total exemptions for quadriplegics, for certain permanent disabilities with limited income, for those totally and permanently disabled through service, for surviving spouses of those who died on active duty and for first responders disabled in the line of duty, plus a deployment exemption on Form DR-501M. Churches, schools, hospitals, nursing homes, affordable housing and historic buildings fall under property-use exemptions. With 22.5 percent of residents 65 or older, many sellers qualify for something here.

How to dispute a value

Start with a conversation at the appraiser's office. If that fails, a petition goes to the Value Adjustment Board. The TRIM notice goes out in mid-August, and you may file within 25 days of that mailing. The date is printed at the top of the notice.

The Clerk of the Circuit Court and County Comptroller manages the process and posts the petition form, at 904-819-3600. A denied exemption, classification or portability claim has its own 30 day window, so if you think the assessment is too high, act before you list the house.

Stamp tax, delinquency and closing payoffs

Stamp tax is seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price and binds every party named on the deed. The clerk charges $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each page after it. Debt that stays on the house is counted in the price.

Unpaid bills turn delinquent April 1, certificates are sold by June 1, and a holder may apply for a deed after two years, with half the latest assessed value added to the opening bid on homestead land. Ask the collector for a payoff and have the title company search for certificates.

On a cash sale the same payoffs apply, but there is no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait for, so closing can move as fast as the title work allows. Bring your deed, a recent tax bill and any payoff letters to the title company on day one.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the 2026 homestead exemption total in St. Johns County?

$51,411. The first $25,000 reaches all levies and $26,411 applies to value between $50,000 and $75,000, excluding school taxes.

Is the March 1 homestead deadline ever different?

Yes. When March 1 falls on a weekend, filing moves to the next business day.

Does a St. Johns County buyer keep the seller's capped value?

No. A sale resets the home to market value the next January 1. The seller may port up to $500,000 of the gap to a new Florida homestead within three tax years.

Can I rent my whole St. Johns County homestead for a few months?

Renting the entire home for more than 30 days in two consecutive tax years ends the exemption. A rental beyond six months in one year is presumed commercial.

Who runs the Value Adjustment Board paperwork?

The circuit clerk and comptroller, at 904-819-3600. A petition is due 25 days after TRIM notices are mailed.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

St. Lucie County at a glance

St. Lucie County counted 277,789 residents in 2010, 329,226 in 2020 and an estimated 402,449 by mid-2025. About 78.6 percent of homes are owner occupied, there are 137,453 households, and 24.9 percent of residents are 65 or older, so age-linked tax breaks reach many sellers here. Building permits totaled 4,008 in 2025, and 89.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which tells you most owners stay put once they buy.

Which office answers which tax question

The property appraiser's office, at 772-462-1000, splits its work across four departments: appraisal, mapping, tax roll and tangible property. It values parcels, tracks ownership changes, keeps boundary maps and grants exemptions. It does not set a rate. Elected county and city officials, the school board and districts for fire, roads, port, airport and water management do that.

The tax collector mails bills at the start of November and collects payment. Call 772-462-1650 for equipment tax questions. The Clerk of the Court records deeds and answers copy requests at 772-462-6900. The appraiser's real estate search shows a record card, a TRIM button and a map for each parcel, which is the fastest way to see what the county has on file before you list.

Reading your TRIM notice

Page one of the mid-August notice compares three scenarios, color coded. The orange column holds last year's values and budgets, for comparison only. The blue column shows this year's tax if every taxing body raised the same dollars it did before. The green column shows the tax at each body's proposed rate, which can still shift after public hearings.

Page two lists market value for both years, then assessed value, exemptions and taxable value per taxing authority. A gray band reports reductions such as the agricultural classification, the 3 percent or 10 percent cap and any portability benefit. The notice also prints the Value Adjustment Board deadline. It is an estimate and not a bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

From market value to taxable value

Five links turn a sale price into a tax figure.

  • Just market value: the price signal from sales before the January 1 assessment date.
  • Cap: a 3 percent limit on homestead growth and a 10 percent limit for other property.
  • Assessed value: just value minus the cap.
  • Exemptions: reductions for which the owner applied and qualified.
  • Taxable value: assessed value minus exemptions, which is the number each millage rate multiplies.

Some bill lines sit outside that chain. Non ad valorem charges pay for services like lighting, landscaping, security and trash, and they do not track the value of the home.

Why a bill jumps after a purchase

The previous owner's protections do not travel with the house. Each January 1 the property is reassessed, and a new owner receives market value with the old exemptions and capped amount erased. A neighbor's lower bill usually comes from a cap built up over years of homestead or from an extra exemption the neighbor holds.

The cap begins to accrue only after the first year of homestead, and only when market value is rising. If you are listing, warn buyers that the tax figure on a listing can understate what the next owner pays.

Homestead and the cap when a deed changes

Homestead cannot be handed over. A new application is needed whenever title changes or a new home is established. Adding a name to the deed normally leaves the exemption alone but can cost part of the cap, depending on the tenancy.

Adding an owner to the deed
How title is heldNew owner files homestead?What happens to the cap
Joint tenants with survivorshipYesResets to market value and restarts the next year
Joint tenantsNoLeft unchanged
Tenants in commonNoShrinks to the original owner's share; the other share is assessed at market, then under the 10 percent limit

Inheritance follows the same logic. An heir generally cannot keep the decedent's exemption or cap, which end with the year. Two exceptions let a cap continue: a surviving spouse who files for homestead, and a legally or naturally dependent person living in the house at the death who then files. Placing a home in a trust requires the beneficial interest language of s. 196.041 on the deed or in the trust pages, and the appraiser asks for the trust if the deed lacks it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Carrying your cap to a new house

Portability moves the accumulated gap between market and assessed value, up to $500,000, to a new Florida homestead. You need a homestead exemption on the old property in at least one of the three preceding tax years, and a new homestead established by January 1 within three tax years of abandoning the old one.

File with the new homestead application by March 1, at either office location or online. A former spouse sharing the old home must file the DR-501TS share designation first. A larger new house transfers the full amount, while a smaller one carries it over in proportion.

Payment dates and delinquency

The collector gives a 2 percent discount in January for real estate and equipment tax. November through February runs the usual 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent scale. For homestead tax deferral, call the collector for the current filing deadline.

An unpaid bill turns delinquent April 1, certificates are sold by June 1, and a holder may seek a deed two years after April 1 of the issue year. A title company will ask for a certificate search, so order one early. If a bill is open when you sell, the closing agent pays it from your proceeds, whether the buyer pays cash or uses a loan.

Equipment tax when a business changes hands

The tax follows the equipment, so buyer and seller should check balances before closing. Call the collector on 772-462-1650 to learn whether tangible personal property tax is unpaid, and ask the closing agent to prorate.

Returns are due April 1. Late filers pay 5 percent for each month or part of a month, a missing return draws 25 percent, and unreported assets can add 15 percent. There is no minimum value, and a landlord must report furniture and appliances supplied in a rental. A thirty day extension can be requested online before April 1 with written reasons. When a business closes, the owner files a final return and an account status change form.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Agricultural land after a sale

An agricultural classification does not transfer with the land, and applications are taken between January 1 and March 1. The classification lowers value, but it is not an exemption.

Use on January 1 controls the outcome, and the appraiser inspects. Evidence includes care of the land, income and expense records, a Schedule F or C, receipts for feed, seed or fertilizer, business plans and insurance. Land used mainly for residential, development or investment purposes is not eligible, and agricultural zoning does not create the classification. Owners must report any change in use or acreage or risk losing it.

Amendment 3 and look-alike mail

A proposed constitutional amendment, labeled Amendment 3 (CS/HJR 1F), appeared on the November 2026 general election ballot and needed at least 60 percent approval to take effect January 1, 2027. Call the appraiser for what it means for your homestead.

Watch for mail that looks like a bill. Letters from a county records office or property site are solicitations and not amounts due, and those companies have no tie to the county. A real deed copy comes from the clerk or from the parcel's record card.

Frequently asked questions

Is the TRIM notice a bill in St. Lucie County?

No. It is an estimate built from proposed rates, January 1 value and exemptions. The tax collector sends the actual bill at the beginning of November.

What is the usual homestead filing window in St. Lucie County?

January 1 through March 1. The appraiser also allows pre-filing for the following year at any time, and portability is filed alongside the homestead application.

Can a St. Lucie County heir keep a parent's capped value?

Generally no. A surviving spouse who files for homestead, or a dependent living in the house at the death who files, may keep it.

Who handles deed copies in St. Lucie County?

The Clerk of the Court, at 772-462-6900, or the parcel's record card on the appraiser's site. Mailed offers for copies are solicitations.

Does St. Lucie County have an early payment discount in January?

Yes, 2 percent. Call the collector for the current homestead tax deferral deadline.

Selling in a retirement-heavy county

Sumter County is older than almost any place a seller will meet. Residents 65 and up make up 57.6 percent of the population, and only 7.6 percent are under 18. The headcount reached an estimated 157,772 by mid-2025, a rise of 21.6 percent over the 2020 base of 129,752.

A household averages 1.93 people, and owners live in 87.6 percent of homes. The typical owned home is valued at $385,400, and owners paid a median $1,686 monthly with a mortgage against $602 without. Buyers here tend to ask hard questions about yearly carrying costs, so know your tax picture before you list. Permits totaled 3,516 in 2025, so a resale often sits next to new homes.

Which offices handle property tax

The appraiser values land and decides exemptions, while a separate collector sends the bills. The county's clerk of court also keeps the file for the Value Adjustment Board.

That board has five seats: two commissioners, one school board member, and two citizens, one named by each body. It hears appeals about value, classification and exemptions, leaves rates to the taxing authorities, and may not lower a value or give an exemption because of hardship. Qualified appraisers or attorneys serve as special magistrates, hear each petition and recommend a ruling.

Tax calendar

Sumter follows the statewide calendar. January 1 fixes the assessment, March 1 closes homestead and classification filing, and April 1 is for personal property returns.

August brings the proposed-tax notice and a 25-day clock to petition. A denied exemption or portability claim has its own 30-day clock from the date the letter was mailed. Bills show up in November with a sliding discount of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent through February, and April 1 marks delinquency.

Homestead and portability

Homestead reduces taxable value by as much as $50,000. The first $25,000 applies to school taxes and the rest does not. You must be living there on January 1, then apply on Form DR-501 at the appraiser's office.

After a sale the house is reassessed at market value, so the buyer's first full bill may far exceed yours. If you stay in Florida, you can carry up to $500,000 of capped difference to your next homestead if it is set up within three years, and Form DR-501T goes in with the application. Leaving the state forfeits it, because portability only links Florida homes.

Disputing a value without a lawyer

You can. The petition goes through the clerk, who also acts as clerk to the Value Adjustment Board, and a special magistrate hears the case. The magistrate is independent of the property appraiser, so you present evidence of value, such as recent comparable sales, repair estimates or errors in the property record.

The panel looks only at whether value, classification or exemption is right. A tight household budget does not move the outcome. If you have a contract pending, tell the title agent about any open petition so the closing statement handles the tax correctly.

Exemptions for older owners and service-connected disability

Many Sumter County sales touch age or military benefits. Counties and cities may adopt an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 for owners over 65 with limited income, and a larger one equal to assessed value for 25-year residents whose home is worth under $250,000.

  • Older owners with a lasting service-connected disability: discount matching the VA rating.
  • Former servicemembers rated 10 percent or more disabled: $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Total, permanent service-connected disability: possibly full relief on homestead.

Ask the Sumter County Property Appraiser which local ordinances add to this list and how a surviving spouse is treated.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The buyer's first bill versus yours

Expect a jump. You may have lived under the Save Our Homes limit, which holds yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the inflation change (2.7 percent for 2026). Once the deed records, the house is valued at market on the following January 1 and the limit starts over for the buyer.

A buyer who wants homestead also needs to apply by March 1, since the exemption is not automatic. Both sides gain from knowing this before closing, because the old bill on the listing sheet is a poor guide to the new one.

  • Your capped value does not transfer.
  • The buyer applies for homestead after taking title and living there on January 1.
  • If you move within Florida, you may port the savings.

What can cancel homestead before a sale

Three events end it: renting the home out, ceasing to use it as the permanent residence, or no longer being a Florida permanent resident.

If you move away before listing, speak with the appraiser about your status. One exception: a servicemember may rent out the homestead without abandoning the exemption. You and your listing agent should confirm the status before preparing the tax proration, and buyers should ask what exemptions the parcel carried last year.

Deed costs at closing

Stamp tax is seventy cents for each hundred dollars of price. A mortgage the buyer takes over is added to the price.

Everyone on the deed is liable, so let the contract say who funds it. The clerk bills $5.00 on page one and $4.00 afterward, plus add-ons. A probated estate gets relief because a personal representative's deed is not taxable. A family deed made only for estate planning gets none.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling a house with unpaid tax

Overdue taxes become certificates sold by June 1, and a holder can seek a deed after two years. At the clerk's tax deed auction the winner leaves 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and pays the balance in 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.

Paying at closing avoids all of it, and a title company will normally insist on that anyway. A homestead parcel is further protected, since its opening bid in a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value. Request a payoff and a certificate search before you sign a contract.

With a cash buyer, the same steps apply, but there is no lender to wait on, so the payoff letter and title search set the closing date. Bring your deed, latest tax bill and any HOA or lien paperwork to the first meeting.

Because so many Sumter owners are retirees, buyers often arrive with cash from a prior home sale and ask for quick possession. That can shorten the timeline, but it does not shorten the paperwork: the clerk still has to record the deed, and the appraiser still has to move the exemption off your name. Ask your closing agent to confirm that the tax proration, any open petition and the payoff for earlier years are all on the settlement statement before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

What share of Sumter County is 65 or older?

Over half, at 57.6 percent.

When is the Sumter County homestead deadline?

March 1, filed with the Sumter County Property Appraiser.

Who hears assessment appeals in Sumter County?

The Value Adjustment Board, an independent five-member panel, with hearings run by special magistrates. The clerk serves as its clerk.

Can the board cut a Sumter County value for hardship?

No. It cannot change an assessed value or grant an exemption or classification based on personal hardship.

Does a Sumter County seller pay a deed tax?

Yes: seventy cents per $100 of price, owed at the clerk's counter. The contract decides which party actually pays, and every signer stays liable to the state regardless.

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

Who bills and collects in Monroe County

In the Keys, valuation and collection sit in separate buildings. One elected office decides what a parcel is worth and who gets an exemption. Another prints the notices and takes the payments. A seller in Key West and a seller in Key Largo deal with the same two offices at different counters.

The sequence runs like this: the appraiser's January value, combined with millage from the commission and other taxing bodies, becomes the roll certified for collection. Notices go to the address of record on that roll. Escrow lenders request the bill themselves, so the owner may only receive a copy.

Under Statute 197.122, the owner is responsible for learning what is due and paying before delinquency, bill or no bill. A separate bill goes out for each parcel, matched to the way the deed is recorded, so an owner of two lots should expect two notices.

If a bill never arrives, do not wait. Call the collector, confirm the address of record, and ask for a reprinted statement. Late payment carries the same delinquency date whether or not you received the mailing.

Housing in the Keys at a glance

Monroe County had 80,406 residents in mid-2025 across 983.04 square miles of land. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $780,600, and 65.8 percent of the 56,009 housing units are lived in by their owners. Median rent is $1,999 a month. Seniors make up 27.2 percent of the county, so the senior and homestead programs below get heavy use.

Tax Collector offices

The tax collector runs five offices along the Keys, and each one handles property tax.

Monroe County Tax Collector offices that take property tax
OfficeStreet addressHours
Key West main office1200 Truman Ave, Ste 1018:00 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday to Friday
Marathon branch3015 Overseas Hwy8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday to Friday
Plantation Key branch88800 Overseas Hwy8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday to Friday
Key Largo branch101487 Overseas Hwy8:00 AM to 4:45 PM, Monday to Friday
Big Pine Key satellite247 Key Deer Blvd9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Tuesday to Thursday

Services and hours vary by location, so call before you drive. Mailed payments go to the post office box on the collector's property tax page, and overnight or priority mail goes to the Key West street address. For a missing bill, call (305) 295-5044.

How to prepare an appeal or correction

Start with the August proposed-tax notice. A value challenge uses a DR-486 petition that the clerk must receive within 25 days, so write the deadline on the notice the day it arrives.

A denied exemption has its own 30 day petition clock. Owners of furnished rentals or business equipment also file Form DR-405 by April 1.

  • Gather recent sales of similar properties on your island or key before you file.
  • Photograph any damage that existed on January 1, since value is set on that date.
  • Keep the notice and your filing receipt together.

You can also ask the appraiser for the comparable sales behind your value.

Bills, discounts and delinquency

Statements normally mail by November 1, and March is the last month at full price.

  • November: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent, and February brings 1 percent.
  • March: the gross amount, no discount.

On April 1 an unpaid account turns delinquent, and tax certificates are sold by June 1. Instead of a lump sum, owners can ask about a quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment plan or a homestead tax deferral program. The application date for these is May 1. Sellers who expect to close before the bill is issued should ask the title company how the estimate will be handled, and whether a holdback or a post-closing true-up is part of the contract.

Homestead and Save Our Homes in a Keys sale

A capped assessment belongs to the owner and ends when the house sells. With a typical owned home valued at $780,600, the distance between a long-held capped value and a fresh assessment can be wide.

The exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value if filed by March 1. Yearly growth in assessed value is held below the lesser of 3 percent or CPI, which the state chart pegs at 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale, the next January 1 assessment starts from just value for the new owner. If you are buying again in Florida, ask the appraiser about portability, which has a three year window.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Other exemptions

With a large senior population, relief tied to age and military service comes up often. The state offers a $5,000 assessed value reduction for a disabled ex-servicemember, a homestead discount for qualifying veteran owners 65 and older, and a possible total exemption for permanent and total disability.

Seniors may also benefit from an optional local ordinance. Ask the property appraiser whether Monroe County or a city in it has adopted one, and what income limit applies.

Taxes and deed costs at a Keys closing

The title company usually divides the sale year's tax between the parties on the settlement statement. A spring or summer closing happens before that year's bill exists, so the figure is an estimate.

Keys deeds carry state stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of price (section 201.02), unlike Miami-Dade. Payment goes to the clerk, whose recording charges under section 28.24 start at $5.00 for the first page.

Unpaid taxes lead to a certificate sale and, years later, a clerk-run deed auction. Pay off any open year before closing.

On closing day, expect the title company to confirm payoffs, collect your signature on the deed in front of a notary and witnesses, and send the deed to the clerk for recording. Keep a copy of the settlement statement for your own tax records.

Getting ready to list a Keys home

A few routine steps help. Pull the parcel record and check the owner name and mailing address. Collect the last statement for each parcel you own, since a two-lot sale involves two bills. Ask the collector's office for a payoff on any open year, and ask your title company for a proration estimate. If you rented the home furnished, confirm whether a business equipment return is outstanding. Write down every phone number and name of the office you spoke with, along with the date. Share the paperwork with your closing agent early so the settlement statement holds no surprises.

A buyer who pays cash can skip lender requirements, but the same taxes, liens and recorded documents still have to be sorted out before the deed is recorded.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When does the Monroe County bill stop being penalty free?

Pay by March 31. That is when the gross amount falls due, and April 1 starts delinquency. Earlier payment, November through February, shrinks the bill by 4, 3, 2 or 1 percent.

Who answers questions about a lost Monroe County bill?

The tax collector, at (305) 295-5044. Each parcel gets its own bill, matched to the deed as recorded.

Does a Keys homeowner's capped value go to the buyer?

No. The buyer's first assessment starts at just value. You may be able to carry part of the savings to your next Florida homestead through portability.

Can I pay Monroe County taxes in installments?

Yes, through the tax collector's quarterly installment plan, a statutory partial payment option or a homestead deferral. State guidance sets May 1 as the application date.

Who runs a tax deed auction in Monroe County?

The county clerk holds the auction, so overbid or surplus questions go to the clerk.

Newcomers arrive often, and many ask about new construction, district fees and what their own bill will look like. Ask the property appraiser how your parcel's assessed value compares with its just value, since that gap is what a sale erases.

Estimating a bill for a buyer

The tax collector advises buyers never to treat a seller's past or current tax amount as a forecast. A new owner does not inherit the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions.

The property appraiser can help estimate upcoming taxes, but that office cannot see non-ad valorem assessments such as community development district fees. Those fees are added to the bill separately, and the estimate has to come from the district itself. If your neighborhood sits inside a district, tell the buyer so the closing numbers include it.

Setting expectations early helps. A buyer reading your old bill may expect a lower figure than reality, and a clear note about reassessment avoids a surprise at the table.

Bill dates and the discount schedule

Payment runs on a sliding monthly discount that ends March 31. Anything left unpaid becomes delinquent April 1.

  • November payment: 4 percent off.
  • December: 3 percent.
  • January: 2 percent.
  • February: 1 percent.

Florida's revenue department places the notice of proposed taxes in August, public budget hearings in September and October, and tax bills in November. A value challenge goes to the clerk's value adjustment board petition process within 25 days of the notice. For questions about a bill, call the tax collector's tax department at 904-491-7420.

What to tell a buyer about the tax bill

Give the buyer the parcel's real situation, not a rule of thumb. A clear explanation protects both sides before a contract is signed.

  • Say whether a homestead exemption and a capped value are on the roll today, and that neither carries over.
  • Name any community development district or other non-ad valorem assessment, and give the buyer the district's contact so the buyer can ask for the amount.
  • Explain whether taxes are escrowed. If a lender pays, partial payments are discouraged and the lender sets the timing.
  • Mention any unpaid prior year, since the lien follows the land.

A buyer who learns these things at the start is less likely to ask for a credit late in the deal. A plain written summary, with a printout from the appraiser's estimate tool, makes closing day smoother. The appraiser's estimate will leave out district fees, so ask the title company to add them.

Exemptions and capped values

Exemptions come from the property appraiser, who takes applications each year. About 26.7 percent of residents are 65 or older, so the senior programs see steady use.

A county or city may adopt an extra senior exemption within an income limit, and another ordinance may help long-term residents with lower-value homes. Ask the property appraiser which of these apply in Nassau County or its towns.

  • A $5,000 reduction in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember.
  • A homestead discount for veteran owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A possible full homestead exemption for total and permanent disability.

A rented unit cannot keep homestead, so a landlord selling a former residence should confirm what is on the roll.

Partial payments

Partial payment is allowed on a current-year bill under section 197.374. The office accepts payments from November 1 through March 31, with the postmark counting. The costs are real.

  • The account loses the early-payment discount, even if the balance is later cleared in a discount month.
  • Escrowed accounts paid by a lender should not make partial payments.
  • Accounts on an installment plan should skip partial payments.
  • Whatever is unpaid on April 1 enters the delinquent process of advertising and a certificate sale.

To set one up, contact the tax department at 904-491-7420 or taxes@nassautaxes.com. Payments can then be made in person, by mail or online.

Unpaid taxes and tax certificates

The tax collector must hold a certificate sale on or before June 1, conducted online on the LienHub platform.

Nassau tax certificate terms
TermRule
Sale deadlineOn or before June 1 each year

Lien statusEnforceable first lien on the real estate
ValiditySeven years from issuance
Tax deed applicationAfter two or more years of delinquency

To remove the lien, the owner pays the collector all delinquent tax plus interest, costs and other charges. A certificate holder cannot demand payment from the owner for two years after April 1 of the issuance year, and a deed application carries a $75 fee. Homestead land with a small delinquency goes to the county rather than to a bidder.

If you are behind, call the tax department before the June sale. Paying early limits the added costs, and a title company can pay the full amount from your sale proceeds at closing.

Homestead rules and deed taxes in a sale

The standard exemption takes up to $50,000 off taxable value and is filed by March 1. Capped assessment growth was 2.7 percent for 2026. A buyer's value starts over after a sale.

Deed stamps follow section 201.02 at 70 cents on every $100 of price. Liability sits with all parties to the deed, and payment goes to the clerk at recording.

Steps before you accept an offer

Check the parcel record for the right owner name and mailing address. Ask the tax department whether any year is unpaid and request a written payoff. Find out whether a district assessment applies, and ask the district for its current amount. Ask the title company how the sale year's taxes will be prorated, then confirm the plan in the contract.

A cash buyer who takes the house as is can skip lender timelines, but unpaid taxes, district fees and recorded liens are still settled from the sale proceeds before the deed is recorded. Keep your closing statement and the paid receipts together, since a later question about the sale year's bill is easier to answer with them in hand.

Frequently asked questions

Does a new Nassau County owner get the seller's tax amount?

No. The buyer does not benefit from the prior owner's assessed value, Save Our Homes cap or exemptions, so past bills are not a safe estimate.

Do community development district fees show on the appraiser's estimate?

No. The appraiser cannot see non-ad valorem assessments, so ask the district for its amount, which is then added to the tax bill.

Do I lose the discount if I make a partial payment in Nassau County?

Yes. The account is no longer eligible for discount even if the rest is paid during a discount month. Partial payments run November 1 through March 31.

When does Nassau County sell tax certificates?

The sale is held by June 1 each year on the LienHub site. Bids start at 18 percent and fall, and the lowest rate takes the certificate.

How long before a tax deed can be sought on a Nassau County parcel?

The certificate holder may apply once two or more years of delinquency have run. Until then, the owner can redeem by paying taxes, interest, costs and charges.

Which office handles what

Two offices matter here. Values and exemption filings sit with the property appraiser, while billing and payment sit with the tax collector. The collector runs three branches: the DeFuniak Springs courthouse for north Walton, the Santa Rosa Beach courthouse annex for south Walton, and a Freeport office. The mailing address is a post office box in DeFuniak Springs. Branches are open weekdays into late afternoon, with a slightly later Wednesday start.

Call the appraiser about the estimated tax shown on a TRIM notice, and the collector about what you owe or what is late. The county runs from the Gulf shore to the inland towns, so you may be a long drive from the right counter. The online parcel search and payment page spare you that trip.

Walton County property tax calendar

The collector posts a month-by-month schedule. Here are the entries a home seller will care about.

Walton County real estate tax calendar
MonthWhat is due or happens

December3% discount; third installment due the 31st
January2% discount

June and SeptemberInstallments one (June 30) and two (September 30)

The property appraiser mails the TRIM notice in August.

Installment plan

Owners who dislike one big bill can spread it over four payments, and the first three carry a discount.

  • Sign up by April 30 for the coming year.
  • Last year's tax must have topped $100.00, and the bill cannot go through an escrow account.
  • June 30 brings the first installment with a 6% discount, September 30 the second at 4.5%, December 31 the third at 3%, and March 31 the fourth with no discount.
  • Payments one and two are each a quarter of last year's tax.
  • Skip the first payment and you are dropped from the plan for that year.

Once enrolled, you stay on without filing again. If you are selling mid-plan, ask the collector what remains after each payment, because the later installments are trued up once the roll is final.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens when taxes go delinquent

Real estate tax still open on April 1 turns delinquent, and the collector adds a 3% charge to the gross figure. Business equipment is treated differently and gathers 1.5% interest each month.

Next, the delinquent list appears in the DeFuniak Herald three weeks running, and an advertising and auction fee lands on your account. The certificate sale follows, scheduled by June 1 as an online auction at lienhub.com/county/walton. Bidders begin at 18% and go down in quarter-percent steps, and a 5% minimum interest applies unless someone bids zero. A certificate stays alive for seven years.

A holder who has sat on the certificate for two years after the April 1 delinquency date may ask for a tax deed. The Clerk of Court schedules those sales, which run online at walton.realforeclose.com, and you can still redeem right up until the clerk signs the deed. Accepted payment types are cash, cashier's check, money order and card, and cards add a convenience fee.

Exemptions and the March 1 filing date

A homestead exemption belongs to the person, not the house. Once you sell, it ends, and the new owner files separately with the property appraiser by March 1.

Homestead is worth up to $50,000 off taxable value. The first $25,000 reduces every levy, while a second amount reduces only non-school levies on value above $50,000. Renting the home out or moving away forfeits it.

The tax collector also has a page on military property taxes. Servicemembers who rent out a homestead are covered by a separate state provision, so ask the collector whether it applies.

Who pays the taxes when a Walton County home sells?

Your sales contract sets the split. Most Florida deals prorate taxes through the closing date, with the title agent pulling the current balance and any certificate from the collector and charging it to the seller's column.

Deed stamps are collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded, at 70 cents per $100 of the price, and each party on the document can be held liable no matter who agreed to pay. Recording charges start at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, plus a few extra per-page fees.

If the house carries a certificate, redeem it at or before closing. A buyer who spots a certificate more than two years old should ask the Clerk of Court if someone has applied for a tax deed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling when taxes are unpaid

Start with a call to the tax collector, since the price of waiting climbs monthly. Closing before April sidesteps the 3% charge and advertising fee. Closing after the certificate sale means interest and extra fees on top.

  • Search the parcel on the tax collector's payment portal for the current balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate exists and what rate it sold at.
  • Check homestead status with the property appraiser before March 1.
  • Tell the title company so the payoff is ordered ahead of the closing date.

A cash buyer can close on a short timeline, but the payoff letter still has to be in hand before the closing date.

Business personal property tax

Equipment used in a business is taxed on its own account and punished faster than land and buildings. After April 1 the unpaid amount grows by 1.5% every month.

Roughly 45 days past the March 31 deadline, the newspaper carries the delinquent accounts at the owner's expense. One list runs in May, and warrants start June 1. If you own a rental with furnishings or tools inside, ask the collector whether an equipment account is filed under your name.

  • The early-payment discounts mirror real estate at 4%, 3%, 2% and 1%, November through February.
  • Late real estate takes one flat 3% hit rather than monthly interest.
  • The two kinds follow separate advertising rules, so confirm which list you are on.

What does a certificate holder have to wait for?

Someone who buys your certificate gets a lien, not the house, and faces a slow clock. The paper lasts seven years. A deed application cannot be filed until two years after April 1 of the delinquent year, and state law bars the investor from chasing you for money in those first two years.

That gap gives you room to sell. A common route is to list the home, line up a buyer, and have the closing agent pay off the certificate out of your proceeds. Request the redemption total for your planned closing day, since the interest figure moves each month.

Frequently asked questions

When do Walton County property taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Unpaid real estate tax is delinquent on that date and a 3% charge is added to the gross amount.

What is the Walton County installment plan discount?

6% on the first installment, 4.5% on the second, 3% on the third and none on the fourth. Applications are due April 30.

Where does Walton County hold its tax certificate sale?

Online, at lienhub.com/county/walton, on or before June 1. Bidding starts at 18% and goes down in quarter-percent steps.

Can I still keep my house after a Walton County tax certificate is sold?

Yes. The owner may redeem until the Clerk of Court signs the tax deed. A tax deed application cannot be filed until two years after the April 1 delinquency date.

When is the Walton County exemption deadline?

March 1. Exemptions are due to the Property Appraiser's Office by that date.

Putnam County offices

Two offices handle your tax life, and they do different jobs. The appraiser decides what the house is worth and who gets an exemption. The collector mails the bill, takes payment and distributes the revenue. If a name, address or assessed value is wrong on the roll, go to the appraiser, not the collector.

The appraiser's main office is at 312 Oak Street in Palatka, with a mailing box at PO Box 1920, Palatka, FL 32178. Satellite offices in Crescent City (Mondays and Wednesdays) and Interlachen (Tuesdays and Thursdays) keep set days. The exemption department's number is (386) 329-0286. Property tax pages for the collector are at putnamtax.com, and tax certificate sales run through an online bidding site.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, tangible personal property, roll corrections.
  • Tax Collector: bills, discounts, installments, delinquent taxes and certificates.
  • Clerk of the Court: tax deed sales and recorded deeds.

Which taxing authorities send charges?

One Putnam bill can combine lines from the county, a fire district, the school board, two water management districts and one of five municipalities. The collector's website gives a phone number for each, so you can ask the right office about its rate.

The roster: the county, the Fire MSTU District, the Putnam County School Board, the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee Water Management District, the City of Palatka, the City of Crescent City, and the Towns of Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka. A parcel inside a city pays that city's levy on top of the county's.

Non-ad valorem charges ride beside the tax lines. The county added a solid waste assessment on residential units, divided among landfill improvements, garbage collection and recycling. Commissioners have also approved 28 separate MSBU projects for road maintenance or paving, which charge only the parcels that benefit. The Hastings Drainage District has its own assessment. Homestead doesn't reduce any of these, and a buyer will see them on the bill.

Payment schedule and discounts

Assessments are pegged to January 1 and collection typically begins November 1. Pay the gross figure by March 31 or the real estate account is delinquent from April 1.

Early payment discounts on current real estate taxes
Payment monthDiscount
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%
MarchNone, gross amount due

Owners with an estimated bill above $100 can use a quarterly installment plan. Your application must be in the office by April 30 ahead of the first payment year. Payments come due June 30 (6% discount), September 30 (4.5%), December 31 (3%) and March 31 (no discount). Miss the June payment and the account drops out of the plan until the next year, when you apply again. The first two payments are based on the prior year's taxes and the last two on the new roll.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Unpaid taxes and tax certificates

Delinquent parcels are advertised in a local newspaper three weeks running, and a certificate sale is held online by June 1. A certificate is a lien. It doesn't hand over the house.

Bidding opens at 18% and falls in quarter percent steps, and the lowest bidder gets the certificate. Owners who redeem afterward can owe interest of up to 18% a year, depending on the winning bid rate. After delinquency the office accepts cashier's check, certified check, cash or money order, and the amount due is set by the day it receives your payment.

  • If taxes stay unpaid two years from April 1, the certificate holder can usually file a tax deed application.
  • Applications run through RealTDA, and the county keeps a Lands Available for Taxes list of parcels that drew no bidder.
  • Paying the taxes cancels the lien, but every payment after delinquency must be in certified funds.

Selling a house that carries a certificate? Get a redemption quote from the collector and give it to the closing agent early. Interest keeps accruing until the lien is cleared.

Homestead and senior exemptions

Homestead removes the first $25,000 of value from every ad valorem levy. It leaves special assessments alone. The Palatka office takes applications all year, and the satellite offices help during the first two months of the year.

Exemption applications are due March 1, counted from the year after you buy. Later filers also have to complete an Extenuating Circumstances form. On the assessment date you need title in your name, Florida permanent residency and the house serving as your primary home. Proof includes a Florida driver license or ID with the home address, and a Florida vehicle registration. Trust-owned homes get a closer review.

  • Low income senior exemption: a county ordinance adds $25,000 against the county general millage for homeowners 65 and over under the income limit. Ask the office for the current limit.
  • Super Senior exemption: for 25-year residents with a just value under $250,000, it exempts the whole assessed value where a taxing authority has enacted it. Putnam County, Palatka, Crescent City, Interlachen, Pomona Park and Welaka have.
  • Deployed service member, total and permanent disability and first responder exemptions, each with its own proof requirements.

An approved exemption renews by itself, but you must report a change in use or status right away.

How a sale changes the next bill

The buyer's first roll starts at just value, and any exemption you held stays behind. Florida treats a sale, foreclosure or title transfer as a change of ownership. Spouses and certain transfers at death are exceptions.

A house one family has held for years may carry a bill that looks small next to what the new owner sees on the first full roll. The assessment cap, set at 2.7% on the state's 2026 chart, applies only while the same owner keeps the homestead. If you're moving within Florida, the portability form can carry up to $500,000 of your accrued benefit to the new homestead, filed with the exemption application by March 1.

Deed stamps cost $0.70 per $100 of price and are paid through the Clerk when the deed records. The contract may shift the cost to one party, but anyone named on the deed remains liable.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Seller checklist

Before you list, confirm three things: the current bill is paid or will be settled at closing, no tax certificate is outstanding, and the exemption record matches how you use the house. Renting the house out, or moving away, ends homestead.

Both offices are in Palatka and the roll is public. Print the parcel record and the bill and hand both to the closing agent. Ask whether any MSBU road assessment or solid waste charge is unpaid, since those ride on the same bill as the taxes.

Collect this paperwork now, before offers arrive:

  1. The latest tax bill with proof it was paid.
  2. Any exemption approval letters.
  3. Payoff statements for a mortgage, a lien or a certificate.
  4. Notes on assessments that will carry over to the buyer.

With a cash buyer, the same payoff and proration steps happen at closing, just with fewer lender conditions in the way.

Frequently asked questions

How much can I save by paying early?

The discount is 4% for November and drops a point each month through February. March carries none. Bills open for collection November 1.

When do Putnam County taxes become delinquent?

April 1. Anything unpaid after March 31 is delinquent the next day and heads for a certificate sale by June 1.

Is there a payment plan?

Yes. The quarterly plan needs an application in by April 30 and an estimated bill over $100. Its first three payments carry 6%, 4.5% and 3% discounts.

Where do I file for homestead?

File with the Property Appraiser in Palatka, or at the Crescent City or Interlachen satellite office during the winter filing season. The cutoff is March 1 after you buy.

Can I lose my house over unpaid taxes?

Eventually, yes. After two years a certificate holder may seek a tax deed and the house can go to auction. Paying the full amount before the sale keeps it yours.

Levy County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Last updated November 14, 2026.
