Where to pay and ask questions

Levy County owners pay at the Tax Collector's main office in Bronson, 310 School Street, Suite 102 (352-486-5172), or at one of two branches. Valuation is handled by the Property Appraiser, whose office is also in Bronson, at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 4:30.
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

No address change can be made at the collector's counter, whether the account is real property or tangible. Those go through the appraiser. A seller should update the mailing address there so a stray bill reaches the right person after closing.

Property tax dates in Levy County

Bills are due November 1, and a balance still open after March 31 becomes delinquent on April 1. The state discount starts at 4 percent in November and shrinks one point a month to 1 percent in February.

Reminder letters on unpaid accounts are sent by April 30. The delinquent list is prepared in May for the newspaper and the web, and the certificate auction usually runs by May 31. Chapter 197 requires it to start no later than June 1.

The earlier part of the year follows a fixed state calendar too: value is set as of January 1, exemption filings are due by March 1, a proposed-tax notice arrives in August, and a petition on value must be filed within 25 days of that notice.

Paying online or at the counter

Card payments online carry a fee and e-checks do not. The collector's site shows 2.3 percent on credit cards, a flat $1.75 for charges under $76, and nothing for an online e-check (ACH). The processor keeps those fees, not the county.

At the counter, each payment draws 2.3 percent and e-checks are unavailable. A payment processed after 11:59 p.m. counts as the next calendar day, which can trap someone near a deadline. A seller who wants a clean payoff can use an online e-check before midnight and avoid both the fee and the next-day rule.

Accepted cards are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. If the system gives trouble, call 352-486-5172 on a weekday.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?

Delinquent tax is sold as a certificate, which is a lien on the property rather than a transfer of the house. Its face amount adds up the unpaid tax, 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent collector commission, the advertising charge and the cost of the sale.

Levy County tax certificate terms
Certificate termRule
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list runs weekly for three weeks before the auction. A certificate buyer must wait two years, counted from April 1 of the issuance year, before reaching out to the owner.

Tax deed applications

Someone applying for a tax deed has to complete these steps, and the fee amounts can change without notice:

  • File a signed tax deed application.
  • Redeem any other outstanding certificates and pay current tax if owed.
  • Pay a $150 title search fee and a $75 application fee.

The county clerk then schedules the sale and charges for advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

When homestead is on the current roll, the opening bid adds half the assessed value to the taxes and costs. A parcel that draws no bids can join the list of lands available for taxes, and land left unsold there for 3 years reverts to Levy County. Unpaid government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

For an owner planning to sell, timing is what counts. Ask the collector for a payoff on any certificate before you list, because a title company will want every lien cleared at closing.

Agricultural classification when you sell

Farm classification belongs to the owner, not the land. The appraiser calls it non-transferable, so a buyer files a new application after any sale or transfer.

Filing runs January 1 through March 1. Under the statute the office cites, only land used mainly for bona fide agriculture, meaning good-faith commercial use, qualifies. Zoning alone earns nothing, and the use should be in place on the January 1 assessment date, or a reasonable effort to start it must have been made.

If you are selling acreage, tell the buyer which parcels carry the classification today. A buyer who fails to qualify can face a higher assessment. Denials are mailed to the applicant, who can ask the appraiser to talk it through.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How the certificate auction works for bidders

The sale is online through West Florida Business Systems, and the Tax Collector says no deposit is needed under the current format. Each bidder submits a Participating Bidder Agreement after registering or logging in, plus an electronic W-9 every year.

A practice system lets new bidders try things out, and bids made there do not carry to the live sale. A certificate can be resold to another buyer once the endorsement form and a $2.25 transfer fee per certificate reach the Tax Collector. The office cautions that a certificate is not a guaranteed investment, and one left without action through its seven-year life while the tax stays unpaid is cancelled. For you as the owner, the point is that a private investor holds the lien, cannot contact you for the first two years, and may then apply for a deed.

Levy County in brief

Levy County is rural, with about 48,520 residents across 1,118 square miles, up 13.1 percent since the 2020 count. Of 22,192 housing units, 81.4 percent are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied value is $190,600. Long tenure is common, which usually means a Save Our Homes assessment below market value that resets after a sale.

A Levy County deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax. The clerk collects it at recording from whichever party the contract assigns, and every party stays liable.

Steps before selling with taxes owed

  1. Call the collector for a current account balance and any certificate payoff.
  2. Confirm the mailing address with the appraiser.
  3. If the land is farmed, list which parcels carry agricultural classification.
  4. Give the closing agent the payoff letters so liens are cleared from your proceeds.

A cash buyer can close faster, but title work still turns up unpaid tax, so the payoff comes first either way.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?

The main office is at 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson. Branches are at 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, and 226 North Main Street, Chiefland. All keep weekday hours.

Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?

Cards add 2.3 percent, or a flat $1.75 under $76, paid to the processor. Online e-checks are free, while payments at the office add 2.3 percent.

When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?

On April 1 after the bill year. Reminders go out by April 30, and the certificate auction normally wraps up by May 31.

Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?

No. It is non-transferable, so the buyer files a new application by March 1 and must meet the bona fide agriculture test.

How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?

A certificate holder may apply two years after April 1 of the issuance year. If your parcel has a certificate, ask the collector for a payoff figure.

Flagler County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Flagler County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Flagler County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Flagler County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Flagler County property tax?
We buy Flagler County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Who does what in Flagler County

Value is the Property Appraiser's job. Notices and payments belong to the Tax Collector. The rates come from whichever bodies levy on your parcel, among them the county commission, the school board and each city commission. If a deed needs recording or a parcel is headed to auction, that is the circuit court clerk.

At flaglertax.gov you will find pages for property taxes, tangible personal property, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. Anything about a value, exemption or classification goes to the Flagler County Property Appraiser, who can give you current forms and filing dates.

How the bill is built and mailed

Taxes here are billed in arrears. The tax year is the calendar year, and the bills for real estate and for tangible personal property are mailed October 31, with payment opening November 1.

Behind that mailing is a fixed sequence:

  • The appraiser finishes the roll by assigning values and applying exemptions.
  • That certified roll is handed to the Tax Collector.
  • Flat non-ad valorem assessments, which have nothing to do with value, are merged in and print on the same notice.
  • The finished notice is mailed to the last address the roll holds for you.

If a servicer pays from escrow, it requests the bill under the Tax Collector's criteria, and your copy is only for your information.

Rentals and other accounts

The real estate bill is not the only account the Tax Collector keeps. Landlords and anyone selling business property should know about these.

  • Tangible personal property tax, charged on furnishings and equipment that a rental or business uses.
  • Tourist development tax, owed on short stays in a rental.
  • Business tax receipts for operating a business in the county.
  • Online payment of tax bills.

Winding down a rental? Have the office confirm each account is paid and closed. A leftover balance can surface well after the deed is recorded.

Pay through the official online payment page, not a link that arrives by text or email, since fraudulent texts have circulated.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

If a bill never arrives

A missing bill does not excuse the tax. Under section 197.122, which the Tax Collector cites, the owner is expected to learn what is due and pay before delinquency.

People who have moved out, landlords whose tenants pick up the mail and heirs at a house with an old address are the ones caught most often. Lobbies may close at 4 p.m. when crowded. If November ends with nothing in your mailbox, look up the account online and give the Property Appraiser a current mailing address.

The Flagler tax year at a glance

Florida's statewide calendar governs here, and Flagler's offices carry out each step.

Annual property tax dates
DateStep
January 1Property is assessed as of this day
March 1Exemption filings due
April 1Business and rental equipment returns
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition window
September and OctoberMillage hearings
NovemberBills and early-payment discount
April 1 followingDelinquent

Pay in November and the discount is 4 percent; it drops a point each month until it reaches 1 percent in February.

Installments and deferral

You can ask for either one, and both requests go to the Tax Collector. For installments the date is May 1 of the assessment year. For deferral you file Form DR-570 by March 31 of the following year.

A homestead owner who defers puts off whatever part of the tax exceeds a slice of household income, 5 percent for most people and 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. The Tax Collector may or may not take partial payments ahead of delinquency; that is its call. The May installment date falls long before any bill is mailed, so phone the office and learn how Flagler handles its plan before you build around it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Does the assessment cap follow the house?

No. Your buyer is assessed at full just value. Title changes reset a parcel the following January, spousal transfers being among the exceptions, so the capped figure you enjoyed does not pass on.

As long as you keep the homestead, assessed value can climb each year only by 3 percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is smaller; the 2026 figure on the state chart is 2.7 percent. Should you buy another Florida home, part of that savings can be ported if you claim it within three years. The homestead and portability forms both go to the Property Appraiser by March 1.

Veteran exemptions

The Tax Collector's site has a veteran benefits page, but the Property Appraiser handles the exemptions themselves. Florida's list is short.

  • $5,000 off assessed value for a disabled former servicemember whose rating is 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount that follows the VA rating, for an owner 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • An exemption based on deployment, claimed on Form DR-501M.

Find out from the Property Appraiser what proof each one needs, and carry your discharge or VA rating papers when you go.

When a parcel reaches a tax deed auction

Two years after a certificate is issued, the holder can apply for a deed and the clerk puts the parcel up at public auction. The Tax Collector compiles whom to notify: the titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the party assessed and any recorded contract buyer.

  • Whoever bids highest puts down a deposit that cannot be refunded, the greater of 5 percent of the bid or $200.
  • Everything else, including stamps and recording costs, is owed inside 24 hours, weekends and holidays excluded.
  • If nobody buys the parcel, it lands on the county's lands-available list.

Selling ahead of the auction lets you redeem out of the proceeds. The redemption figure keeps growing with interest, so ask the Flagler Tax Collector for a current one.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Taxes at closing

Whatever is owed on the parcel comes out of your sale proceeds, handled by the closing agent. Request the balance from the Tax Collector's office. Deed stamps are collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded, at 70 cents per $100 of price statewide.

A certificate on the parcel does not block a sale. It simply gets paid off at the table so the buyer ends up with clean title.

A few days before closing, give the title agent your ID, deed and latest tax bill. Then ask to see a draft settlement statement and make sure its tax line matches the figure the collector quoted for the payment date. When April 1 is close, a cash buyer who skips lender delays can be a real help.

Frequently asked questions

When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?

Right around the start of November. The mailing date for real estate and tangible personal property bills is October 31, and you can start paying November 1.

What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?

Yes, the tax is still owed. Section 197.122 leaves it to the owner to find the amount and pay before delinquency, so call the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

Can I defer Flagler County property tax?

If you have a homestead, apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. What can be deferred is the tax over 5 percent of household income, or over 3 percent if you are a permanent resident 65 or older.

Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?

No, a sale puts the property back at just value on the next January 1. Part of your cap may be portable to a new Florida homestead.

Who sets Flagler County millage rates?

Each levying body sets its own: the county, the school board, the cities and other authorities. The Property Appraiser deals only with value.

Highlands County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Highlands County, FL Property Tax Guide: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Highlands County, FL Property Tax Guide sale
  • Turn the Highlands County, FL Property Tax Guide offer down and you owe us nothing

Owe Highlands County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Highlands County property tax?
We buy Highlands County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Highlands County context for sellers

Highlands County is large and mostly rural, with about 113,000 parcels on the roll and more than 24,000 homestead exemptions in force. Farmland, groves and pasture make up much of the acreage, so a parcel with agricultural use gets treated differently from a house on a town lot. The tax collector serves residents from offices in Sebring and Avon Park, and the Highlands County Tax Collector site carries the payment pages and deadline lists referred to below.

When is Highlands County property tax due?

The collector mails bills by October 31 and starts taking payment in November. The whole amount is due by March 31, and an account that is unpaid or lacks a March 31 postmark turns delinquent on April 1, when interest and fees start to build.

The early payment discount steps down from four percent in November to three, two and one percent in the following months, ending in February. Highlands taxes are paid in arrears, covering the calendar year from January through December. At a closing that means the seller owes a share of a year whose bill the buyer will receive.

  • Installment plan: apply by April 30 for the next tax year. Payments fall in June (6% discount), September (4.5%), December (3%) and March (final, no discount).
  • Missed first payment: an account with no first installment by July 31 is dropped from the plan and receives a full bill in October.
  • Homestead deferral: file by January 31 to use the deferral program.

Property tax calendar

Dates run from the January 1 valuation to the April 1 delinquency, and a few of them catch sellers off guard.

Highlands County property tax calendar
MonthWhat happens
January 31Homestead tax deferral filing deadline
March 1New homestead exemption and agricultural classification applications due
April 1Unpaid taxes become delinquent
April 30Installment plan applications due
On or before June 1Tax certificate sale
AugustTRIM notices mailed
October 31Bills mailed

During May, delinquent real estate accounts are advertised three times in a local newspaper. Delinquent tangible personal property accounts are advertised once.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead and agricultural classification

File a new homestead exemption with the Highlands County Property Appraiser by March 1. It costs nothing for a qualified owner and can be completed in minutes, either at the office or at visits the appraiser makes to municipal sites around the county.

New owners sometimes get mail offering to cut their taxable value for a fee. The appraiser's office points out that those offers sell the same savings the homestead exemption already provides, and that the paid service is generally just instructions on how to apply.

Agricultural land follows a separate path. The application goes to the appraiser before March 1 of the tax year, and only land used in good faith for commercial agriculture qualifies. After approval the classification renews yearly. A house on the parcel does not disqualify the land, but the home site is assessed at just value. Citrus is valued by variety, and the office adjusts assessments after disease or freeze damage cuts production. It stays out of groves because of disease concerns.

Challenging a value or exemption

Petition the Value Adjustment Board before the deadline printed on your TRIM notice. The petition must be notarized and carries a $50 filing fee for each parcel. The board consists of three county commissioners and two school board members, and it usually appoints special masters, independent of the appraiser's office, to hear the cases.

  • On a value dispute, bring sales of comparable properties from the prior year, before January 1, or an appraisal.
  • On a denied exemption, show that you qualified as of January 1.
  • The board cannot lower a bill because of hardship or because the value rose from last year.
  • A petitioner who loses may sue in circuit court under section 194.171.

The board's clerk mails the written decision within 20 days of the ruling. Millage comes from the county, the cities, the school board and the water management districts, so neither the board nor the appraiser can change a rate. A household that cannot absorb an increase may qualify for a deferral or the installment plan through the tax collector.

What happens if Highlands County property tax goes unpaid?

Once the newspaper notices have run, an unpaid account goes into a tax certificate sale held by June 1. The certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years from delinquency, and no later than seven years after the certificate was first issued.

Interest on the applicant's side runs at 1.5 percent a month, starting the month after the application and continuing until the account is redeemed or sold. The applicant is not guaranteed the property. The Highlands County Clerk of Courts schedules and runs the sale. State rules send a homestead certificate under $250 to the county instead of auction, and the opening bid at a homestead deed sale includes half of the last assessed value.

A seller with a certificate on the parcel can still close. Paying it off from proceeds redeems the lien before any deed application is filed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling a Highlands County property

Order a payoff figure before you list, and find out whether this year's bill has been issued. Bills go to the owner of record, and the recorded deed is what puts the new owner on the appraiser's roll.

The appraiser's database leaves out special assessments such as solid waste collection and fire or road improvement districts, yet those charges appear on the tax bill. Only the tax collector can give you the complete bill with non-ad valorem charges included. If you are splitting a lot or merging parcels, a survey is needed, all taxes on the parcels must be paid, and a mortgage holder must approve in writing.

The state deed stamp tax is 70 cents for each $100 paid. A change of ownership returns a capped assessment to just value on the next January 1. For a current millage figure, read your TRIM notice or ask the appraiser.

Some routine steps save time. Bring the parcel number and a copy of your deed when you contact the offices. Ask the title company to confirm that every earlier tax year is paid. If you are enrolled in the installment plan, list the payments you have made so the closing agent can divide the year correctly. When back taxes would hold up a buyer who depends on a mortgage, a cash purchase has no lender underwriting to wait for, and the title company can settle the balance from your proceeds.

Frequently asked questions

When is Highlands County property tax due?

The full bill is owed by March 31, and April 1 marks delinquency. Bills are mailed October 31, and the discount begins at 4 percent in November and drops a point each month to 1 percent in February.

How do I join the Highlands County installment plan?

Send an application to the tax collector by April 30 for the coming tax year. Payments fall in June, September, December and March, with discounts of 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three and none on the last.

What is the filing deadline for a Highlands County homestead exemption?

March 1, with the Highlands County Property Appraiser. Filing is free for qualified owners, and the office advises ignoring paid mailers that offer to reduce taxable value for a fee.

Can I petition the Value Adjustment Board in Highlands County?

Yes, before the deadline on your TRIM notice. The petition is notarized and costs $50 per parcel, and hardship or a rise in value from last year is not enough on its own to win a reduction.

Who runs the Highlands County tax deed sale?

The Clerk of Courts schedules and conducts it. A certificate holder applies through the tax collector's vendor once two years have run from the date of delinquency, and the holder is not guaranteed to get the property.

Who does what on a Columbia County bill

The appraiser supplies values and exemptions. Local taxing bodies adopt budgets and millage, and the tax collector, based in Lake City, mails bills and takes payment.

The tax collector's main line is 386-758-1077, and the Tax Department answers at 386-758-1080. For value or exemption questions, dial the appraiser at (386) 758-1083. The Clerk of Court, at 386-719-7580 for tax deed questions, runs the deed sales that follow long delinquency.

Due dates and discounts

The regular annual bill is due by March 31, and unpaid taxes generally turn delinquent April 1. The bill arrives in November, and the early-payment discount opens at 4% that month and falls a point each month through February.

The notice that arrives in August is a TRIM notice. It is a proposal, not the payment bill, so use it to check values, exemptions and hearing dates. When a due date lands on a weekend or holiday, Florida law gives qualifying payments next-working-day treatment, though a close call deserves a phone call.

The collector's year-at-a-glance calendar is a planning guide, and late-mailed bills, weekends and holidays can move a deadline, so follow the dates on your own notice.

  • April 1: unpaid taxes generally become delinquent, and tangible personal property returns are due to the appraiser.
  • April 30: installment applications are due.
  • May: delinquent-tax advertising and certificate sale preparation begin.
  • June 30 and September 30: the first two installments fall due.
  • November: annual collection starts at the 4% discount.

Ways to pay

You can pay online, by phone, at the counter, through the mail, or at the Lake City drive-through and drop box. The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum and a $1.50 e-check fee for online or phone payments, and receives no part of the card fee.

  • Search by owner name, address or account number in the property tax portal.
  • If a mortgage escrow pays your tax, confirm the lender paid the right year, to avoid a duplicate payment.
  • E-billing is available, registered one property account at a time.
  • A duplicate notice can go to a second recipient, but the owner remains responsible.

Quarterly installments

The plan lets an owner prepay the current year in four payments if estimated tax is over $100 per notice. Submit Form DR-534 to the tax collector by April 30. The first payment confirms participation.

Columbia County installment schedule
Due dateDiscount
June 306%
September 304.5%
December 313%
March 31None

The first two installments use prior-year tax as the estimate, and later ones adjust to actual tax. A late first installment is accepted through July 31 without the June discount. The plan doesn't cover delinquent taxes.

Partial payments

On current taxes, an owner can sign a partial-payment agreement with the office and pay in pieces from November 1 through March 31. No early-payment discounts apply, and the full balance must be paid by March 31.

Tracking is your job, because the local plan mails no balance reminder before April 1. Any unpaid balance becomes delinquent with interest and costs, and partial payments do not stop a certificate sale if real estate tax remains unpaid. State law leaves partial payments to the tax collector's discretion before delinquency.

Homestead and relief programs

The Property Appraiser decides homestead, disability, widow or widower, military service, senior and agricultural benefits. March 1 is the usual filing deadline. The homestead exemption reaches $50,000, and its first $25,000 also lowers school tax.

Save Our Homes ties a homestead's yearly assessment growth to 3 percent or the CPI change, whichever is lower, and the next January 1 after a sale brings the parcel back to just value. A disabled ex-servicemember may take a $5,000 cut in assessed value. A former servicemember aged 65 or over with a lasting service-connected disability may receive a discount matching the VA disability rating. A deferral request for homestead tax is filed with the collector by March 31 after the assessment year.

The tax collector's page also mentions income-based help and certain vacancy reductions for service assessments. Call to confirm which one fits.

Unpaid tax at a house closing

Closing agents usually pay the current year out of the seller's proceeds, and the collector can confirm what posted. Ask for an exact payoff for your closing date, since interest and costs change the amount.

A tax certificate is a lien and doesn't transfer ownership. Under section 197.502 a certificate holder can seek a tax deed two years after April 1 of the issue year, and the clerk's office holds the sale. Redemption is available until a tax deed is issued, unless the buyer has paid the clerk in full, so call the Tax Department at 386-758-1080 with your parcel number before any sale date. The office accepts cash, money order, cashier's check or card for certificate redemption and cautions against assuming a personal check works.

Other items on the bill

Besides value-based tax, the bill can carry non-ad valorem assessments for services such as fire, solid waste, paving or lighting, depending on the parcel's location. The county, city or district that creates an assessment sets it, and the tax collector only bills what the tax roll certifies.

Business equipment is a different account. Returns generally reach the appraiser by April 1, and unpaid accounts can lead to tax warrants rather than a certificate sale. Anyone selling a house that hosted a business should ask both offices whether an equipment account is open under the same name.

Mailing addresses are another trap. The tax roll address comes from the Property Appraiser, so a new owner who wants the November bill sent elsewhere should ask that office to update the record. The collector also takes a forwarding request.

If your value looks wrong

Contact the Property Appraiser first, then use the Value Adjustment Board if needed. A value petition reaches the clerk within 25 days of the Notice of Proposed Property Taxes, and an exemption denial can be appealed in the 30 days after a denial letter goes out.

Payment questions and value disputes go to separate offices, and a petition does not replace paying the bill the tax collector sends in November.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps for sellers

Pull your latest bill and note whether you are on an installment plan. Ask the Tax Department for a payoff through your expected closing date, and give a copy to the title agent. Check that your mortgage lender, if it pays from escrow, has paid the right year. After closing, send the collector a forwarding address and keep the paid receipt with your settlement papers. A cash sale skips lender underwriting, but the tax payoff and the lien release work the same way.

Frequently asked questions

What date makes Columbia County tax delinquent?

The ordinary annual bill must be paid by March 31, and April 1 usually starts delinquency. Discounts run from 4% in November to 1% in February.

How do I join the Columbia County installment plan?

File Form DR-534 with the collector by April 30. Estimated tax must top $100 per notice, and your first payment confirms participation.

What card fee does the Columbia County tax collector charge?

The office lists a 2.5% card fee with a $2 minimum, plus a $1.50 e-check fee, for online or phone payments.

Which number covers a Columbia County homestead exemption?

Call the Property Appraiser at (386) 758-1083. March 1 is the usual filing deadline.

Who runs tax deed sales in Columbia County?

The Clerk of Court conducts them and issues deeds to winning bidders. Tax deed questions go to 386-719-7580.

Who sends the Jackson County tax bill

In Jackson County the Tax Collector produces your bill, and the office's online portal lets you look up a parcel by tax year. What the property is worth is the Property Appraiser's call. Tax rates are voted on by the County Commission, the School Board and the other districts that levy against you.

The collector's calendar runs month by month through the year. Vehicle and license deadlines share it with property tax, so the table below picks out only the property rows. Compare them with your contract date to see which deadline comes next.

The county runs on Central Time. If you pay online at the end of a month, check the local clock first.

What are the Jackson County property tax months?

Collection opens in November and ends at the gross amount on March 31, with the discount shrinking in between.

Property tax months for Jackson County
MonthWhat to expect
NovemberCollection opens; 4% discount if paid by November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax delinquent on April 1; 3% penalty

Business equipment, which is tangible personal property, follows the same discount months. A homeowner can usually ignore that row, but a landlord or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

Delinquent accounts

A 3% penalty lands on real property tax that is still owed on April 1. Within 45 days the delinquent list is printed in a local paper at the owner's cost, then repeated weekly for three weeks in May ahead of the certificate sale. March is when the sale date gets chosen, which lets a seller find out early.

Buying a certificate gives an investor a lien, not the house. When two years pass with no redemption, the investor can ask for a deed and the clerk runs an auction. Where the parcel is a homestead, statute 197.502 adds half of the latest assessed value to the opening bid, in addition to the amount owed.

Equipment taxes run on a different clock: 1.5% interest a month, advertising within 45 days, and tax warrant work from May 1.

Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?

Yes. There is a four payment plan against the coming year's tax, and applications are due April 30. Owners already enrolled continue without applying again.

  • First payment: due on or before June 1, with cancellation if nothing arrives by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.
  • Third payment: by December 31.
  • Final payment: by March 31.

Two dates apply to the first payment, so phone the office to learn which governs your account. Selling mid-plan? Give the closing agent your paid installment list so the split is calculated correctly.

Homestead and assessment limits

Homestead here follows the statewide pattern: occupy the home on January 1, submit DR-501 by March 1, and as much as $50,000 is taken from assessed value. School tax drops only on the first $25,000.

Yearly increases in a homestead's assessed value cannot exceed the smaller of 3 percent or inflation; for 2026 the state chart shows 2.7 percent. Parcels without homestead are limited to a 10 percent increase. Both limits end when the property sells, which is why the buyer's first bill is frequently bigger than the seller's last.

  • Seniors: owners 65 or older with limited income may get an extra exemption if a county or city ordinance provides one.
  • Veteran disability: a disability connected to service, rated 10 percent or more, can earn a $5,000 cut in assessed value.
  • Leasing the house or leaving it removes homestead status.

Check with the Property Appraiser about any local ordinance covering your address.

Contesting a Jackson County value

August brings the TRIM notices, and you have 25 days after that to file a Value Adjustment Board petition. If an exemption is denied, the clock is 30 days from the date of the denial letter.

Start with a conversation at the appraiser's office. Staff can sometimes correct wrong square footage or a wrong exemption status with no hearing at all, and a deed, survey or builder's records back you up when the property record itself is mistaken.

Do mobile homes and business equipment follow the same dates?

Partly. Business furniture and equipment, called tangible personal property, use the same discount schedule as real estate, though a late account pays 1.5% interest each month.

Mobile homes are handled separately. If one is not assessed as real property, its decal must be renewed by December 31, and registrations for mobile homes, trucks over 8,000 pounds and truck-trailers share that December window. Selling land with a mobile home on it? Ask the collector whether the home is billed as real property or carries a decal, because the answer sets your deadline.

Tell the closing agent early whether a mobile home or business equipment goes with the property, so each related account is located and paid before settlement.

Selling with taxes owed

A tax balance will not block a sale. It is a lien on the parcel, and the title company handles it as one more payoff. The usual order of events is below.

  1. Request the amount due for every open year from the Tax Collector, noting how long the quote holds.
  2. Pass that figure to the title agent for the settlement statement.
  3. The title agent pays the Tax Collector out of your proceeds at the table, and the lien is released.
  4. File the paid receipt with your closing papers in case an old year surfaces later.

When a certificate has already been sold on the parcel, the payoff must cover what the investor is owed, so ask the office for a redemption figure before choosing a closing date. Buyers paying cash can often close faster here, since nothing waits on a loan approval.

What a seller should line up before closing

Obtain the payoff in writing and note which tax year it covers. At the table, the title agent splits the current year between the two sides.

  • Use the portal's tax-year search to check whether earlier years remain open.
  • If April 1 has already come and gone, ask about the penalty and advertising costs.
  • Search the Clerk's records for recorded liens.
  • Hand the closing agent your installment history.

Put the parcel number, a copy of your deed and your latest bill in one folder, because each office asks for them. Have balances quoted with a date, since totals change during the year. A seller up against a delinquency or certificate sale date can arrange a fast cash closing, with the tax paid from proceeds by the title agent. Without a lender appraisal or underwriting in the way, the schedule depends mostly on the title work.

Frequently asked questions

What is the final day to pay Jackson County property tax without a penalty?

The gross amount is accepted through March 31. Early payment earns 4% in November, then 3%, 2% and 1% over the next three months.

What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?

Real property gets a 3% penalty, while business equipment is charged 1.5% interest per month.

When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?

The collector sets the date in March, before April 1 delinquency begins. Call the collector for the exact day.

Does Jackson County allow installment payments?

Yes. Apply by April 30 for the following year, then pay in June, September, December and March. The office can confirm the June date.

Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?

Usually. A sale ends the Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit, and the following January 1 resets the property to just value.

Who bills Hendry County property tax

The tax collector bills and collects. The property appraiser handles value and exemptions. The county, the school board and the cities levy the tax and choose the rates. The collector's office will help you work out whom to call about what. Its main office is at 25 E. Hickpochee in LaBelle.

  • Tax collector: 863-675-5280, mail to P.O. Box 1780, LaBelle, FL 33975-1780. Payments do not require an appointment, so you can walk in with your bill or parcel number.
  • Property appraiser: 863-675-5270, the contact for homestead filings, assessed value questions, mailing address changes and parcel description errors.
  • Clerk of court: records the deed at closing and handles tax deed sales.

What gets taxed

The collector's page separates three kinds of charge. Real estate tax falls on land, buildings and improvements, rises and falls with the appraiser's value, and attaches to a parcel number. Tangible personal property tax applies to furniture and equipment in businesses and rental properties.

The third is non-ad valorem assessments: set amounts that taxing authorities collect for things like storm water, street lighting, fire and rescue, and solid waste. They do not depend on what your house is worth. Landlords should ask the property appraiser whether a rental they are selling has a personal property account. Read every section of a Hendry bill before listing, since a title company will want the flat assessments settled too.

Due dates and delinquency

Hendry's tax year is the calendar year, and the bill shows up in November. Paying is the owner's duty even when no notice arrives, so call the collector if November passes with no bill.

Taxes turn delinquent April 1. Real estate then carries 3 percent minimum interest plus ad costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1. Delinquent payments must be in certified U.S. funds drawn on a U.S. bank, and the amount due depends on the date payment is received.

Earlier in the year come the state deadlines: March 1 for exemptions, April 1 for business property returns, a TRIM notice in August, and 25 days after that notice to petition the value adjustment board.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Late tax on rental and business equipment

Equipment tax runs on a harsher clock than the house. Unpaid tangible personal property takes 18 percent interest a year plus advertising and fees, and warrants are expected on or about June 1.

A landlord selling a rental should call the property appraiser at 863-675-5270 and ask whether the address has an equipment account. Settle any balance before closing, and keep proof of payment, since it is a separate bill from the real estate tax and the buyer's title company can find it.

Because the total depends on the day payment is received, a quote given weeks before closing may be stale. Ask for a fresh figure in the last days before you sign, and have the closing agent confirm the amount that was wired.

The installment plan

Hendry's collector offers quarterly prepayment under s. 197.222 on accounts above $100 in tax. Sign-up opens each November 1 and closes April 30 of the year you want to join.

Hendry County quarterly plan, four payments
InstallmentAmount basisDueDiscount
1stOne quarter of prior year's taxesJune 306%
2ndOne quarter of prior year's taxesSeptember 304.5%
3rdCurrent liability less 1st and 2nd, divided by 2December 313%
4thRemaining current liabilityMarch 31None

The first installment must be in by July 31 or the account drops out and the full tax is due by March 31, though the 6 percent discount ends after June 30. The first notice is mailed by June 1. If June 15 passes without one, call the office. Enrolled owners are re-enrolled automatically in later years. The plan usually yields a discount close to the 4 percent November rate, though that can shift with exemptions and values. A change in ownership, value or exemption shows up in the last two bills, so a house sold mid-year needs a payoff check before closing.

Partial payments and deferral

Call the tax collector about partial payments, installment payments and homestead tax deferral plans. A partial payment plan agreement is posted on the office's website, and under s. 197.374 the collector decides whether to accept partial payments before delinquency.

  • Homestead deferral uses Form DR-570, filed by March 31 following the assessment year.
  • It postpones the share of tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 and up.
  • Several checks for one bill must travel in one envelope, and the bill is payable in a lump unless an installment or partial plan applies.

Anyone may pay the bill, which is handy when you are traveling or tied up with a move. A buyer, relative or closing agent can pay on your behalf. The collector's portal takes online payments. Put your account and phone numbers on a mailed check's memo line, and make sure the words and numerals agree.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead and the sale

An owner who claimed homestead enjoyed a cap on assessed value growth, and that cushion does not travel to the buyer. The state's cap chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024, and the next owner starts at just value on January 1 after the sale. If you plan to buy again in Florida, ask the appraiser there about portability, which moves part of the saved amount to a new homestead set up within three years.

The exemption itself is filed with the Hendry County Property Appraiser by March 1. The property appraiser's number is 863-675-5270.

Selling with taxes owed

Ask the tax collector for a payoff, then pass it to the closing agent. The flat assessments, the tax and any April 1 charges come out of proceeds, using the figure quoted for the day payment arrives.

If a certificate was sold on your parcel, redemption has to be in certified funds, and the holder must wait before seeking a deed. A financed buyer might take longer than a cash buyer, which counts when time is short.

It also helps to be realistic about order of events. The payoff request comes first, because every other number depends on it. Next you confirm whether any equipment account or flat assessment is open. Last, you decide whether to pay ahead of closing or let the title agent pay from proceeds. Whichever you choose, get the confirmation in writing so a question months later has a clear answer.

Before the closing date, gather your deed, ID and latest bill, and ask the title agent for a draft settlement statement. Compare each tax line with the collector's figure and ask about anything that differs. After closing, keep the receipt or payoff letter with your records for the year of sale.

Frequently asked questions

Who do I call about Hendry County property taxes?

Bills and payments go to 863-675-5280 (tax collector). Value and exemption questions go to 863-675-5270 (property appraiser).

What is the installment deadline in Hendry County?

Sign-up ends April 30, and the 6 percent discount needs the first payment by June 30. Payment after June 30 and before July 31 receives no discount.

When do Hendry County taxes go delinquent?

April 1. Real estate then adds a 3 percent minimum interest charge and advertising costs, and a certificate sale follows by June 1.

What if I do not get a tax bill in November?

The tax is still yours to pay. Call 863-675-5280 or search your account online.

Can someone else pay my Hendry County taxes?

Yes. Anyone may pay. Options include online, mail to P.O. Box 1780 in LaBelle, or an office visit.

Suwannee County parcels: what sellers will see

Suwannee County became Florida's 37th county on December 21, 1858, cut from the western part of Columbia County. Live Oak grew up where the Pensacola and Georgia Railroad passed a large live oak tree and pond, and sawmills later shaped the west side.

What that means for a seller is a mix of in-town lots, river and spring frontage, old farm tracts and mobile home sites. Legal descriptions and parcel numbers deserve a second look before any contract.

Who does what on a property tax bill

One office sets worth, another sends the bill, and elected boards pick the rates. The county commission, school board, city councils and water management district choose the tax rate, not the appraiser.

  • Property Appraiser: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, phone 386-362-1385, weekdays from half past eight to five, closed on listed holidays including Good Friday and the Thursday and Friday of Thanksgiving.
  • Tax Collector: Live Oak office at 386-362-2816.
  • Planning and Zoning, which also handles flood plain questions: 224 Pine Ave. S.W., phone 386-364-3401.

Working values can change daily until July 1, so a figure you see in spring is not final.

Filing dates for exemptions and classifications

March 1 is the big one for exemptions and special classifications, and April 1 is for business personal property. The collector adds a March 31 cutoff for indigent relief and for adjusting non-ad valorem assessments.

  • March 1: homestead, $5,000 disabled veteran, widow and widower exemptions, DR-501DV, DR-501M, agricultural classification (DR-482), conservation classification (DR-482C) and the conservation exemption (DR-418C).
  • June 1: financial information for the low-income senior exemption (DR-501SC).
  • April 1: tangible personal property return (DR-405).

Agricultural classification does not transfer. A new application is needed when land changes hands, and farm zoning alone does not earn the classification. The land must be in bona fide agricultural use on or before January 1.

Unpaid bills and penalties

Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty on April 1, and certificates are sold on unpaid accounts on or before June 1, which adds charges for the owner. Business personal property accrues interest instead and may face a tax warrant.

The collector sets a firm rule on payment type: after April 30 only certified funds are accepted, and personal checks mailed or left in the drop box are returned. The office adds a 2.35 percent charge to card payments and does not run cards over the phone. A mailed payment is judged by postmark before April 1 and by date of receipt after.

A certificate holder may seek a deed two years after the April 1 of issuance. Anyone holding a recorded contract for deed gets notice ahead of a tax deed sale, and homestead land carries a larger opening bid. Request a written payoff covering all open years before you list.

Installment plan and tax deferral

The quarterly plan needs an estimated bill above $100 and an application at the collector's office before May 1. It stays in force each year without a new form once the first payment is made on time.

Quarterly installment schedule
InstallmentDue byDiscount
First quarterJune 306%
Second quarterSeptember 304.5%
Third quarterDecember 313%
Fourth quarterMarch 31None

Payments after June 30 and through July 31 are taken without a discount, and a missed first payment drops the parcel from the plan. Deferral is a separate tool for homesteads: the owner postpones the part above 5 percent of household income, or above 3 percent at 65 or older, and all of it under $10,000 of income ($12,000 at 70 or older). The mortgage may not exceed 70 percent of assessed value, total liens plus deferred tax may not exceed 85 percent, and applications are due January 31 after bills go out. The deferred tax becomes a lien.

Exemptions that end with a sale

All of them. Homestead requires that the home be in your name and your permanent residence on January 1. The list includes a $25,000 exemption plus $5,000 each for a disabled veteran, a widow, a widower, a disabled person and a blind person.

First-time applicants should bring a deed or contract, Florida driver's license and vehicle tag details and Social Security numbers. An owner 65 or older with a combat-related permanent disability may get a discount equal to the VA percentage. A person with a total and permanent service-connected disability may qualify for a full homestead exemption, which can carry to a surviving spouse married five years.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth in assessed value to 3 percent or the inflation rate, whichever is less, but after a sale the parcel is reassessed at full just value when the new year begins. If you plan another Florida purchase, ask about portability on Form DR-501T.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Building and zoning rules that affect a sale

Check building history first. The 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code and the 2023 National Electrical Code apply to permit applications from January 1, 2026. The Building Department's phone is (386) 364-3407.

Mobile homes get special attention. Permits issued after May 1, 2022 require the pad to be inspected before the home is installed, and failure can mean the home is removed. Permits are not issued until all subcontractors have signed the addendum, and the driveway permit fee has been $50 since October 11, 2021.

The appraiser's site offers a property record search, a GIS map, subdivision plat maps and a form to report homestead fraud, all useful for checking a legal description before a contract. Call Planning and Zoning with the parcel ID to learn whether the lot is in a flood plain zone. The appraiser's office can supply the parcel number.

What to expect at the closing table

Your title or closing agent prorates this year's tax by the closing date, and earlier unpaid years are paid from your proceeds. If you sell, hand the bill to the new owner or bring it back to the tax collector's counter.

If the sale is a quick cash purchase of an inherited, vacant or behind-on-tax house, the same steps apply: the purchaser accepts the property in its present condition and a tax balance is settled out of the price. Compare an offer with what listing would net after commissions, repairs and carrying months, and confirm that the parcel number and legal description on the deed match the appraiser's file.

The Suwannee clerk files the deed, and the state deed tax is paid at filing. Afterward, ask the appraiser to update ownership and drop your exemption, and keep the signed closing statement for your records.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Suwannee County Property Appraiser's address?

The office is at 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak, FL 32064, phone 386-362-1385, open Monday through Friday between half past eight and five, apart from holidays.

Does Suwannee County let me pay property tax in installments?

Yes, if your estimated bill exceeds $100 and you apply before May 1. Four quarterly payments are due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

Can I defer Suwannee County property tax?

Yes, for a homesteaded home when the tax is high against low income. Applications are due January 31 after bills are mailed, and the deferred amount becomes a lien.

Is agricultural classification transferable to a buyer in Suwannee County?

No. A new application is required after a sale, due March 1, and the land must be in bona fide agricultural use by January 1.

What happens if I miss the April 1 deadline in Suwannee County?

Real estate takes a 3 percent penalty, and after April 30 only certified funds are accepted. Unpaid accounts can be sold as certificates on or before June 1.

Jefferson County in brief

Jefferson County is a rural Big Bend county of about 14,000 people, with Monticello as the county seat, 25 miles east of Tallahassee. Farms, ranches and timberland cover most of it. A town lot in Monticello, a farm parcel in the north and a coastal tract do not sit in the same taxing districts, so two Jefferson County bills rarely look alike.

Who sends and who reads a Jefferson County tax bill

Three independent offices share the work. The county's website points residents to jeffersonpa.net for parcel search and exemption filing.

  • Property Appraiser: sets the assessed value and takes exemption applications.
  • Tax Collector: mails statements on or before November 1, accepts payment and runs the certificate sale.
  • Clerk and Comptroller: keeps official records and conducts a tax deed auction if one is requested.

Every August the appraiser mails a TRIM notice showing the parcel's value and the rates each taxing body proposes. The hearings listed on it take place before rates are set in September.

2026 millage lines

Six lines appear on the Tax Collector's millage list. A house inside Monticello sees all six, while a rural parcel skips the city line. One mill is one-tenth of a cent, or a dollar per thousand of taxable value.

2026 Jefferson County millage lines

Jefferson County.007367307.3673

School, discretionary.002248002.2480

The commissioners, the school board, the city council and the two water districts each vote on their own rate. Charges for services appear apart from these lines, so ask the collector which ones apply at your address.

What does the calendar look like from November to June?

Statements must be mailed by November 1. An early payer saves 4 percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. After that the clock runs toward April.

  • April 1: unpaid real estate tax is delinquent and takes a 3 percent penalty.
  • Early May: unpaid accounts are advertised in the local paper.
  • By June 1: the online certificate sale.

Tangible personal property, such as business equipment, draws a 1.5 percent monthly penalty once it is late. A year's lien attaches at the start of that year.

Homestead and other exemptions

Homestead can cut $50,000 from the taxable figure. The first $25,000 applies to every levy, and the second $25,000 spares school levies. Send Form DR-501 to the appraiser before the March 1 cutoff for a house that was your permanent home on January 1. Renting the house or moving out ends the exemption.

An income-tested senior add-on worth as much as $50,000 exists only where the local government chose to adopt it. Disabled veteran and deployed servicemember benefits are also listed by the state. Ask the Jefferson County Property Appraiser which local options are in force. Annual growth in a homestead's assessed value is capped, and that cushion ends at a sale.

Does land use affect a Jefferson County sale?

It can. Building in the county is a two-step process: a Development Permit from the Planning Department first, then building permits from the Building Department. No building permit is issued for a site without the first. Land Development Regulations reach every kind of development, including driveways and power poles.

Any subdivision of land needs approval under the Land Development Code, and that approval should be confirmed before new deeds are recorded. If land is conveyed without it, later owners may be unable to get a building permit. A seller splitting off acreage should settle this before a buyer's attorney raises it.

  • Older and historic structures raise their own questions at sale time, such as roof age, wiring and flood zone. FEMA's Flood Map Service Center, which the county links, shows the zone for a given parcel.
  • The county holds a Community Rating System score of 8 under the federal flood insurance program, which earns premium discounts.

Handling the tax balance as a seller

The seller carries the tax up to the closing date, and older unpaid years must be cleared for clean title. The closing agent normally requests a payoff from the collector and pays it at the table from the seller's side.

The roll is a working roll and amounts can change during the year, so any quote is only a snapshot. Get the payoff in writing with a date near closing. If an escrowing lender holds your money, ask how soon any leftover balance returns.

  • Search the parcel on the collector's site and note every year with a balance.
  • Ask whether a certificate was sold, since redemption takes certified funds.
  • Confirm exemptions with the appraiser so the title company prorates correctly.
  • The clerk records the deed and takes the stamp tax at the counter.

Bring your parcel number and a copy of your deed when you contact an office. A buyer paying cash has no lender appraisal or underwriting to wait for, so a back-tax payoff can be taken from your proceeds without delaying the closing.

Before you list a Jefferson County property

A little groundwork keeps a sale on schedule. Start by pulling your parcel record and your latest tax statement, and check that the owner name and legal description match your deed. Next, ask the Tax Collector whether any earlier year still shows a balance. Then talk to the Property Appraiser about whether your exemptions will end at closing and how that affects the split between you and the buyer.

If you plan to sell part of a larger tract, settle the subdivision question with the Planning Department first. Rural parcels with wells, septic systems or old outbuildings may also draw questions from a buyer's inspector, so gather permits and receipts you already have. A sale to a cash buyer skips the mortgage appraisal step, which can help when a parcel is unusual or has paperwork gaps, though the title company still needs a clean record.

What happens to unpaid Jefferson County tax?

The debt is sold to an investor as a certificate. The collector describes it as a lien created by paying the delinquent tax, not a purchase of the property. The sale is a reverse auction on interest that starts at 18 percent, and the lowest bidder wins.

Certificates last seven years, and the face amount includes the 3 percent penalty, a 5 percent collector's commission and advertising costs. A homestead whose face value is under $250 is issued to the county at 18 percent instead of being sold. If the 22 month period runs out, the parcel can go to a tax deed sale, which the clerk runs after the holder applies once two years have gone by. The opening bid on a homestead includes half the latest assessed value. A March 31 deferral application date may help an owner at risk.

Frequently asked questions

When does unpaid Jefferson County real estate tax turn delinquent?

April 1, when a 3 percent penalty lands. The local paper runs unpaid accounts in early May, and the online certificate sale follows by June 1.

What discount do I get for paying a Jefferson County bill early?

Four percent in November, 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. Statements are mailed on or before November 1.

Is the Monticello millage line on every Jefferson County bill?

No. The 2026 list has a separate Monticello line of .00685010, which applies to parcels inside the city only.

Can I build on Jefferson County land without a permit?

No. The county requires a Development Permit from Planning first, then building permits, and subdivisions need approval before new deeds are recorded.

Where do I file for homestead in Jefferson County?

At the appraiser's office or on jeffersonpa.net, using Form DR-501, before March 1.

Hamilton County in brief

Hamilton County is rural, with farmland, small towns and an estimated 14,799 residents. Jasper is the county seat, and the municipalities of Jennings and White Springs also levy tax. The county sits at the crossroads of I-75 and I-10, so buyers can come from Jacksonville, Gainesville or Tallahassee, and your bill depends on whether the parcel is inside a town.

The county has a moratorium on single-site RV and camper living, and no electric permits are issued for RVs. If the property you plan to sell has an RV hookup, ask the county before you list.

Offices that handle the bill

Each of three offices owns one step. The appraiser sets value and exemptions, the collector bills and collects, and the clerk runs the value adjustment board and tax deed sales.

  • Property appraiser: values every parcel, keeps the exemption rolls, and handles name, address and legal description changes. Call or visit the office in Jasper before March 1 to file for homestead.
  • Tax collector: online at hamiltontaxcollector.com, with a parcel search and online payment.
  • Clerk and value adjustment board: 207 NE 1st Street, Room 106, Jasper, phone 386-792-1288.
  • County commission: sets the county millage rate and handles questions such as the RV rule above.

Phone before you drive in, since county offices keep their own hours. Bring your parcel number or a copy of your last bill, which lets staff find your account quickly and answer questions about what is owed.

Millage lines

The collector lists rates in decimal form. Compare them with your TRIM notice and November bill.

Hamilton County millage lines by taxing unit

Only one town line applies to a parcel. A rural parcel carries the county, school and water lines, while a house in Jasper adds the Jasper line. Non-ad valorem assessments are separate flat charges for services such as fire or solid waste, and they print on the same bill.

Millage is one dollar per thousand dollars of taxable value, so each line shows how much one body adds. Appraisal is the value, assessment is the tax owed, and the tax lien dates from January 1 of the tax year, which is why a bill can follow a house across a sale.

Billing and late dates

Statements are mailed by November 1. Payers get 4 percent off in November, then 3, 2 and 1 percent in the following three months. March is full price, and on April 1 the bill goes late. Real estate tax then takes a 3 percent penalty and the parcel is listed in the local paper from May on. Unpaid business property accrues 1.5 percent monthly.

Liens on unpaid real estate are sold online at the end of May or on June 1. Earlier in the year come the January 1 valuation date, the March 1 exemption cutoff and the August TRIM notice. A value petition is due 25 days after the TRIM notice.

Appealing an assessment

You petition the value adjustment board through the clerk. The board decides only whether property is appraised at fair market value and whether an agricultural classification or exemption should be approved. It cannot lower a value because you cannot afford the tax, and it has no say over rates.

  • The filing fee is $15, and $5 more for each extra parcel when contiguous parcels are combined on one petition.
  • If the property appraiser or tax collector denied a timely homestead exemption or homestead tax deferral, there is no fee.
  • Petitions need an original signature, and copies or faxes are not accepted.
  • A late petition is sent to the board attorney, and a hearing is set only for good cause.

Talk to the property appraiser before filing; the clerk encourages it. The form is DR-486, and a postmark by the deadline does not save a petition that arrives late.

Homestead and relief programs

Homestead is the main one. File by March 1; it applies only to your permanent residence, so a rental or second home does not qualify. The first layer of the exemption is limited to $25,000, and a second layer can reach up to $25,000 more, school taxes excluded.

Owners with limited income can seek a deferral under Form DR-570, with the application due at the tax collector by March 31. When you sell, the cap that protected your old assessed value disappears, which is why the buyer's bill is often higher than yours. If you are moving to another Florida home, ask the property appraiser there about carrying part of the cap forward.

If a property goes to a tax deed sale

Once a certificate holder files an application, the clerk conducts the auction. Every property sells buyer beware and as is, with no promises on title, zoning, access or physical condition. The high bidder's nonrefundable cost deposit is set by s. 197.542(2).

A holder may apply two years after April 1 of the issue year, and homestead land opens at the taxes due plus half its latest assessed value. Paying the collector before the sale takes the parcel off the block. If your house has an advertised date, plan the sale of the home around it.

Getting ready to list

A little work up front keeps the sale smooth. Look up your parcel on the collector's site and note the amount due and the year it covers. Make sure the mailing address on file is current, because a bill sent to an old address still carries the same dates. Check that your name and legal description match your deed.

If you rent the property or run a business there, ask the appraiser whether a separate personal property account exists. Then decide whether you would rather pay the bill now or have it paid from the proceeds at closing. Either works, and the title agent will show it on the settlement statement. Keep a copy of the paid receipt or payoff letter with your closing papers in case a question comes up later.

Selling with unpaid taxes

Tell the closing agent about each unpaid year at the start. The agent gets a payoff from the collector and pays it from the sale proceeds, so you do not need cash in hand. Plan the timing around April 1, because the 3 percent penalty and the newspaper charge raise the payoff.

Ask for a draft settlement statement before the closing date and check that every tax line matches the collector's figure. Bring photo ID, your deed and your latest bill to the title agent, and confirm where your proceeds will be sent. Buyers who pay cash can often meet a tight schedule, a useful option when a certificate or sale date is near.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

When does a Hamilton County bill go late?

On April 1. The collector adds a 3 percent penalty to real estate tax on that date and lists the parcel in the paper beginning in May.

How much is the Hamilton County early payment discount?

It starts at 4 percent for November and falls one point each month through February.

What does it cost to petition the Hamilton County value board?

$15, plus $5 for each added contiguous parcel. Petitions over a denied homestead or homestead deferral request have no fee.

Can a house with a tax certificate be sold in Hamilton County?

Yes. Closing pays the collector, the lien clears, and the buyer gets clean title. Ask for a payoff figure that includes interest.

Who decides the rate on my Hamilton County bill?

The taxing bodies decide, such as the county, school board, towns and the river district. The appraiser only sets value and handles exemptions.

Franklin County, FL Property Tax Guide: Offices, Dates and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Florida

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Franklin County, FL Property Tax Guide sale

Owe Franklin County Property Tax? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Franklin County houses as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Behind on Franklin County property tax?
We buy Franklin County houses as-is, and the title company pays unpaid tax from the proceeds.
Get My Cash Offer →

Three offices behind a Franklin County bill

Franklin County sits in the northwestern Panhandle and has more than 11,000 residents. Outside the cities of Apalachicola and Carrabelle, the county commission serves as the local government. Those two cities, the commission and the school board set the rates.

The tax work is split three ways: the appraiser puts a value on the parcel, the tax collector sends the bill, and the clerk of court handles any tax deed auction. Know which desk to call and you save time.

  • Property appraiser: keeps the roll, takes exemption filings and mails TRIM notices in August. It neither sets rates nor collects tax.
  • Tax collector: 33 Market Street, Suite 202, Apalachicola; (850) 653-9323. Prints bills, accepts payment, sells certificates.
  • Clerk: holds the courthouse auction of tax deeds and records your deed when you sell.

Tax calendar

Exemption paperwork comes early in the year and the bill comes last.

Franklin County property tax steps
WhenStepOffice
January 1 to March 1Window for homestead and agricultural classification filingsProperty appraiser
April 1Business personal property returns dueProperty appraiser
AugustTRIM notice, marked as a notice and not a billProperty appraiser
By November 1Statements mailedTax collector
November through FebruaryDiscount slides from 4% to 1%Tax collector
April 1 of the next yearReal estate bill late; 3% penaltyTax collector
On or before June 1Online lien auction for unpaid parcelsTax collector

The TRIM notice is not a bill, even though it comes in the mail. Wait for the November statement before you pay.

Millage lines

The tax collector posts a millage table, written as decimals. A millage figure is the tax per thousand dollars of taxable value. The lines below are the 2025 figures, so ask the collector for the table covering the current year before relying on them.

  • County: .00504590
  • School, local effort: .00194400
  • School, discretionary: .00224800
  • Northwest Florida Water Management: .00002070
  • Carrabelle: .00750000
  • Apalachicola: .00834570
  • Dog Island: .00400000
  • Eastpoint district: .00375000
  • Alligator Point: .00123040

Only one local line fits a given address. Carrabelle and Apalachicola are the two cities, while Eastpoint, Dog Island and Alligator Point appear as districts. County, school and water lines stack on top. Flat assessments for services print on the same statement, so read the lower part of the bill too.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead and other reductions

Florida's homestead exemption takes up to $50,000 off the value of a home you live in permanently. The appraiser accepts applications from January 1 through March 1. Once you start renting the house out, eligibility is gone.

Once a homestead is in place, a statutory cap limits how fast its assessed value can rise. A sale wipes out that cushion for the next owner, so your buyer's first Franklin County bill may look much larger than yours did. If you plan to move to another Florida home, ask the appraiser there whether part of your cap can carry over.

Gather what the appraiser will want before you visit: a photo ID, proof that you live in the home, and a copy of your deed. A quick call to the office beforehand can spare you a second trip.

Paying in pieces

State law lets you prepay in quarterly installments under s. 197.222 if you apply to the tax collector by May 1 of the assessment year. Low-income homestead owners can also defer part of the tax with Form DR-570 by March 31. Whether either one helps depends on your income and timing, so call the collector at (850) 653-9323 before the dates pass. Lenders that escrow normally pay the bill themselves. Selling mid-plan? Say so to the closing agent, so any installment still owing is paid at the table instead of falling to the buyer.

After April 1 on an unpaid parcel

Real estate bills pick up a 3 percent penalty as April begins. Come May, the parcel appears in the newspaper for three weeks running, and the owner pays for the ad. Business equipment and mobile home attachments follow a rougher path of monthly interest and warrants.

Around the end of May the collector auctions a lien certificate online. Bidders start at 18 percent and bid the rate down, and the lowest rate wins. The winner pays your tax and holds a lien, and you owe them the bid rate. A buyer cannot take your house at that point. A deed application is allowed two years after April 1 of the issue year, and a certificate left unredeemed for 22 months can end in a deed sale.

Homestead parcels owing under $250 are not offered to the public. The county holds those at 18 percent a year until the total passes $250.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How a tax deed sale works

The clerk's office runs the sale. When sales are scheduled, they are generally held on the first Monday of the month at 11:00 AM inside the main courthouse at 33 Market Street, Apalachicola. Call the clerk to verify before attending. Notice runs in the Apalachicola Times once a week for four weeks.

  • You can redeem by paying the tax collector before the sale, or before the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
  • For homestead property, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value to the taxes, interest and fees.
  • The winning bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater, and pays the balance within 24 hours.
  • Documentary stamps of $.70 per $100 of the bid and recording fees are due from the bidder.
  • Some government liens survive the deed, and every property is sold as is.

Most title insurers want a quiet title lawsuit before they will insure a tax deed property, and the deed gives the buyer a right to immediate possession even though legal action may still be needed to get it. For an owner the lesson is simple: a sale you close before the auction date avoids all of that, and your own buyer gets a normal title search.

Selling with taxes owed

An unpaid balance is a lien that the buyer's title company will insist on clearing. The closing agent can send the payoff to the tax collector from your proceeds. Ask for a figure good through the closing day, since a bill past April 1 grows by a 3 percent penalty and newspaper advertising.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Documentary stamps run 70 cents on each $100 of consideration outside Miami-Dade, and every party to the document is liable. The clerk takes the payment at recording.

Bring your ID, your deed and your latest tax bill to the title agent, and read the draft settlement statement before you sign. A cash buyer can often close faster, which helps if a sale date or the April 1 penalty is near.

Frequently asked questions

Which month is the cheapest to pay in Franklin County?

November. The tax collector prints a 4 percent discount for November, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February.

Does the appraiser or the collector set my rate?

Neither. The appraiser does not set rates, and the rates come from the county commission, school board and each city or district.

Is a house with a tax certificate on it still sellable?

Yes. Closing pays the redemption to the tax collector, which then repays the certificate holder. Ask (850) 653-9323 for the redemption total.

When is the Franklin County exemption filing cutoff?

March 1. Filing opens January 1, and the home must be your permanent residence.

How fast can a tax deed auction happen?

Slowly. A certificate holder waits two years after April 1 of the issue year to apply, and you can redeem up to the point the clerk receives the winning bidder's full payment.
